title: Salman Khan announces December 4 release date for his much-delayed movie 'Maatrubhumi'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Mumbai, Superstar Salman Khan on Friday opened up that his much-delayed war drama movie "Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace" will finally make its debut in theatres across the country on December 4.

Adding to this, Salman Khan announces December 4 rollout date for his much-delayed movie 'Maatrubhumi' Salman, who headlines the Apoorva Lakhia-directed movie, based on the 2020 Galwan Valley clash between Indian and Chinese troops, shared the rollout date at the movie's promotional event here.
Meanwhile, Asked about the delay in the movie's rollout, Salman shared the team wanted to ensure that the visual effects were up to the mark.

Notably, "Today, there are a lot of VFX experts out there who examine each and every shot of a movie. So, with this movie, we don't want to give anyone an opportunity to zoom in on a scene and criticise its VFX. We want this movie to visually blow everyone's mind. It is a beautifully shot movie," the superstar told reporters.

As per the latest buzz, "We thought we would be able to complete the movie in 45-50 days, but madam got injured, and it took her time to recover. We were earlier supposed to rollout the movie in either January or June, but it was then pushed to August. Now, we will rollout it on December 4," he added.

In further updates, The movie, which was earlier titled "Battle of Galwan" before being rechristened "Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace", is inspired by the military standoff in eastern Ladakh in May 2020.

On top of that, Clashes at the Galwan Valley in June that year resulted in a severe strain in ties between India and China. Twenty Indian Army personnel laid down their lives in the Galwan Valley clashes.
Salman essays the role of Bikkumalla Santosh Babu, who laid down his life along with 19 other soldiers of the 16 Bihar Regiment during the clash.

title: Delhi HC asks Doosra makers to add disclaimer, give ₹2 crore bank guarantee in Sourav Ganguly case
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

There is a new development in Sourav Ganguly's legal battle over the movie Doosra. As per PTI, the Delhi High Court has asked the movie's makers to add a disclaimer and give ₹ 2 crore rupees bank guarantee on Sourav’s plea over personality rights violations. The cricketer had accused the makers of commercially exploiting his identity, personality and iconic moments from his cricketing career without his permission.

Adding to this, Sourav Ganguly had accused makers of Doosra of commercially exploiting his identity. The dispute also involves movie production and distribution company Luv Films, which had acquired the rights to make an authorised biopic on Ganguly, titled Dada : The Sourav Ganguly Story, starring Rajkummar Rao.

Meanwhile, The row began ahead of the theatrical rollout of Doosra: India's Other Freedom Struggle on October 23. Ganguly and Luv Films LLP filed a lawsuit against the movie's makers, alleging that it used elements of the former cricketer's identity and career without authorisation. Luv Films also argued that the movie interfered with the rights granted to it under its agreement to make an authorised biographical movie on the cricketer.

Notably, The former cricketer's legal team particularly objected to the movie's portrayal of India's historic 2002 NatWest Series final against England at Lord's. Sourav's shirtless celebration on the Lord's balcony, after India defeated England to win the final, remains one of the most iconic moments of his cricketing career.

As per the latest buzz, According to cricketer's counsel, the second half of Doosra heavily focuses on the NatWest Series final and uses moments associated with the former cricketer to promote the movie.

In further updates, The makers have maintained that Doosra is not a biopic on Ganguly but a fictional story about a middle-class girl from Rajasthan who finds inspiration in the cricketer's achievements. Their legal team also argued that they had obtained the necessary permissions from the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) and the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) to use footage from the 2002 NatWest Series. They further contended that Ganguly's personality rights do not give him ownership of cricket match footage.

On top of that, In earlier hearings, the Delhi High Court declined Ganguly's request to stop the theatrical rollout of Doosra. However, it sought a response from the filmmakers and directed them to arrange a screening of the movie so that the court could examine the objections.

During the October 29 hearing, the court asked Ganguly to identify the specific portions of Doosra that allegedly infringed his personality rights, along with the reasons for his objections. The court also sought details of the disputed scenes, including their timestamps, to examine the allegations.

title: Unaccustomed Earth trailer: Freida Pinto, Siddharth explore lost love and second chances in show based on Jhumpa Lahiri's book
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

It is always special when a beloved book gets a new life on screen. This time, Jhumpa Lahiri's internationally acclaimed 2008 short story collection, Unaccustomed Earth, is being adapted into an eight-episode series. Starring Freida Pinto and Siddharth , the show brings together characters and stories from the original collection, weaving them into a continuous narrative.

Adding to this, Unaccustomed Earth stars Freida Pinto and Siddharth in lead roles. Unaccustomed Earth trailer The trailer introduces Freida Pinto as Parul Chaudhary, a married Indian-American woman and mother who begins to realise that she has been sleepwalking through life. After being diagnosed with cancer, she returns from Mumbai to her old life at Cambridge, US. The change brings her face-to-face with memories of her past, including an old love played by Siddharth, whom she had lost to an arranged marriage. As the two reconnect, old feelings resurface, setting off a series of events that complicate Parul's personal life and relationships.

Meanwhile, Speaking about the show, Freida shared it would immerse audiences in the traditions, food and culture of an Indian-American Bengali family. She explained how the series explores a community that has rarely been represented on television in such a detailed manner.

Notably, She shared, “It’s the kind of South Asian American community that we’ve never seen on television. We haven’t seen it before through this very holistic, culture-embracing way, while also dealing with the complexities of what it is to be this tight-knit community. Every character has something universal. From the perspective of Parul’s character is the question, ‘How far would you go to live the dream that you really want to live? And are you up for the consequences?’”

As per the latest buzz, The eight-episode family drama is created and written by Madhuri Shekar, known for her work on 3 Body Problem and The Nevers. Apart from Freida Pinto and Siddharth, the ensemble cast includes Sarayu Blue, Indraneil Sengupta, Adi Roy and Iyla Sundarsingh McKaig.

In further updates, Produced by John Wells Productions and Warner Bros., the series is executive produced by Shekar, John Wells, Ritesh Batra, Jhumpa Lahiri, Nisha Ganatra, Erica Saleh, Erin Jontow and Celia Costas. Batra, known for directing Irrfan Khan's critically acclaimed movie The Lunchbox, will also direct and executive produce the first two episodes.

On top of that, Before Unaccustomed Earth, another of Jhumpa Lahiri's celebrated literary works made it to the big screen. The Namesake (2006), directed by Mira Nair and starring Irrfan and Tabu, was widely acclaimed.
Unaccustomed Earth will premiere on Netflix on December 17.

title: Mahesh Bhatt says he was in tears watching son-in-law Ranbir Kapoor in Ramayana, feels actor ‘touched the God in him’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ramayana is receiving praise from all quarters, but for star Ranbir Kapoor , some of the most special appreciation has come from his family. Ranbir's father-in-law and filmmaker Mahesh Bhatt lauded the movie, particularly Ranbir's portrayal of Lord Rama. During a recent interaction, Mahesh recalled how he almost broke down while watching the scene in which Rama is sent into exile.

Adding to this, Mahesh Bhatt lauded Ranbir Kapoor's portrayal of Lord Rama in Ramayana. ‘I tried hard not to cry’ In conversation with Variety India, Mahesh shared, "Just before the interval, Rama was sent into exile for 14 years. I felt my throat close. I tried hard not to cry. I had gone [to watch the movie] with young filmmakers and writers, and people in the hall knew they were sitting with Ranbir Kapoor’s father-in-law. When the lights came on, I tried to hide my tears. I couldn’t. Nor could I say much. Great experiences make you silent."

Meanwhile, Mahesh also lauded the movie's director, Nitesh Tiwari, for his sensitive portrayal of Rama and Ravana. He lauded Yash's performance as Ravana and shared Ranbir's portrayal of Rama brought out a side of the star that his previous films had not explored. He shared, "Yash mesmerized me as Ravana. Nitesh Tiwari reins in all that power; it could so easily have become too much. I was still under its spell when Ranbir entered, and the movie did not immediately rise for me with his arrival. Then he walked towards the camera and folded his hands. I saw him touch something in himself that his other films had never asked him to. I felt he had touched the God in him. As the family gathered around Rama, the epic came close. Arun Govil was heartbreakingly total."

Notably, On Thursday, Alia Bhatt had shared pictures of their daughter Raha from the sets of Ramayana and penned a heartfelt note for Ranbir. Praising his dedication to the movie, she wrote, “You poured everything into this one and somehow still had all of it left for her. So proud of you Ranbir and of every single person who brought their heart and soul to this incredible experience at the movies. Some stories are bigger than all of us & Ramayana is one of them.”
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Alia Bhatt 💛 (@aliaabhatt)

In further updates, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is a two-part cinematic adaptation of the Indian epic. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman.

On top of that, The ensemble cast also includes Arun Govil, Lara Dutta, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, and Kajal Aggarwal. Sunny Deol is set to play Lord Hanuman in Part 2. Produced by Namit Malhotra, the ambitious project has a combined budget of ₹ 4,000 crore rupees for both instalments.

title: Gaiety-Galaxy made stars feel like SUPERSTARS; where are they now? Bollywood's RADIO SILENCE raises eyebrows as Manoj Desai pays FULL salaries despite ZERO revenue for 2 months
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Many expected the theatre to resume operations within a week or two. However, what has astonished movie lovers and industry members alike is that nearly two months have passed, and the issue remains unresolved.

Adding to this, Gaiety-Galaxy has always been synonymous with the quintessential big-screen experience, where audiences whistle, clap, cheer and hoot to their hearts' content, especially during mass entertainers. Two such films, Drishyam The Conclusion and Jailer 2 , were rolled out last month, but sadly, neither could be screened at the iconic complex. The of late rolled out Ramayana , too, missed out on a rollout at Gaiety-Galaxy. One can only imagine the frenzy that would have erupted in the auditoriums during the entry sequences of Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sunny Deol.

Meanwhile, An industry insider commented, “Manoj Desai (executive director of G7 and also Maratha Mandir) and his team are trying their best to get the issues sorted. But since it’s a government-related procedure, it's taking time and no one knows how much more time will be taken to get the issue sorted. Meanwhile, Manoj Desai is keeping the morale high of the employees. He is paying full salaries to his employees even though he has not collected a single paisa since September 7 from G7. The employees are grateful for getting their wages, especially in these festival times. But they miss the theatre and can’t wait to get back and serve the patrons.”
Notably, However, what has particularly astonished the industry insider, as well as several followers of Gaiety-Galaxy, is the complete lack of support from Bollywood celebrities.

As per the latest buzz, The insider thundered, “So many actors learned that they became stars when they saw the films getting an insane response in Gaiety-Galaxy. They have visited the theatre to check theatre reactions and to promote their films and themselves. They also proudly shared videos of followers hooting, whistling and dancing during the movie at Gaiety-Galaxy. And now, not a single one of them has posted anything about the theatre. Agreed that they’ll reason that the cinema complex is shut due to non-renewal of license and they fear being trolled over it. But at least they can write ‘Missing Gaiety-Galaxy’ or ‘hope the issues are resolved soon’. This may hopefully bring attention to the theatre and may speed up the process. Alas, there’s radio silence.”

In further updates, Meanwhile, as the closure approaches the two-month mark, the uncertainty continues for the management, employees and countless moviegoers who have made Gaiety-Galaxy an inseparable part of their movie-watching experience.

On top of that, Gaiety-Galaxy was established on November 24, 1972. Ramesh Sippy’s much-loved Seeta Aur Geeta (1972) was the inaugural movie. G7 multiplex originally started with just 3 theatres – Gaiety, Galaxy and Gemini. Gaiety and Galaxy are the biggest screens, consisting of a stall and balcony. While Gaiety is the bigger one, comprising nearly 1000 seats, Galaxy has around 800 seats. Gemini, with just one class, has around 240 seats.

In the late 90s, the management added 4 more theatres. Grace, the preview theatre, which is not open to the public, was constructed above the balcony of Gaiety. Gem, located next to Galaxy’s stall and Glamour, constructed between Galaxy’s stall and the balcony, and has just around 45 seats. And finally, there’s a 105-seater Gossip. This cinema hall also has a separate entrance at the back.

title: Ramayana box office collection day 2 (updated live): Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film sees drop after big opening day, crosses ₹80 crore
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana did not have the earth-shattering start at the ticket-window that its makers had hoped for. However, the movie still did great business, setting a new record for a pre-Diwali rollout in India. But the true test begins now, on its first Friday. The movie is likely to see a drop in collections on its second day before the Diwali weekend picks up the pace again. It remains to be seen whether positive word of mouth will offset that drop, and by how much.

Adding to this, Ramayana stars Yash as Ravana alongside Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama. Ramayana ticket-window update Ramayana began with houseful shows on day 1, netting ₹ 64.85 crore rupees net in India on its opening day. The figure was low given the movie’s scale, but it was still the fourth-highest opening in Bollywood history. On Friday, Ramayana began on a slower pace in the morning shows. By 4 PM on day 2, the movie had collected ₹ 19.23 crore rupees net in India, taking its two-day haul to over ₹ 84 crore rupees . The movie should aim to cross the ₹ 100-crore rupees barrier by the end of the day and hope for a strong weekend to bounce back and regain momentum.

Meanwhile, What is worrisome for the movie is that its earnings have come largely on the back of some good performance by the Hindi version. Despite Yash ’s presence as Ravana, the Kannada version has started extremely slowly. It collected just ₹ 7.50 crore rupees on day 1 and has lacked pace on day 2 as well. Of the other versions, Telugu has fared well, while Malayalam and Tamil are just filling the ranks. The makers would hope that positive critical reviews and audience reactions will lead to increased footfall in the days to come.

Notably, On its opening day, Ramayana beat the opening-day hauls of blockbusters such as Pathaan ( ₹ 57 crore rupees), Animal ( ₹ 63 crore rupees), and Drishyam 2 ( ₹ 62 crore rupees). However, it also missed out on Bollywood’s all-time day-one record, set by Ranveer Singh’s Dhurandhar 2 ( ₹ 102 crore rupees), and fell short of Adipurush as well ( ₹ 86.75 crore rupees). The trend continued on the second day. By the end of day 2, Adipurush had collected ₹ 151 crore rupees net in India. Ramayana is almost certain to miss the mark. However, it must be noted that Adipurush’s first two days in theatres were a Friday and a Saturday, while Ramayana’s first two days included a working Thursday and Friday.

As per the latest buzz, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. The first rolled out worldwide on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2028.

title: Karan Johar is trying to dissuade his twins Yash and Roohi from joining Bollywood, says he'd be ‘too old’ to protect them
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood filmmaker Karan Johar has introduced several actors who went on to become stars and delivered numerous blockbusters and memorable films. However, the filmmaker of late opened up that he is concerned about his children entering the industry and is almost trying to dissuade them from joining the business.

Adding to this, Karan Johar doesn't want his kids to join Bollywood. Karan Johar says he doesn't want his kids to enter Bollywood While discussing the challenges of raising children in the movie industry on season 9 of Koffee With Karan with Saif Ali Khan and Kareena Kapoor , Karan shared, "Well, look, as I shared, it’s not an easy place. It’s tough. I am almost dissuading my children from the business. And everybody says, ‘Why are you doing that? Why are you doing that?’ I am like, look, I will be too old to protect them at that time."

Meanwhile, Kareena then offered a different perspective on parents being protective of their children. “But I feel maybe the protection is also what is causing the issue. I think sometimes we just have to, like, probably just… you know, we’re all so protective towards our children, I feel sometimes our parents used to say just let us go and say, ‘Karni hai toh karo, you know, karo. You have to go and ‘ragdo (If you want to do it, then do it. You have to go and really push yourself).’" Karan agreed with her before the conversation moved on.

Notably, Kareena had earlier opened up that her son, Taimur, is not particularly interested in drama or acting and is more inclined towards sports. The star also shared that Taimur often asks her whether she is friends with Virat Kohli, Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi.

As per the latest buzz, Karan is a father to twins, Yash and Roohi Johar. The filmmaker welcomed them through surrogacy in February 2017, becoming a single father at the age of 44. While his son is named after his late father, filmmaker Yash Johar, his daughter's name, Roohi, is an anagram of his mother's name, Hiroo. Now nine years old, Yash and Roohi often feature in Karan's social media posts. The filmmaker has frequently spoken about how fatherhood has changed his life and how raising his children is one of his greatest joys.

In further updates, Karan is currently awaiting the rollout of Dharma's web series, Student of the Year: After Dark. His college romance franchise has been reimagined as a dark murder mystery. Shanaya Kapoor plays twins Aayesha and Aditi. After Aayesha is found dead, Aditi enters the cut-throat contest at St Teresa Heritage School to uncover her killer. Directed by Reema Maya and produced by Dharmatic Entertainment, the series also stars Divik Sharma and Manya Grover. It is scheduled to premiere on JioHotstar on November 13, 2026.

On top of that, Riya Sharma is a content producer at Hindustan Times who lives and breathes entertainment. Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Rakul Singh (@rakulpreet)

title: Ranveer Singh’s Pralay shoot sparks BIG controversy at Mumbai’s Azad Maidan; Under-14 and Under-16 cricket matches POSTPONED; MCA FUMES over disruption
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

As per a report in Mumbai Mirror, the Government of Maharashtra’s Sports Department granted the makers of Pralay permission to shoot in Azad Maidan for six hours. This angered the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) as it disrupted the schedule of Under-14 and Under-16 interschool cricket matches. The report further claimed that due to Pralay ’s shoot, the MCA was compelled to postpone the matches even though it was planned in advance.

Adding to this, The Mumbai Mirror report also opened up that this is the first time a movie shoot has been permitted at Azad Maidan. The MCA has now expressed its displeasure over the decision by writing a letter to the Deputy Director of Sports.

Meanwhile, MCA Apex Council member Nadim Memon spoke to the tabloid and shared, “This is the first time a movie shoot has taken place at Azad Maidan. Large sets were erected and artificial grass was laid for the shoot of Pralay . This is not a movie-shooting venue but a cricket ground where players hone their skills to progress to the international level. Our ongoing tournaments were disrupted because of the shoot. Who will take responsibility for this loss? You cannot commercially exploit a cricket ground by allowing a commercial movie shoot.”

Notably, Nadim added, “Azad Maidan’s sporting culture is being affected by the Sports Department. Instead of supporting sports, it is allowing commercial bookings at the ground...We are working to nurture young cricketers and organise several interstate tournaments. But because of the movie shoot, we had to postpone matches. How can the Sports Department allow this?”

As per the latest buzz, According to Mumbai Mirror, the Maharashtra government granted permission to Light Rays, the Mumbai-based production house backing Pralay , to use 5,000 square yards of government land at Azad Maidan for the shoot. The makers were charged a rental fee of Rs. 40,000 for six hours, at the rate of Rs. 800 per 100 square yards. Additionally, they were required to deposit Rs. 40,000 as refundable security.

In further updates, However, the approval came with several restrictions. The production team was prohibited from bringing vehicles onto the cricket pitches, cooking, digging or carrying out any activity that could damage the ground. The makers were also required to secure necessary permissions from the police, traffic department and BMC, along with a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the MCA. They were further asked to submit an undertaking on a Rs. 100 stamp paper.

On top of that, The permission was signed by Sports Department Under Secretary Ashok Damayyawar on October 30 and subsequently forwarded by the Deputy Director of Sports and Youth Services, Mumbai, on November 2.

title: HC sets aside Jharkhand govt order cancelling exams amid protests against irregularities
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Jharkhand High Court on Friday set aside the state government’s order cancelling the Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examinations and the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) recruitment process, as students took to the streets against alleged irregularities in July and August.

Adding to this, Chief minister Hemant Soren promised to look into irregularities in all recruitment exams in the state since 2014. The court observed that there was no definitive or widespread evidence on record proving a complete paper leak compromised the selection of the entire pool of successful candidates. Over 1,900 selected candidates had cleared the exams.

Meanwhile, In August, the cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination and all other recruitment tests conducted by the private firm TSR Data Processing Private Limited met one of the main demands of students protesting alleged irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) examinations. Chief minister Hemant Soren also promised to look into irregularities in all recruitment exams in the state since 2014.
Notably, Students protested against alleged irregularities for 24 days. Some of them sat on a hunger strike for 16 days.

As per the latest buzz, A bench of Justice Deepak Roshan ruled in favour of the successful candidates, effectively restoring the JSSC-CGL selection process. It clarified that the ongoing Criminal Investigation Department (CID) probe into individual cases of exam malpractice and fraud will continue uninterrupted. The court shared final appointment of the recruits would be subject to the outcome of the finality of the ongoing probe.
In further updates, The state government issued a blanket notification cancelling the entire JSSC-CGL recruitment drive, citing interim CID findings and student protests.

On top of that, The petitioners, including Akash Gaurav, who cleared the exam, moved the high court. They argued that penalising all hard-working and deserving candidates for the misdeeds of a corrupt few was inherently unjust, especially since investigative agencies had identified suspect candidates.
The government presented a sealed cover report in the court citing massive system failures.

title: Sandeep Reddy Vanga praises Ramayana's magnitude, calls Namit Malhotra the most committed producer he has known
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ranbir Kapoor and Yash -starrer Ramayana opened in theatres to rave reviews on Thursday. The movie has been receiving praise from all quarters, including celebrities from different movie industries. After filmmaker SS Rajamouli lauded the movie, Animal director Sandeep Reddy Vanga took to social media to laud not just its cast but also producer Namit Malhotra for backing the epic and remaining committed to the project for years.

Adding to this, Sandeep Reddy Vanga lauded Namit Malhotra for his commitment to Ramayana. ‘Ranbir and Yash nailed it’ Taking to X, Sandeep lauded Ranbir and Yash's performances, saying that both actors had nailed their respective roles. He wrote, "Want to experience the magnitude of Ram and Raavana? Please go watch Ramayana. Ranbir and Yash — both nailed it bone-deep. 👌 Made their presence absolutely commanding 👏 I loved it. ❤️"

Meanwhile, Sandeep also tagged Namit Malhotra and reserved special praise for the producer's commitment to the project. He wrote, "I have never known a producer to be this committed 🙏 @malhotra_namit."

Notably, Ramayana is being made as a two-part project with a combined budget of ₹ 4,000 crore rupees. While speaking at the movie's trailer launch in Bengaluru in October, Yash, who has co-produced the movie, spoke about the movie's budget and clarified that the amount covers both films, including post-production and promotional expenses.

As per the latest buzz, “I know that Namit's statement went widely shared on social media. In India, there is a problem. People don't like it when you talk confidently. That's what happened with Namit's statement. But in the West, it's the total opposite. If you tell them we have made a good movie in a humble manner, they will dismiss our movie as a small project. That's exactly why Namit has confidently shared that this movie is mounted on ₹ 4,000 crore rupees. We need to prove the strength of the Indian movie industry to the global market,” Yash shared.

In further updates, He added, “Ramayana is a two-part project, and the budget for both the movies combined is definitely ₹ 4,000 crore rupees. The budget includes post-production and promotional expenses as well.”

On top of that, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. title: Ramayana vs Adipurush: Why Ranbir Kapoor, Yash's combined star power failed to beat Prabhas' much-maligned adaptation at the box office
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

A good benchmark for an Indian movie, in terms of wide rollout, is 10,000 screens globally. Most tentpole Indian films - the RRRs and Jawans of the industry - secure 6000-7000 screens in India and 3000+ overseas. That is what a wide international rollout means. That is why Ramayana was considered historic. Sony Pictures gave it 50,000 screens outside India, 15 times what an Indian movie normally gets. Even in India, the movie managed 8000-9000 screens, higher than any movie in the multiplex era. On top of that, it had positive reactions and reviews in its favour.

Adding to this, Ramayana was unable to match Adipurush's day 1 ticket-window earnings. Yet, it fell short of that expected historic start. In fact, it fell short of even Adipurush , the much-derided and maligned adaptation of the epic from three years ago. How did that happen? The answer lies in a combination of misfired marketing for Ramayana and the tsunami that is Telugu fandom in the case of Adipurush.

Meanwhile, When it hit the screens in June 2023, Adipurush was the most expensive Indian movie ever made. Mounted on a budget of ₹ 550 crore rupees, it starred Prabhas as Lord Rama, Kriti Sanon as Sita, and Saif Ali Khan as Ravana. It secured around 6500 screens in India on rollout day and 3000 screens overseas. This was one of the widest releases for an Indian movie, bigger than Baahubali 2 and almost at par with RRR and Pathaan.

Notably, In comparison, Ramayana Part 1 has been mounted on a ₹ 1600-crore rupees budget, the highest in Indian cinema history. It boasts of two big stars - Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama and Yash as Ravana. Courtesy this, it secured 9000 screens across India. Its distribution deal with Sony Pictures gave it access to 50,000 screens overseas. This is almost 5x the scale of any Indian movie rollout in the last 30 years.

As per the latest buzz, Ramayana opened to ₹ 64.85 crore rupees net collection in India, largely on the back of a ₹ 47-crore rupees day for its Hindi version. It sold around 25 lakh tickets across the country and was propped up in terms of collections by premium formats such as IMAX. Three years ago, Adipurush opened to ₹ 86.75 crore rupees net on its opening day. The movie had collected ₹ 37 crore rupees net in Hindi and a staggering ₹ 48 crore rupees net in Telugu. Its total ticket sales on day 1 were 55 lakh, much higher than Ramayana's. The chief reason for this was Prabhas’ popularity. The star’s fandom led to a record-breaking opening for the movie in the Telugu states and parts of North India, despite negative reviews. This meant that Ramayana could not surpass these numbers despite a much higher average ticket price and a wider rollout.

In further updates, With 50,000 screens overseas, Ramayana was aiming for a global-level rollout, the kind major Hollywood blockbusters get worldwide. Yet, its day 1 collections do not reflect that ambition. The movie opened with an international gross of around $5.3 million, lower than Dhurandhar 2's earlier this year. And that movie was banned in the Gulf. Adipurush, on the other hand, collected $3 million on its first day overseas, but in just 6% of the screen count. This shows that the wide rollout was unable to generate the desired buzz for Ramayana. Its earnings numbers remained at a level comparable to those of any big Indian movie.

On top of that, If Ramayana has any hope of recouping its costs, the overseas business needs to pick up via word of mouth over the remainder of the weekend. The domestic business may see a boost during and after Diwali given the highly positive first reactions. In the long run, Ramayana will certainly surpass what Adipurush achieved, possibly in its opening weekend, but its day 1 collections betray its ambitions.

Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is directed by Nitesh Tiwari. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. A sequel is scheduled for rollout in 2028.

title: Farah Khan says younger batch of actors are insecure, lack confidence; calls Shah Rukh Khan, Salman Khan, Akshay Kumar the last of the superstars
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker and choreographer Farah Khan believes the era of superstars is over. In a chat with Neha Dhupia and Angad Bedi on their show Double Date, Farah called out new actors for interfering in different aspects of filmmaking, from choreography and music to casting. She shared their lack of trust in directors stems from insecurity and a lack of confidence in themselves.

Adding to this, Farah Khan says today's actors are insecure, not confident about themselves. Farah Khan takes a dig at today's actors Talking about the mindset of today's actors, Farah shared, "The problem is today's actors don't have confidence in anyone. They don't have confidence in the director. They want to choreograph the song on their own, interfere in music and casting as well. All of this comes when you are not confident about yourself."

Meanwhile, She added that actors who are confident in themselves would trust the process. She then cited examples of superstars, saying, "Shah Rukh has never interfered in casting when I shared I want Sushmita Sen for Main Hoon Na even though she wasn't any big heroine. He didn't question. I shared I want new girl in Om Shanti Om, he didn't question. He just saw the photo (of Deepika Padukone) and shared, 'if you are fine with it, I'm fine.'"

Notably, Farah further pointed out that actors today are insecure and lack confidence in themselves. She added that they want to shoot magazine covers and attend award functions but do not have good films to their credit.

As per the latest buzz, Farah shared that self-belief and hard work are essential to becoming a superstar. She cited Shah Rukh Khan, Amitabh Bachchan, Akshay Kumar and Salman Khan as examples, saying they still work as hard as they did on their first films, with a few working even harder. She pointed out that Salman never asks for days off or refuses to shoot on a Sunday.

In further updates, Farah also called out actors for arriving on set and asking for changes, saying, "That is not your job. You do your job. Learn your lines first. Your job is to know your lines when you come on set. That you are not able to do. It's irritating. I have seen it. I have done actors' first movie, and then after their fifth movie, they think they know it all. They are surrounded by people. The era of superstars is over. They (Salman, SRK, Amitabh, Akshay) are the last of them; enjoy them for as long as they work."

On top of that, Farah Khan has shared that she plans to begin working on her next directorial project towards the end of 2026, once her children leave for college. In one of her vlogs, she shared she would direct the movie only if Shah Rukh Khan stars in it; otherwise, she would rather wait.

title: Ramayana worldwide box office collection day 1: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film opens at ₹127 crore, unable to beat Adipurush despite wider release
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

It had everything going for it - the biggest budget in Indian cinema history, the widest rollout, a Hollywood studio’s backing, and full-scale promotions in the West. Yet, Nitesh Tiwari and Namit Malhotra’s Ramayana came up short at the ticket-window. The movie had a strong start at the domestic ticket-window, but its global box-office numbers did not justify the scale on which the movie was mounted. Ramayana still minted over ₹ 100 crore rupees worldwide on its opening day, but failed to enter the top 15 biggest openings for Indian films, lagging behind even Adipurush .

Adding to this, Ramayana rolled out worldwide on November 5, ahead of Diwali. Ramayana worldwide ticket-window opening The Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer opened to great reviews on Thursday, with initial audience reactions largely positive. Yet that did not drive footfall momentum very strongly. The movie collected ₹ 64.85 crore rupees net ( ₹ 77.50 crore rupees gross) in India on its opening day. Perhaps the most disappointing aspect of this collection was that the Kannada version netted only ₹ 7.50 crore rupees, one-third of what Yash ’s last two films - KGF Chapter 2 and Toxic - managed on their first days. This means word of mouth now needs to drive the movie’s growth over its extended four-day Diwali weekend.

Meanwhile, The bigger trouble for Ramayana has been its overseas earnings. Sony Pictures distributed the movie internationally, giving it a rollout on 70,000 screens worldwide, almost three times as many as any Indian rollout so far. Yet Ramayana’s day-one overseas haul has been under $5.5 million. Of this, $1.5 million has come from the paid previews in North America. These numbers would be considered impressive for any other Indian movie, but Ramayana’s scale and ambition do not justify a sub-$10 million opening. Ramayana’s total worldwide gross on day one stands at ₹ 127.50 crore rupees.

Notably, Given that Ramayana is the most expensive Indian movie ever made, it should have aimed for the biggest opening for any Indian movie as well. Pushpa 2’s ₹ 274-crore rupees record always looked safe, though. But Ramayana not even breaking the Bollywood record of Dhurandhar 2 ( ₹ 202 crore rupees) should be concerning. In the end, its ₹ 127.50-crore rupees start is only the 16th best in Indian cinema history, behind Jawan ( ₹ 129 crore rupees) and even Adipurush ( ₹ 128 crore rupees).

As per the latest buzz, Ramayana's inability to beat Adipurush has been surprising, given that the latter, starring Prabhas, was a much-derided and criticised adaptation of the Ramayana. Yet its day one was bigger than the Ramayana in both gross earnings and footfalls.

In further updates, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. title: Ravana's throne in Ramayana was made out of 24K gold, cost ₹1 crore; Surpanakha's chariot cost ₹1.5 crore, reveals art director
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana is the most expensive Indian movie ever made, with a reported budget of ₹ 1600 crore rupees for Part One. Much of the budget has been spent on creating the extraordinary visuals through VFX and CGI. But a large part of it also went into the grand production design. In a recent interview, the movie’s art director opened up that, contrary to popular belief, grand items like Ravana’s throne, the flying Pushpak Vimana, and even Surpanakha’s chariot were all real models, painstakingly built at great cost.

Adding to this, Yash plays Ravana in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana. Ramayana art director opens up on Ravana’s throne One of the most prominent sequences in Ramayana is when Ravana conquers Lanka and takes over the rule from Kuber. A scene shows the newly anointed king creating a throne of gold and sitting on it as he looks at his subjects. Ramesh Andhale, the art director of Ramayana, told Prabhat Khabar that the grand throne took the movie’s art design department four months to make. Ramesh added that at first, a clay model of the entire throne was created based on the designs, following which the team constructed the throne using fibre. But what added to its visual appeal was that real 24-karat molten gold was used in its decoration. According to Ramesh, gold leafing was applied to the throne, and the final product cost around ₹ 1 crore rupees.

Meanwhile, Ramesh added that similar painstaking attention to detail was done for almost all of the movie’s major objects and sets. He opened up about the gold-plated chariot that carried Surpanakha (played by Rakul Preet Singh). The chariot appears in only one scene when Surpanakha visits Lord Rama and Lakshman in the Panchavati forest. Yet, the production design team went all out in its making. Ramesh shared that the chariot took three months to complete, as the team had to make it functional while getting the balance right between functionality and aesthetics. It cost ₹ 1.5 crore rupees to make, according to him.

Notably, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. title: Jantar Mantar July protests: Supreme Court asks enquiry panel to submit reports in a month on police crackdown, alleged brutality
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Supreme Court on Thursday directed the high-powered enquiry committee (HPEC), examining complaints of police excesses and violence during the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) -led July protests at Jantar Mantar, to submit its fact-finding reports within a month, after the panel informed the court that its complaints portal became operational on October 14.

Adding to this, The Supreme Court allowed former Meghalaya DGP LR Bishnoi to resign from the five-member panel and asked it to indicate whether a replacement was required. (HT Photo) The five-member committee, formed in August under the chairmanship of former Supreme Court judge, justice (retd) R Subhash Reddy, informed the court in a confidential report that only a few complaints had been received on the portal, with no complainant appearing in person or approaching the committee through email.
Meanwhile, The bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and justice Joymalya Bagchi shared, “We would like the committee to start submitting its fact-finding reports.”

Notably, The court referred to its August 18 and September 10 orders, which had asked the committee to consider submitting reports on two priority issues: targeted violence, harassment and molestation of women protesters; and grievous harm and injuries allegedly caused to protesters by police and security personnel, including the need for interim compensation.
As per the latest buzz, Posting the matter for December 2, the bench shared, “The committee may submit an interim report on the priority issues identified by us.”

In further updates, The court asked the petitioners to encourage victims and complainants to file their representations with the committee. At the same time, it clarified that the panel need not wait indefinitely for complaints. “Whatever information and material is submitted by the parties, including material submitted by petitioners on behalf of the victims, will be examined and considered,” the bench shared.

On top of that, The court also shared that since complainants were not required to disclose victims’ identities, petitioners could share with the HPEC material already submitted before the court, including copies of petitions and video clips attached to them.

The committee’s confidential report was circulated only among the judges. Senior advocate Monika Gusain, assisting the court as amicus curiae, shared the reports were not being shared with her. Petitioners represented by senior advocates N Hariharan and Gopal Sankaranarayanan also shared they were unable to assist the court without knowing the contents of the HPEC reports.

title: Karan Johar reveals celebrities ask for post-edit clearance on Koffee With Karan, says no one wants a PR nightmare
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Nostalgia immediately hit followers when Karan Johar opened up that the current season of Koffee With Karan , Season 9, would be the last one, as he bids adieu to his much-loved talk show. The show, which started in 2004, has, in many ways, shaped Bollywood pop culture and offered audiences unprecedented access to their favourite celebrities.

Adding to this, Karan Johar had earlier declared that this will be the final season of Koffee With Karan. However, it has also courted its fair share of controversies over the years, often landing its guests in trouble. From the KL Rahul-Hardik Pandya row to Alia Bhatt's rapid-fire answer about India's President, several moments from the show have made headlines.

Meanwhile, In a recent interaction with Variety India, Karan shared that, over the years, celebrities have become increasingly conscious of what they say on the show to avoid controversies. He also observed that guests are now less open than they were in the earlier seasons. Karan pointed out that star entourages have grown considerably, with several more team members accompanying guests to the sets.

Notably, He shared, "I know the steam has become lesser, the brew is much milder. That's only because everyone's very worried. Because you saw what happens. Anyone comes on this show and says even something tiny and it blows up and it's a PR nightmare and no one wants that. When I started Koffee With Karan, and I used to look beyond the stage, there used to be nobody there, it was just an empty set. Now when I look, there are publicists, managers, image-management people, teams. The hair and makeup and entourage has also increased substantially.”

As per the latest buzz, Karan also opened up that celebrities now request post-edit clearances before an episode is aired. Acknowledging the high stakes of modern star culture and the possibility of statements triggering a PR crisis, the filmmaker shared he understands their concerns and does not mind accommodating such requests.

In further updates, He shared, “And I absolutely respect that because I would do the same if I was invited to ‘Koffee With Karan’ because I don't want to go through a PR nightmare. So while our coffee brew is milder, that's only because everyone's worried,” he laughs.

As per the latest buzz, "I salute, I applaud and I have the deepest respect for each and every team member of Ramayana…. All of us can dream it… they actually went out and achieved it!!!!", he shared.

He also lauded Tiwari for his craft and confidence in telling a simple story.

title: Aakhri Ride short film review: Chandan Roy shines in Vijesh Rajan and Yashoda Parthasarthy's fun satire disguised as horror
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

What is Aakhri Ride ? Is it a horror movie about a man’s tryst with a witch, or a satire on the difficulties gig workers face in Mumbai? Or is it simply a short that shows us a mirror, depicting what society has become and what it still is. It is all of the above and none of it. In 24 minutes, Aakhri Ride takes us on a wild ride with our protagonist, showing the good, bad, and ugly of our world without ever sermonising or preaching, and always entertaining.

Adding to this, Aakhri Ride stars Chandan Roy in the lead role. The premise Aakhri Ride is the story of Aman, a cab driver in Mumbai. We meet him on a particularly dire day. He needs ₹ 150,000 for his sister’s dowry. But there is no way he can get a loan. So he reconnects with a scammer friend who suggests he sell the cab he drives and run away. But before he can drop the car to a thief on the outskirts of Mumbai, he must finish one last ride. Sadly for him, the passenger seems to be a witch, complete with a black face, long talons for nails, and a shrieky voice.

Meanwhile, Aakhri Ride may address life's inequalities and cast a shadow over society’s preconceived notions and prejudices, but it never loses sight of the fact that it is, first and foremost, an entertaining story. The movie chooses comedy as the genre to do so. Even when it scares, Aakhri Ride chooses to do so in the most frivolous manner, making you laugh at what the protagonist is facing.

Notably, It can do so because Chandan Roy is just so earnest. As Aman, he brings simplicity, helplessness, and industriousness mixed with desperation. And he does all of it without becoming a bechara. He is just one of us, shackled by the conditions life has put on him, trying to make the best of it all. When his boss, the owner of the cab he drives, calls to berate him every now and then, every salaried employee who has been in a toxic workplace at some point becomes Aman too. That is how the movie reels you in.

As per the latest buzz, And then when the twist arrives, and the movie becomes an ‘anti-horror’, it never feels like a betrayal. Because Aakhri Ride does that honestly, logically, and without losing sight of the rules it has set for the story. It still remains tense, but again, with humour thrown in it, with a rather satisfying, if somewhat all-too-convenient conclusion.

In further updates, Aakhri Ride takes place in the space of a single night. That creates the urgency needed in the narrative. The shots, largely taken from inside the car, often through rearview mirrors, effortlessly take us into our protagonist's world. The accompanying music never gets overpowering, and the supporting acts remain just that: good but never overshadowing. It is a crisp story that delivers bite-sized entertainment in a novel manner, without resorting to sermonising. And that, alone, makes it worth a watch.
On top of that, Aakhri Ride is currently streaming on Oh Short Flips YouTube channel.

A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism. title: Regina Cassandra questions Karan Johar for ignoring her during Kesari 2 promotions, says Janhvi Kapoor, Radhika Apte comments fuel north-south divide
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Regina Cassandra has weighed in on Janhvi Kapoor's remarks about the objectification of her character in Peddi and Radhika Apte's comments about her experience working in Telugu cinema. Regina shared actors who feel uncomfortable with a movie's portrayal should walk away from the project if they have the choice. She also shared that such conversations can create a divide between the North and South Indian movie industries.

Adding to this, Regina Cassandra spoke about Peddi row. 'Please walk out of the movie if you are not comfortable' In an interview with India Today, Regina shared, "I feel like at the end of the day, if they feel uncomfortable, please walk out to the movie. I don’t think, we should be put in a place where we say we didn’t have a choice. This is not against a man or a woman. As a woman, it is very easy for me to take sides, I will obviously take the side of the woman, but I don’t think any of us today, especially the examples that you gave, I don’t think either of them are in a place where they can't walk out a movie, especially being who they are."

Meanwhile, Regina also spoke about her experience during the promotions of Kesari 2, in which she played the role of the movie's lead Akshay Kumar's wife. She claimed that Dharma Productions did not acknowledge or tag her while promoting the movie.

Notably, She shared, "I really have a big issue with when a north Indian star talks about south Indian cinema like that because you're making a north-south divide without you even realizing it and that's absolutely wrong. There are different ways of handling this. Also, Janhvi has spoken about being objectified on Karan Johar's show, the same Karan's Dharma Productions decided not to promote me in their movie Kesari 2. Now, what am I supposed to call that? Objectifying what? That I'm a South-Indian? Till date I do not even know why they didn't. It is very strange. They shared that Kesari 2's song on Instagram and I am featuring in that song from start to finish, but they didn't even tag me."

As per the latest buzz, Radhika Apte of late spoke about her experience working in South Indian cinema and recalled a Telugu movie in which she played a woman who was married to her maternal uncle. Without naming the movie, she told Zoom, "There was a Telugu movie I did where I had to marry my Mama (maternal uncle) in the movie. It was the most challenging movie. I hated everything about it."

In further updates, Janhvi starred opposite Ram Charan in Buchi Babu Sana's Peddi. Her portrayal became the subject of debate, with many criticising the camera angles and calling out makers objectification and sexualisation of her character.

On top of that, She spoke about it during her apperance on Koffee With Karan. She admitted that she could have been more vigilant while filming and acknowledged that the portrayal was problematic. She called the experience "violating" and shared, "I don’t like saying this because it sounds like I am shifting blame but it’s like you listen to the director and what he says. I was navigating how to make things less problematic as and when information was becoming available to me. In the south, very rarely there is a bound script. Very rarely do you see the camera angles. I should have taken advantage of my privilege. It was a violating experience in a way."

title: Lara Dutta humbled to be part of Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana, calls Kaikeyi one of the ‘most misunderstood’ women in history
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The biggest Indian movie has arrived in theatres today. Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana , starring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Yash as Ravana, and Sai Pallavi as Sita, rolled out worldwide on November 5, ahead of the Diwali. Star Lara Dutta , who plays Kaikeyi in the movie, has now penned a heartfelt note on being part of the journey from the start and how she got the chance to play ‘one of the most misunderstood women in history.’

Adding to this, Lara Dutta shared her experience on playing Kaikeyi in Ramayana. In Ramayana, Queen Kaikeyi demands two boons from King Dasharatha that directly affect Rama: Her son, Bharata, be installed as the rightful king and crown prince (Yuvaraja) of Ayodhya, and that Rama be banished to the Dandaka forest for 14 years.

Meanwhile, Taking to her Instagram account, Lara shared a few stills of her look as Kaikeyi from the movie and penned a long caption to speak about the privilege of being part of a historical journey with Ramayana. She began, "What began many years ago as a fervent wish… to be a part of something greater than oneself. Greater than the collective. Something that transcends time itself… something woven into the very fabric of our being.
Notably, And today, that wish finds its place in a story as timeless as eternity."

As per the latest buzz, She added, “What an extraordinary privilege to portray a mother who has perhaps been one of the most misunderstood women in history. To be entrusted with the responsibility of bringing alive her humanity… her angst, her vulnerabilities, her guilt and her remorse. A woman who changed the course of history. Or perhaps, one could say, set it upon the path it was always destined to take. I am humbled. I am deeply grateful.”
In further updates, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Lara Dutta Bhupathi (@larabhupathi)

On top of that, Speaking about the rollout, Lara shared, “Today, this divine story comes to you. And I hope, in my own small way, I will do justice to Mata Kaikeyi. That you will look beyond the perceptions of centuries and embrace her for the pivotal role she played in bringing a divine prophecy to fruition. Jai Shree Ram.”

The star thanked the makers and wrote, “My heartfelt gratitude to @iamnamitmalhotra and @niteshtiwari22 for entrusting me with this extraordinary opportunity. And to my incredible cast and crew… my deepest respect, love and gratitude. It is a privilege to walk this journey with you. I miss my father tremendously today and wish he was here with me to see this. Some stories are not merely told. They are lived, felt and carried within us. This is one such story.”

title: Peace will never go out of fashion: Agastya Nanda on ‘Ikkis’
body: Here's the latest fashion moment turning heads:
Mumbai, Star Agastya Nanda says his 2025 movie "Ikkis" may not have performed well commercially, but he takes pride in being part of a war movie that spoke about the importance of peace.

Adding to this, Peace will never go out of fashion: Agastya Nanda on ‘Ikkis’ Directed by Sriram Raghavan, the movie narrates the story of Arun Khetarpal , a second Lieutenant, who was martyred at the age of 21 during the Battle of Basantar in the 1971 Indo-Pak war.

Meanwhile, "'Ikkis' may not have done well commercially but I do not think any of us stand here like failures. We've a lot of pride for the movie we made and we will be forever grateful for preaching peace and love and peace will never go out of fashion," the star told PTI in an interview.
Notably, Nanda shared the outcome of a movie is not entirely in the hands of its actors and makers, whose primary goal is to give their best creatively and hope for the best.

As per the latest buzz, "The beauty is that a movie will find its path even if it's not a big budget movie, we've seen it very of late with 'Hanuman Ansh' and with the Hollywood movie 'Obsession'. So, destiny has its own way of playing its part.

In further updates, "The best you can do is make something you believe in and hope it finds the right audience. Money is something that is not in our hands at all. So, we do our bit and hope the rest is up to the audiences and all."
On top of that, Co-star Vivaan Shah shared they were overwhelmed with the strong critical reception that "Ikkis"garnered.

"It did very well critically. In fact, it has got the best reviews that I have ever seen. We are all subject to the laws of the marketplace, and that is very important. But also, the fact that it did so well critically should be appreciated. There are people who are still writing essays and articles about 'Ikkis'. So, it lives on in people's hearts," he shared.

title: Ramayana box office collection day 1 (updated live): Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film takes a huge start, mints ₹32 crore by afternoon to beat Dhurandhar
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

The biggest and grandest Indian movie has arrived in theatres in magnificent style. Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana rolled out worldwide on Thursday, November 5, ahead of the Diwali weekend in India. The ₹ 1600-crore rupees Part One is the most expensive Indian movie ever made. Advance bookings indicated a strong start, and positive reviews have ensured that. Ramayana has taken off at the ticket-window on its opening day.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana. Ramayana advance bookings set records Advance bookings for Ramayana opened on Dussehra, 15 days before rollout. After a disagreement between the exhibitors and distributors was sorted out last week, the pre-sales began in full flow. By the time of its rollout, Ramayana had already sold tickets worth ₹ 200 crore rupees worldwide. Of this, over ₹ 120 crore rupees was in India alone. The opening day accounted for ₹ 45 crore rupees in gross in India. All the signs pointed to a massive day one for Ramayana.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ramayana: Rise of a Legend (@ramayanamovie)

Notably, Ramayana is seeing houseful shows even on Thursday morning in many parts of India. While the advance bookings did not reach the monumental levels that Dhurandhar 2 had earlier this year, the movie is still on course for a record-breaking opening. By 4 PM on rollout day, Ramayana had collected ₹ 32.81 crore rupees net in India. This is largely on the back of some good performance by the Hindi version. Despite Yash ’s presence as Ravana, the Kannada version has started slowly, contributing only ₹ 3.91 crore rupees so far. Of the other versions, Telugu has fared well, while Malayalam and Tamil are just filling the ranks.
As per the latest buzz, But this meant that by the afternoon, Ramayana had surpassed Dhurandhar's full-day 1 collection. The Ranveer Singh movie opened at ₹ 28 crore rupees last year.

In further updates, Given its solid advance booking, Ramayana was certain to cross the ₹ 70 crore rupees net mark on opening day. This means the movie will cross the opening-day hauls of blockbusters such as Pathaan ( ₹ 57 crore rupees), Animal ( ₹ 63 crore rupees), and Drishyam 2 ( ₹ 62 crore rupees). It should also beat Shah Rukh Khan’s Jawan ( ₹ 75 crore rupees). But the real target for Ramayana will be the all-time day-one record, set by Ranveer Singh’s Dhurandhar 2, which minted ₹ 102 crore rupees on its opening day earlier this year.

On top of that, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The first rolled out worldwide on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2028.

title: Ramayana Part 1 post-credit scene sets the stage for Sunny Deol's Lord Hanuman's arrival; watch Hanuman Chalisa sung by Diljit Dosanjh
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ramayana Part 1, also titled Ramayana: Rise of a Legend , saves one of its biggest reveals for the very end. Rolled out in theatres on November 5, the movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. However, Sunny Deol 's appearance as Lord Hanuman is what gives the closing moments an added surprise. The star makes his appearance in a post-credit scene, offering a first glimpse of his character and setting up his role in the second installment. The brief appearance has already got followers talking, particularly those who have been eager to see Sunny step into the shoes of the much-loved mythological character.

Adding to this, Ramayana: Sunny Deol makes a powerful entry as Lord Hanuman, flies with gada in post-credit scene as Hanuman Chalisa plays. Sunny Deol appears as Lord Hanuman in post-credit scene Those who stay back until the end credits get a glimpse of Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. Rather than introducing the character earlier, the makers have saved his appearance for the final sequence, using it to set up what audiences can expect from the second part.

Meanwhile, The scene opens with a powerful musical backdrop, as Hanuman makes his entry. While his face remains hidden, a wider shot towards the end shows him flying through the air with his gada as he hails Jai Shri Ram. The Hanuman Chalisa, sung by Diljit Dosanjh, Sukhwinder Singh, Mohit Chauhan, Kailash Kher and Anirudh Ravichander, plays in the background, adding to the impact of the moment. The makers have revealed just enough to build curiosity around Sunny's portrayal without giving away his complete look. Before Hanuman's appearance, the movie also offers a glimpse of Raghav Juyal as Meghnada, Ravana's eldest son and the crown prince of Lanka.

Notably, Hanuman's arrival also marks a significant point in the Ramayana for the sequel which will arrive in 2028. He becomes one of the most important figures in Rama's journey after Ravana abducts Sita. From finding her in Lanka to helping Rama prepare for the war against Ravana, Hanuman plays a crucial role in the events that follow.

As per the latest buzz, At the end, the movie also confirms that the second installment will arrive in 2028, instead of the earlier planned 2027 rollout. In an interview with E! News, producer Namit Malhotra explained why the team has decided to take an additional year to complete the sequel. He shared, “So the idea was now that we've got so much excitement that the world has had, we want to take a little bit more time to make sure that when we present the grand finale, we have a little bit more time to do what we did on part one. That extra year is what I genuinely believe we need to do justice for a movie of this size. When you see part 2 coming in, that will be a whole other story. We didn't want to do a rush job or get ahead of ourselves. We want to deliver the finale in the most grand way that it deserves.”

In further updates, Ahead of its November 5 rollout, Ramayana received a 'U' certificate from the Central Board of Movie Certification (CBFC). An excerpt from Hindustan Times review read, “To sum it up, Raavan may have had ten heads, but the makers have a rather bigger challenge to deal with: the expectations of an entire country. Part 1 has managed to navigate that minefield, giving us a visually spectacular retelling while staying true to the emotional beats of the epic. The real fireworks are reserved for the next instalment. With Sunny Deol's arrival as Hanuman, the Sanjeevani buti scene and the much awaited war still to come, Part 2 has its work cut out. The good news? The makers seem to know what they are doing. The bad news for Raavan? Well, we all know how this ends.”

title: Amid Eetha Marathi accent controversy, Shraddha Kapoor says she doesn't ‘handle’ criticism, barely checks her phone
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Shraddha Kapoor has opened up about her approach to criticism after facing online scrutiny over her Marathi dialogue delivery and accent in the trailer of her soon-to-release movie, Eetha . The star essays the role of legendary Lavani and Tamasha performer Vithabai Narayangaonkar in the movie.

Adding to this, Shraddha Kapoor plays legendary Lavani and Tamasha performer Vithabai Narayangaonkar in Eetha. During a recent Ask Me Anything session on social media, a fan asked Shraddha how she handles criticism. The star shared her trick is to stay away from her phone, which is why she pays little attention to negativity and prefers to focus on her work.

Meanwhile, Shraddha shared, "I actually don't handle criticism. What's there to handle in that? I can't even handle my WhatsApp." The star added that her habit of staying away from her phone has helped her but has also led to her getting scoldings from directors. She shared, "I don't even have a manager, nor am I affiliated with any agency. My friends, directors, and producers keep scolding me that I don't check my phone. I'm not interested in handling any criticism. All I want to do is work, and more and more work. That's it."

Notably, Eetha is a biographical drama directed by Laxman Utekar. Rooted in Maharashtra's traditional Tamasha and Lavani dance forms, the movie is inspired by the life of Vithabai Narayangaonkar. It is produced by Dinesh Vijan and Laxman Utekar and presented by Maddock Films and Kathputli Creations. The movie features music by Ajay-Atul and also stars Mohammed Zeeshan Ayyub and Siddharth Jadhav in pivotal roles. It is scheduled to rollout in cinemas on December 4, 2026.

As per the latest buzz, Vithabai Narayangaonkar was one of Maharashtra's most celebrated Tamasha and Lavani performers. Born on July 1, 1935, in Pandharpur, she grew up in a family of folk artistes. Her grandfather, Narayan Khude, established a travelling Tamasha troupe, which was later run by her father and uncle. Vithabai began performing at a young age and went on to become a prominent name in Maharashtra's folk theatre circuit.

In further updates, She was widely admired for her stage presence and dedication to the art form. She was honoured with medals by the President of India in 1957 and 1990 for her contribution to Tamasha. She also came to be known as 'Tamasha Samradini' or the Empress of Tamasha. The Maharashtra government later instituted the Vithabai Narayangaonkar Lifetime Achievement Award in her memory in 2006. She died on January 15, 2002.

title: Ankita Bhandari's parents stage protest at Rajghat, removed by police
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Parents of Ankita Bhandari, who was murdered at a resort in Uttarakhand in 2022, were removed from Rajghat after they staged a dharna near the public gate of Mahatma Gandhi's memorial, sources shared.

Adding to this, This comes a fortnight after Bhandari's parents were detained by police while protesting against the appointment of Dushyant Kumar Gautam as Sikkim governor. (PTI) This comes a fortnight after Bhandari's parents were detained by police while protesting against the appointment of Dushyant Kumar Gautam as Sikkim governor near India Gate on October 14.

Meanwhile, Bhandari's parents visited Rajghat on Wednesday to offer prayers and interact with the media. They later staged a dharna along with two others near the public gate, which is not a designated protest site, a police source shared.
Notably, The group was repeatedly asked to disperse. After they refused to budge, they were removed from the spot. They were not detained, the source shared.

As per the latest buzz, During the incident, Bhandari's mother Soni Devi complained of health issues and was taken to the Burari government hospital for a medico-legal examination (MLC). However, both she and her husband declined medical examination, the source shared.
In further updates, AAP MLA from Burari Sanjeev Jha and his supporters reached the hospital and Bhandari's parents left with the legislator.
On top of that, Bhandari, who worked as a receptionist at the Vanantra Resort in Rishikesh, was killed on September 18, 2022. Her body was recovered from the Chilla canal four days later.
Resort owner Pulkit Arya, son of former BJP leader Vinod Arya, and his two accomplices were sentenced to life imprisonment in the case.

title: Salman Khan returns to playback singing after 11 years with ‘Teri Sexy Beauty’ from Maatrubhumi
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The movie, directed by Apoorva Lakhia and based on the 2020 Galwan Valley clash, is yet to receive a theatrical rollout date following reported reshoots and pending CBFC screening.

Adding to this, The music video opens with glimpses of Salman entering a recording studio, putting on his headphones and singing the track. Meanwhile, Chitrangda Singh is seen playing the guitar in a red sari. The song features the lyrics, “Teri sexy beauty ka fan ban gaya hu man, main do peg pee ke aeroplane ban gaya hu.”

Meanwhile, Set inside an aeroplane hangar, the video features Chitrangda and background dancers dressed as air hostesses in red outfits, with some of them also seen playing the trumpet. Salman is seen dancing alongside a group of men who appear to be his fellow soldiers enjoying some time off. He later joins Chitrangda on the dance floor. In the movie, the star plays his wife, marking the first time the two actors have been paired together on screen.

Notably, Written and composed by Sajid Khan, ‘ Teri Sexy Beauty ’ features Muskaan on female vocals. Salman’s return to singing comes 11 years after his previous playback contributions to films. He has earlier lent his voice to tracks such as ‘ Main Hoon Hero Tera ’ from Nikkhil Advani’s 2015 movie Hero and ‘ Hangover ’ from Sajid Nadiadwala’s 2014 action comedy Kick .

As per the latest buzz, With this rollout, the makers have unveiled five songs from Maatrubhumi , although the movie's theatrical rollout date is yet to be revealed. The album also includes the patriotic title track, composed by Himesh Reshammiya, written by Sameer Anjaan and sung by Shreya Ghoshal and Arijit Singh. Other songs include ‘ Main Hoon ’, composed and sung by Ayaan Lall with vocals by Ghoshal and lyrics by Shabbir Ahmed, and ‘ Chand Dekh Lena ’, featuring vocals by Nihal Tauro and Ankona Mukherjee. Another patriotic number, ‘ Jai Hind ’, written by Sameer and composed by Reshammiya, was rolled out last month with Stebin Ben on vocals. ‘ Teri Sexy Beauty ’ is the fifth track and the peppiest number from the movie so far.

In further updates, Produced by Salman Khan Films and directed by Apoorva Lakhia, Maatrubhumi has been awaiting its rollout following reported concerns surrounding its portrayal of the Indo-China conflict. Initially titled Battle of Galwan , the movie is based on the 2020 clash between Indian and Chinese troops in the Galwan Valley of Eastern Ladakh. It was subsequently renamed Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace .

On top of that, Reports also suggested that portions of the movie were reshot to introduce a family-drama angle instead of keeping the narrative strictly focused on the military conflict. Following the reshoots, the movie is yet to receive a screening date with the Central Board of Movie Certification (CBFC). It was originally scheduled to arrive in theatres in April this year, but the makers have not revealed a revised rollout date so far.

title: Rajkumar Hirani plans to begin filming Munna Bhai 3 starring Sanjay Dutt and Arshad Warsi in 2027: Report
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

According to a report by Variety India, Farhad Samji is currently working on the screenplay for Munna Bhai 3 and is expected to complete the script soon. Interestingly, Samji has been associated with the franchise since its first instalment, Munna Bhai M.B.B.S ., which was rolled out in 2003. He had written the opening refrain of the movie's popular song ‘ M Bole Toh ’.

Adding to this, The soon-to-release movie is expected to bring back Sanjay Dutt as Murli Prasad Sharma, popularly known as Munna Bhai, alongside Arshad Warsi as his close friend and companion, Circuit. The duo became widely recognised for their on-screen chemistry in the first movie and reprised their roles in the 2006 sequel, Lage Raho Munna Bhai . While the first movie revolved around Munna's journey into the medical world, its sequel explored Gandhian philosophy through humour and the protagonist's unconventional approach to life.
Meanwhile, Rajkumar Hirani on why Munna Bhai 3 took so long

Notably, Despite the audience's continued interest in another instalment, Rajkumar Hirani has maintained that he does not want to move ahead with the movie without a storyline that lives up to the previous two movies. In conversation with Hindustan Times in June, the filmmaker had opened up about the difficulty of developing the sequel and shared, “If you only want to see Munna Bhai up to the interval, I can make five films right now. Because I don't have the story beyond that point.”

As per the latest buzz, Arshad Warsi had also spoken about the challenges surrounding the third movie, revealing that three incomplete scripts already exist. According to the star, these drafts contain interesting scenes and ideas but lack the central connection required to bring the narrative together.
In further updates, Munna Bhai and Circuit's return remains awaited

On top of that, If the reported production schedule moves ahead as planned, Munna Bhai 3 could bring Sanjay Dutt and Arshad Warsi back together on the big screen nearly two decades after Lage Raho Munna Bhai . However, neither the makers nor the actors have officially verified the filming schedule or rollout date.
For now, the development of the screenplay remains the next important step, with audiences awaiting an official announcement about the return of Munna Bhai and Circuit.

title: Jantar Mantar protest case: CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka appear before Crime Branch
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-conveners Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on Thursday reached the Delhi Police Crime Branch office in Rajouri Garden after being summoned for questioning in connection with cases linked to protests at the denotified Jantar Mantar site in October, officials shared.

Adding to this, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were arrested for entering the denotified Jantar Mantar protest site and allegedly violating a peace bond. The two leaders had earlier been arrested and sent to judicial custody after entering the denotified protest site at Jantar Mantar and waving the national flag on October 13, which police shared also violated a peace bond signed by them on October 11.

Meanwhile, They were rolled out from Tihar jail on October 21 after furnishing personal and surety bonds of ₹ 50,000 each. The cases against the CJP leaders were later transferred to the Crime Branch, which had earlier summoned Das and Ranka for questioning before the end of October, but they sought more time.

Notably, The cases stem from an October 14 incident in which Das, Ranka and CJP leader Ajinkya Shinde, along with 11 others, allegedly trespassed into Jantar Mantar, which had been de-notified as the designated protest site. The group was protesting against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and raised slogans against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

As per the latest buzz, All of them were detained by Delhi Police. While Shinde was rolled out on bail after being asked to sign a peace bond, Das and Ranka remained in judicial custody for about a week.

In further updates, Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) Ritu Raj directed the rollout of the two activists after they furnished personal bonds and surety bonds of ₹ 50,000 each until the conclusion of the inquiry in connection with the Jantar Mantar trespassing case.

On top of that, In their written undertakings, Das and Ranka promised not to commit any breach of peace and expressed full faith in the judiciary and all its instruments, including the SEM court, police shared.

title: Ramayana Twitter reviews: Yash steals the show as Ravana; film's 'Avatar X LOTR-level' VFX and climax win praise
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
