Adding to this, Yash's Ravana becomes the highlight in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana. Several viewers have lauded the movie's climax, with many calling it 'mind-blowing'. The visual effects have also received appreciation, with audiences comparing them to Hollywood productions and saying they give the movie an international feel. Ranbir Kapoor, who faced criticism over his casting as Lord Rama when the movie was first revealed, has also received a positive response from viewers, with many calling him 'perfect' for the role. Sai Pallavi has been lauded for her grace as Sita, while Yash appears to have emerged as a major highlight, with several viewers saying he steals the show.

Meanwhile, Calling the VFX award-worthy, an X user wrote, "Visuals are nowhere less than Avatar X LOTR. Yes Namit promised and did it. Animals look so real that I thought they were straight out of Nat Geo. Except Kumbhakarna and subahu, all other large creatures are perfect. Even they don't pull you out of the movie. And Jatayu Man, that deserves a vfx award. A bafta for sure. That's how good it is, like each micro expression can be seen. The scenery, richness, and colours is something we all craved in recent global cinema. It's that good. Acting performances of all the actors are too good, be it ranbir, sai, lakshman, yash perfectly justifying their role. Sita did deserve more screentime. The movie is filled with goosebumps, and at the same time tears, pre interval and climax will tear you up."

Notably, Another moviegoer wrote, "Super Duper extraordinary. Never seen before in Indian cinema. Yash is obviously the highlight but Ranbir Kapoor, sai pallavi is amazingly good as well. Music is great. Yash's costume is out of this world. but the greatest thing about the movie is VFX. Easy LOTR level."

As per the latest buzz, Praising Yash's performance a fan wrote, "Ramayana is the benchmark of Indian cinema. This is how you tell our history and our truth to the world. This is PEAK INDIAN CINEMA. VFX, Action, Emotion, performances everything is absolutely spot on. I am flabbergasted by RAVANA, Yash Boss's performance."

In further updates, A X user was surprised by Ranbir's performance and wrote, "This has to be the best #ramayana ever! First half is peak cinema, second half slows down a bit, but that mind-blowing climax makes it all worth it. Yash as Ravana and Ranbir as Shri Rama were surprisingly excellent. Visuals are out of this world. Absolute must-watch."

On top of that, Many viewers are stunned by the climax of the movie, and one of them wrote, "Yash as Ravana steals the show. Stunning Visuals; Climax Jatayu sequence wow. Ranbir-Sita Episodes fail to bring emotion. Laxman Gud. Music's biggest letdown. Unexciting, Lengthy Drama tests patience in most parts. Grand making and soulless narration. AVG!"

"Breathtaking visuals, monumental scale, and powerful emotions. Yet some moments feel stretched, and the pacing could be tighter. Nitesh Tiwari delivers a grand cinematic experience with flaws, but the impact is epic! A spectacle worth witnessing!" wrote another viewer.

title: Anil Kapoor, Farah Khan apologise to stuntwoman Geeta Tandon after she claims disrespect and 9-hour wait on India Ke Top 1% set
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Anil Kapoor and Farah Khan have apologised to stunt professional Geeta Tandon after she called out the treatment she allegedly received on the sets of India Ke Top 1%. Geeta claimed that she and her son were made to wait for nearly nine hours without proper communication or even basic hospitality. Her account, shared on Instagram, prompted both celebrities to respond, with Anil expressing regret and Farah clarifying that she had no idea Tandon was waiting on the sets.

Adding to this, Anil Kapoor, Farah Khan apologise to Geeta Tandon after stunt artist alleges being left waiting for 9 hours. Anil Kapoor and Farah Khan apologise Anil Kapoor, who hosts the reality show, personally responded to Geeta Tandon's post and acknowledged her disappointment. He wrote: “Geeta ji, it genuinely saddens me to hear this. As the host, I always wanted everyone who was part of the show to feel welcome and respected. You and your son came as our guests. I'm sorry that your experience left you feeling otherwise. I've been in this industry long enough to know how much dignity and respect matter, and I would never want anyone to feel that they were treated with anything less. I take your feedback seriously and genuinely thank you for sharing it.”

Meanwhile, Farah Khan, who was also shooting for the show that day, apologised and shared she was unaware of her presence. Explaining that she was occupied with the second episode, the filmmaker wrote: “Geetaji apologies.. i had no idea you were there as i was shooting for the 2nd episode in the evening.. otherwise would have made you sit in my van as would Anil if he knew.. we have tremendous respect for you and your hard work.”

Notably, The apologies came after Geeta, a stunt professional and body double with over two decades of experience, shared her account of what she described as an upsetting experience on the sets of India Ke Top 1%. She alleged that the production team had repeatedly requested that she and her son appear on the show as guests. Although the appearance was unpaid, she agreed, hoping it would give them some visibility. She also gave up a day's work and called her son back from Goa for the shoot.

As per the latest buzz, According to Geeta, they arrived at the sets at 12:30 PM and were told their segment would be filmed within a few hours. However, the wait kept getting longer, with no clear information about when they would be called. “My son and I were made to sit in a tent, with barely anyone available to even ask for tea or coffee. No proper communication. No updates. No clarity about when we would be called,” she wrote.

In further updates, View this post on Instagram She further alleged that when she finally asked the production team about the delay, the production manager responded, “If they want to leave, let them leave. But they can't leave without signing.” The experience left her and her son with little choice but to walk out. They eventually left the sets at around 9:15 PM. Tandon also used her post to speak about the larger problem of how people working behind the camera are often treated, despite the years they put into the industry.

On top of that, “I have spent years walking alongside some of the biggest names in the industry. Yet people like me, who work tirelessly behind the camera, are still sometimes treated as though our time and our presence mean nothing. The person standing behind the camera deserves the same dignity as the person standing in front of it,” she wrote. She clarified that her intention was not to blame Anil or Farah personally, but to highlight what had happened and draw attention to the need for better treatment of people working behind the scenes.

Geeta's post also received support from actors who have worked with her and recognised her contribution to the movie industry. Tillotama Shome shared a heartfelt note, recalling the physical risks Tandon has taken while performing stunts for actors. She wrote: “Dear Geeta, It’s been an absolute honour to work with you every time. Your spine has broken many times because you were carrying the weight on our behalf. Your dedication and sincerity is unparalleled!! You are not just a good stunt professional, you are a stellar human.”

title: Ramayana Part 1 review: Yash, Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi's spectacular film breathes new life into an epic we know by heart
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Star Ranbir Kapoor is portraying Ram in the movie Ramayana. Cast: Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Yash

Adding to this, Probably every Indian has heard it, seen it, acted in a school play or read about it: the Ramayana. 39 years ago, Ramanand Sagar's television adaptation brought the entire country to a standstill every Sunday. People tell me how they would drop everything to sit in front of the television, with streets practically deserted during the show's time slot. The cultural impact of that adaptation is difficult to replicate. Delivering something that can stand alongside a legacy of this magnitude is a Herculean task.
Meanwhile, Does Namit Malhotra's Ramayana: Part 1 have the bravado to pull it off? In short: yes.

Notably, The story is based on Valmiki's Ramayana , and here, it starts off with Raavan's backstory. It sets the stage up for a visual and narrative contrast when we are introduced to his nemesis, Ram. The screenplay by Sridhar Raghavan and Nitesh Tiwari has enough emotional and dramatic moments. But the first half is slow. The aim, which was always to split the movie into two parts, gave the makers a lot of room for character study. Which gives us long introductions for pretty much everyone. This drags the first half down. There are also some minor issues with the AI dubbing.

As per the latest buzz, The second half thankfully raises the action and we get some truly breathtaking sequences. Which brings me to the VFX. Done by DNEG, Namit's company, perhaps 70 percent of the total budget must have been invested on this technical bit. How else do you justify an alleged ₹ 4000 crore rupees investment?

In further updates, I am happy to report, all that money shows on screen. This is not an average VFX driven movie; care has actually been put into how it all looks. Ramayana Part 1 can truly stand up to any Hollywood movie in this aspect.

On top of that, What is also praiseworthy is how care has been taken to cover the basics properly: from how Raavan took over Kuber's Lanka, his Shiv bhakti, that moment of horror when Kaikayi realises her folly- all this sucks you into the movie. The makers have not messed with how Indians remember the story. (Hi, Adipurush, here's looking at you.)

Now the much publicised collaboration of Hollywood legend Hans Zimmer and Indian titan AR Rahman for the music and background score. While it certainly sounds pleasing and lends a lot to some sequences, the expectations were so sky high that the ultimate results fall short. The songs seem unnecessary sometimes.

title: Rohini Hattangady recalls Dharmendra asking her to wear more makeup as she looked too young to play his mother
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Rohini Hattangady has played mothers to several superstars on screen despite being younger than them. She played Amitabh Bachchan 's mother in Agneepath and Shahenshah, and also shared screen space with Dharmendra as his mother in Humse Na Takrana. In a recent interview with India Today, Rohini recalled how Dharmendra once asked her to wear more make-up because he felt she looked too young to play his mother.

Adding to this, Rohini Hattangady recalls working with Dharmendra. Rohini Hattangady recalls playing Dharmendra's mother in Humse Na Takrana Rohini spoke about being cast in older roles and shared, "It never affected me because when I do a role, it's a role for me. You are doing a character. Main sochti nahi hoon ki yeh bada hai, yeh chhota hai (I was never bothered if the part is that of an elder or younger woman). I'll always act according to my character."

Meanwhile, While Rohini shared Amitabh Bachchan was comfortable with her casting, she recalled an amusing first meeting with Dharmendra on the sets of Humse Na Takrana. During the shoot in Ooty, she went to greet the star on the first day. Soon after she settled into her chair, her make-up artist rushed over with an unexpected request.

Notably, She recalled, "My make-up man came and started working extensively on me. I asked him what he was doing, and why we were still not done. He sheepishly informed me that I was told to put on more make-up because Dharam ji was saying that I was looking young. I wondered how much make-up I would need, and how much white hair we would need? And what am I supposed to do because I am young?" she recalled, laughing.

As per the latest buzz, Directed by Deepak Bahry, the 1990 action drama Humse Na Takrana starred Dharmendra, Jeetendra, Anita Raj and Amrish Puri in lead roles. Rohini Hattangady played Dharmendra's mother in the movie. Born in 1951, Rohini was just 39 when she played the role in the movie, while Dharmendra was 55 at the time.

In further updates, Rohini is best remembered for portraying Kasturba Gandhi in Richard Attenborough's Gandhi (1982). Her performance collected her the BAFTA Award for Best Star in a Supporting Role, making her the first Indian star to win the honour in that category. She also won the National Movie Award for Best Supporting Star for her performance in Party (1984).
On top of that, Over the years, Rohini has featured in several acclaimed films, including Arth, Agneepath, ChaalBaaz, Pukar and Munna Bhai MBBS, among others.

She was most of late seen in the Netflix movie Meethe Mein Kya Hai. Directed by Radhika Bansal, the movie tells the story of a young widower whose grief eases during a joyful Diwali reunion, until his sister's surprise marriage throws the family into chaos. The movie also stars Ritwik Bhowmik, Ayesha Raza, Gaurav Sharma, Tarana Raja, Abhay Kaul and Shivika Rishi, among others.

title: Namit Malhotra feels like ‘Sachin Tendulkar getting picked for World Cup on debut' while taking Ramayana global
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Producer Namit Malhotra has shared that the scale of Ramayana ’s global rollout is unprecedented. The movie, directed by Nitesh Tiwari, is releasing globally on 70,000 screens, more than twice as wide a rollout as any Indian movie has had before. Namit, who has bankrolled the movie, has shared that it is his dream to take Indian storytelling globally with the movie. Now, in a new interview, he re-emphasised this dream, comparing himself to cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar.

Adding to this, Nitesh Tiwari, Yash, Ranbir Kapoor and Namit Malhotra attend the Ramayana press line during 2026 Comic-Con International: San Diego in July. (Photo by Emma McIntyre / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) (Getty Images via AFP) ‘Like Sachin Tendulkar on debut’ Ahead of its rollout, Ramayana had its world premiere at the David Geffen Theatre at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles, where the films nominated for Oscars are screened. This was hailed as a monumental achievement for an Indian movie. Talking with PTI, Namit shared, “The biggest thing I feel right now is gratitude because, to me, the fact that we have a movie industry for over 100 years, and I get to have this golden opportunity to produce Ramayana and to present it to the world like never before, is unbelievable. There are generations of filmmakers who have come before me who are brilliant in what they've done in India. But a Ramayana like this has never been made by any Indian filmmaker. And I get to be that person today. It's like Sachin Tendulkar getting picked to play the World Cup on his debut.”

Meanwhile, Based on the epic by Valmiki, the Ramayana is a story widely known to almost every Indian. But to Westerners, it is largely new. Namit says that with the movie, he hopes to introduce Western audiences to the story. He added, “Just imagine I'm standing here and saying, 'You guys know The Odyssey, Lord of the Rings, Harry Potter, and Star Wars, but do you know that Ramayana came before all of these great epics? And it's not trying to copy or borrow from you. In fact, it's an original story. It's original characters and an original world that have been envisioned. So they are excited about it. And that's why I think that the opportunity to connect with the audience is very exciting.”

Notably, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit's Prime Focus and Yash's Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, and Yash as Ravana. The first part is scheduled for worldwide rollout on November 5, while the second part is set for Diwali 2028. The films will rollout in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam across India.
As per the latest buzz, Sony Pictures will handle global distribution, excluding India, while Dharma Productions will distribute the movie in the Hindi-speaking market.

Delhi HC quashes PIL seeking stay on Suryaa A bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma shared the court was not inclined to entertain the public interest litigation (PIL) as the issue has already been raised by the doctor fraternity in another writ petition which is pending before a single judge.

Meanwhile, On November 2, the single judge issued notice to the authorities and asked them to respond to the petition alleging that the movie portrays doctors in private hospitals as corrupt and that it encourages violence against healthcare professionals.
Notably, The court shared the petitioners may join the proceedings before the single judge and also granted them liberty to pursue their representation before the authorities.

As per the latest buzz, The PIL was filed by Dr Nachiketa Bhatia and Dr Dhruv Chauhan seeking to stay the rollout of the movie on the ground that its official trailer depicts physical violence against medical practitioners as heroic and unfairly generalises corruption in the healthcare profession.

In further updates, The petitioners shared the movie threatens public law and order and sought a direction to the Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting and the Central Board of Movie Certification ( CBFC ) to examine and modify or delete allegedly objectionable scenes or dialogues from the movie.

On top of that, On being asked by the bench as to why it should entertain the plea when a similar petition is already pending before another bench of the high court, the petitioners' counsel shared the issue is sensitive and the scope in a PIL is more as compared to a writ petition.

The counsel for CBFC shared till now, no certification has been issued to the movie and the same is pending consideration. He also shared that the Hindi movie is not the original one and it is a remake of a South Indian movie which is already in the public domain.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Kareena Kapoor made her Bollywood debut with Refugee, rolled out on June 30, 2000, and since then there has been no turning back for the star. Over the past quarter of a century, she has performed a wide variety of roles, from mainstream performers to quirky character-driven pieces, and she has worked across genres to accommodate shifting tastes. She belongs to the prominent Kapoor family of Hindi cinema, being the granddaughter of star Raj Kapoor and the daughter of actors Randhir Kapoor and Babita.

Adding to this, Kareena Kapoor has been a star in the Hindi movie industry for over two decades. ( SHAZID CHAUHAN/ANI) Kareena on being a ‘nepo baby’ But the star has rejected the ‘nepo baby’ tag on her during her appearance on the latest episode of Koffee With Karan with husband Saif Ali Khan. After Saif won a fun segment on the chat show, he quipped that it proves that Karan Johar's show is not nepotistic and biased. Kareena looked surprised and asked why would he say that. In response, Karan elaborated and pointed at her as the nepo baby.

Meanwhile, To this, Kareena had a hilarious response. She shared, “I am the poster girl for being the purest talent of nepotism. The purest, organic talent! Maine kabhi apne maa baap ka naam nahi liya hai (I have never taken the names of my parents)!” Karan shared ‘waah!’ at this comment and joined Saif as they mockingly clapped at this statement.

Notably, The star had previously shared her take on nepotism. In 2020, speaking with Barkha Dutt, she had shared, “21 years of working would not have happened with just nepotism. It is not possible. I can take a long list out of superstars’ children for whom it’s not been able to happen that way.”

As per the latest buzz, Kareena shared that she does not look at her journey as having got opportunities just because of her lineage. “It might sound weird but my struggle is there. There is a struggle but it probably is not as interesting as somebody who comes in a train with just ₹ 10 in his pocket. Yeah, it’s not been that and I can’t be apologetic about it,” she shared.

In further updates, Kareena shared that those coming from movie families work just as hard as outsiders. “The idea is that today so many of our biggest stars whom you (the audience) have chosen, whether it is Akshay Kumar or Shah Rukh Khan or Ayushmann Khurrana or Rajkummar Rao, are all outsiders. They are successful actors because they have worked hard. Whether it is Alia Bhatt or Kareena Kapoor, we have also worked hard. You are enjoying our films and watching them. So, it’s the audience that makes or breaks us,” she added.
On top of that, Kareena was last seen in Daayra , directed by Meghna Gulzar. The movie underperformed at the ticket-window.

title: Kareena Kapoor slams conspiracy theories around Saif Ali Khan knife attack, says son Jeh saw the entire incident
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The latest episode of the final season of Koffee With Karan marked the return of both Saif Ali Khan and Kareena Kapoor to Karan Johar’s couch. The couple spoke in detail about the horrific knife attack on Saif at their home last year, breaking their silence on the conspiracies on whether it was staged and how the star recovered so quickly. Kareena criticized the rumours and shared how traumatised she was to see the blood on Saif.

Adding to this, Kareena Kapoor and Saif Ali Khan have been married for over a decade now. (PTI) What did Kareena say? Kareena shared, “I don't understand the conspiracy theories. That means that the people thought that cops are in cahoots with us because they obviously caught the guy! So then? Are they in the conspiracy? Saif's son took him to hospital with Hari [house help]. It is really bad that people had those concerns. I was hailing a rickshaw in my night t-shirt. Luckily no one got that on video, Karan. I was screaming on the road. I was running like a mad woman while he was bleeding and I looked at Saif in the lift, and when I saw him I shared, ‘Don’t do this.' The first thing that Tim shared was, ‘Abba are you going to die?’”

Meanwhile, Meanwhile Saif shared that he was calm and composed throughout the incident. Recalling the ordeal, Saif called it “the worst night in the history of nights.” The star opened up about the severity of his injuries and the strength it took to remain composed through the situation, especially with their children witnessing it. “You could not walk!” Kareena recalled, sharing how the doctor had to move his nerves to take out the knife from his spine. “I was a wreck, he was fine,” she shared. Kareena shared their youngest son, Jeh, saw the entire incident with his own eyes and gifted Saif his plastic sword to protect him in the future. “He thinks of Saif as some sort of Iron Man,” shared Kareena.

Notably, The incident unfolded in the early hours of January 16, 2025, when an intruder allegedly made his way into Saif Ali Khan’s 12th-floor apartment in Bandra through the fire escape. According to the prosecution’s case, he first confronted Eliyama Philip, the nurse caring for Saif and Kareena Kapoor Khan’s four-year-old son, Jehangir. The intruder allegedly warned her to make "no noise" and attacked her when she tried to pick up the child.

As per the latest buzz, Philip then asked him what he wanted. He allegedly replied, "Paisa chahiye" and demanded ₹ 1 crore rupees. Her screams alerted Saif and Kareena, who rushed to the room. It was during the confrontation that Saif was allegedly attacked.

In further updates, The star sustained six stab wounds, including a serious injury to his thoracic spinal cord. A 2.5-inch piece of the knife was lodged in his spine and had to be removed during emergency surgery at Lilavati Hospital. Doctors also treated injuries to his hand and neck, for which he underwent plastic surgery. Saif was discharged five days after the attack.
On top of that, Police arrested Mohammad Shariful Islam two days later in Thane. They alleged that he was a Bangladeshi national staying illegally in India and had been using the name Vijay Das.

Islam is facing charges under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for alleged armed robbery, causing grievous hurt and house-trespass. The case also includes charges under the Foreigners Act and the Passport (Entry into India) Rules.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Singer Abhijeet Bhattacharya has addressed the row surrounding Daler Mehndi . The singer, who of late performed at Chhattisgarh Rajyotsava 2026, spoke out against the practice of lip-syncing during live performances. Although he did not name Daler , he referred to the incident in which a singer was called out by a minister for not singing live at an event.

Adding to this, Abhijeet Bhattacharya spoke about Daler Mehndi row. ‘Minister spoke the truth, but he became the villain’ A video of Abhijeet addressing the row has been doing the rounds on social media. In the clip, he says in Hindi, which translates to, "If someone is not actually singing live into the microphone, then don't allow it. A few days ago, there was an incident where a minister came onto the stage and spoke the truth. He shared, 'You are not singing. You can barely stand, and you are not really performing live.' He spoke the truth. But he ended up becoming the villain in the eyes of many people. Yet this is something that happens on stages everywhere."

Meanwhile, He added, "I request all of you, especially here in Chhattisgarh, not to let this happen. No matter how I sing, whether I sing badly, whether my voice is strained, whether I get tired, or whether I sing off-key, whatever I do, I will sing live. That is the respect I owe you for giving me your time. You have spent your hard-collected money, invited me here, and made all these arrangements. Behind this event lies the hard work of the administration, the department and all of you. I bow to all of you and promise that I will never cheat you in this way. I will never simply move my lips in the name of singing. Some people do that, but I won't."

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

All eyes are on Ramayana as it releases in screens tomorrow. Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is the biggest Indian movie in terms of scale and budget. After its world premiere in Los Angeles last week, Ramayana held a special screening in Mumbai on Tuesday, attended by the cast and crew, as well as members of the movie fraternity.

Adding to this, Badshah has seen Ramayana and penned a review of the movie. Badshah reviews Ramayana Singer and music composer Badshah has seen the movie and posted a review of the movie just before its rollout day. Responding to a post on X where a user shared that they are excited to see the movie after looking at the rave reviews it is getting, Badshah wrote in the caption, “You have to watch it. Namit has delivered. Every frame is breathtaking. The characters feel so real. It made me cry, even when we’ve known the story since our childhood. INCREDIBL BGM. Ranbir, Sai Pallavi, Ravi Dubey, Yash, Lara Dutta, Arun Govil, Rakul. Everyone nailed it. Jatayu scene is insane. And wait for the moment when the dharti amber theme comes. CLAPSSSS. PLEASE GO WATCH IT.”

Meanwhile, Ramayana, made on a reported budget of ₹ 4000 crore rupees, is one of the most expensive movie productions in the world, not just in India. With VFX from eight-time Oscar-winning studio DNEG, it is being marketed as India's first movie equivalent of Hollywood blockbusters. For its global rollout, the makers have partnered with Sony Pictures, which is giving it the widest rollout for any Indian movie - in 70,000 screens.

Notably, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit's Prime Focus and Yash's Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, and Yash as Ravana. The first part is scheduled for worldwide rollout on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2027. The films will rollout in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam across India.

As per the latest buzz, "In India, there are a lot of questions like, 'Why are they making the Ramayana when there have been so many Ramayanas? We already know the story.' title: Stuntwoman Geeta Tandon accuses India Ke Top 1% team of mistreatment; says she waited nearly 9 hours with son
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
In a strongly worded social media post, the stunt professional recounts being invited for an unpaid appearance, alleging that the team was disrespectful.

Adding to this, Hosted by Anil Kapoor, India Ke Top 1% is a game show featuring around 100 participants competing for prize money of up to Rs. 1 crore rupees. The show airs on Star Plus and also streams on JioHotstar. Tandon shared she had agreed to appear on the programme without any payment, believing it would offer her some visibility. However, she alleged that the experience left her feeling disrespected.

Meanwhile, Opening her post, she wrote, “20 years in this industry. And yesterday, I was reminded how little respect people working behind the scenes are sometimes given.” Explaining how she came to be on the sets, Tandon shared, “My name is Geeta Tandon. I have worked in the movie and television industry for over two decades, as a body double for some of the biggest actresses in the country and as a stunt director. I have dedicated years of my life to this profession, often working behind the camera, and I have always taken immense pride in what I do. Yesterday, I was invited to appear as a guest on the show India Ke Top 1%, to interact with Anil Kapoor, along with my son.”

Notably, According to Tandon, the production team had repeatedly followed up with her for the appearance. She claimed that she gave up a day's work and even called her son back from Goa specifically for the shoot. Recalling the events of the day, she shared she reached the set at 12:30 PM and was informed that her segment would be filmed within a few hours. However, the wait allegedly continued through the day, with little communication from the team. She further alleged that she and her son were made to sit in a tent without proper updates or clarity about when they would be called. Tandon shared that when she eventually confronted the production team, she was met with another response that she found unacceptable.

As per the latest buzz, Recalling the exchange, she wrote, “The production manager, Jaydeep, responded, ‘If they want to leave, let them leave. But they can't leave without signing.’ Signing what? And why should anyone be made to feel that they cannot leave after being kept waiting all day?” Tandon claimed that she and her son eventually left the set at 9:15 PM, after spending nearly nine hours there. Emphasising that the appearance was unpaid, she shared the least she expected was basic courtesy and respect for their time.

In further updates, Addressing Banijay Asia, Anil Kapoor and Farah Khan, she clarified that she did not know how much they were aware of the alleged incident and was not suggesting that they had personally instructed anyone to treat them that way. However, she wanted them to know about the experience of guests invited to the show.

On top of that, Concluding her post, Tandon highlighted the larger issue of how professionals working behind the scenes are treated in the entertainment industry. She wrote, “The person standing behind the camera deserves the same dignity as the person standing in front of it.”

She also dedicated her post to stunt professionals, junior artists, body doubles, technicians, background performers and other guests, reiterating that respect should not depend on someone's star status.

title: Bengaluru-based IT engineer arrested for sending extortion threats to Ayushmann Khurrana, Tusshar Kapoor
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

A 30-year-old IT engineer from Bengaluru has been arrested by the Mumbai police crime branch for allegedly sending threat and extortion messages to several actors, including Ayushmann Khurrana and Tusshar Kapoor . The police shared the accused thought of making a quick buck, taking advantage of the recent threats and firing incidents, allegedly undertaken by Lawrence Bishnoi gang to terrorise Bollywood celebrities.

Adding to this, Ayushmann Khurrana got an extortion threat from an IT engineer. (Sandip Mahankal ) The police shared the arrested man has been identified as Vaibhav Mishra, 30, who worked as an IT engineer in Bengaluru. The accused had sent messages to Ayushmann and several other actors on Instagram.

Meanwhile, “After the information was reported by the actors, we started tracing the sender through his online profile and using technical details, we succeeded in reaching him. We have just taken him into custody,” shared a police officer, adding that the accused had sent an audio clip threatening star Tusshar Kapoor and demanding ₹ 5 crore rupees.

Notably, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Crime Branch) Rajtilak Roushan, verified the arrest and shared that Mishra would be brought to Mumbai after obtaining a transit remand from a local court in Bengaluru.
As per the latest buzz, “As of now, it does not appear that the IT engineer is linked to the Bishnoi gang in any manner, but we are yet to interrogate him and ascertain that,” the officer shared.

In further updates, A few days after the shooting at star Tiger Shroff’s car in Juhu on October 18, Tusshar Kapoor received an audio clip allegedly sent by Hari Chand Jat aka Harry Boxer, a close aide of incarcerated gangster Lawrence Bishnoi.

On top of that, The star alerted the police about the threatening voice clip. Though the police sent the audio clip for forensic analysis, they felt the voice did not match Boxer’s voice samples available in police records. Therefore, they concluded it appeared to be the handiwork of someone else, perhaps trying to take advantage of the situation created by the Bishnoi gang.

title: Ramayana advance booking races to ₹150 crore in final hours before release; Ranbir Kapoor-Yash film beats Adipurush, but way behind Dhurandhar 2
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Advance bookings for Ramayana are set to come to a close as the movie enters the home stretch. Hours remain before the movie's first screenings on Thursday morning, and pre-sales are at their peak. Advance bookings crossed the ₹ 100 crore rupees mark on Tuesday and are now racing towards the ₹ 150-crore rupees mark.

Adding to this, Ramayana will rollout worldwide on November 5. Ramayana advance bookings For the first 10 days after advance bookings for Ramayana opened on Dussehra, pre-sales did not gain momentum. That was largely due to a standoff between the exhibitors and the distributors over revenue sharing. Once that was resolved over the weekend, more screens opened, and advance bookings gained momentum. By Wednesday afternoon, the number of screens for the movie had increased to over 6000. Over a thousand of these were added in the last 24 hours. By noon on November 4, less than 24 hours before the movie releases, Ramayana had grossed a staggering ₹ 78 crore rupees in pre-sales in India. This includes an impressive ₹ 34 crore rupees from the opening day itself. What is truly impressive about Ramayana’s advance-booking trend is that the entire weekend is seeing huge demand for tickets, not just on opening day. Ramayana has now sold over 20 lakh tickets in pre-sales across India.

Meanwhile, Overseas, Ramayana has reached the $6 million mark in pre-sales. This includes $1.5 million from the Wednesday paid previews in the United States, which is among the highest for an Indian movie. As of noon, Ramayana has grossed ₹ 135 crore rupees in advance bookings worldwide, with trade insiders predicting the figure to reach ₹ 150 crore rupees by the end of the day.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sony Pictures UK (@sonypicturesuk)

As per the latest buzz, Ramayana looks set to gross ₹ 40 crore rupees in advance bookings for its opening day across India. The movie has already beaten the marks of Bollywood blockbusters such as Pathaan ( ₹ 27.2 crore rupees), Stree 2 ( ₹ 28.3 crore rupees), and Animal ( ₹ 32.3 crore rupees), as well as Adipurush ( ₹ 26 crore rupees), the previous adaptation of the epic. It is projected to surpass Shah Rukh Khan’s Jawan ( ₹ 34.5 crore rupees) by the afternoon. However, it is a long way behind Hindi cinema’s all-time record, set by Ranveer Singh’s Dhurandhar The Revenge earlier this year. The Aditya Dhar movie amassed ₹ 95.6 crore rupees before rollout in March. This was aided by paid previews, but even after excluding them, Dhurandhar 2’s day 1 advance booking haul of ₹ 50+ crore rupees is beyond Ramayana’s reach.

In further updates, Ashish Saksena, COO - cinemas, BookMyShow shared, “Ramayana’s advance booking trajectory signals the arrival of a major theatrical event. With nearly a million tickets sold on BookMyShow ahead of the rollout, the movie has set a new benchmark for pre-Diwali period becoming the biggest movie title on the platform. Even for a Diwali-window, the movie is poised to set new ticket-window records, looking at the advance sales trends. What stands out is not just the scale of bookings, but the acceleration in demand as rollout day approaches, the strength of its opening-day sales and the traction across multiple language markets."

On top of that, He added that while Hindi accounted for nearly three-fourths of the advance bookings, the Kannada and Telugu dubbed versions were also witnessing strong demand. According to him, this reflected the growing maturity of language markets for large-scale cinematic experiences. He noted that premium formats such as IMAX, 3D, 4D, Dolby and EPIQ were contributing disproportionately to the overall ticket value, with one in every five tickets booked being for a premium format.

Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The first part is scheduled for worldwide rollout on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2028. The films will rollout in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam across India.

title: Ram Kamal Mukherjee wins Best Director at the 11th International Indian Film Festival of Toronto for Lokkhikantopur Local
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
National Award-winning filmmaker shares the prestigious Best Director honour with Bollywood filmmaker Kabir Khan, recognised for Chandu Champion.

Adding to this, The recognition places Mukherjee alongside noted veteran Bollywood filmmaker Kabir Khan, who also received the Best Director honour for his acclaimed movie Chandu Champion , starring Kartik Aaryan. This latest achievement marks another significant milestone for Mukherjee, who won his first National Movie Award in 2023 for his Hindi short movie Ek Duaa . With Lokkhikantopur Local , the filmmaker continues to make his mark through stories rooted in Indian realities and human emotions.

Meanwhile, Sharing his happiness, Ram Kamal Mukherjee shared, “Every award is special, but international recognition for a story told in my mother tongue makes it even more emotional. Lokkhikantopur Local is very close to my heart. It celebrates the people, places, and stories that often remain unnoticed but are deeply woven into the fabric of our lives. To have this movie recognised on an international platform is truly overwhelming. Sharing this honour with a filmmaker of Kabir Khan's stature makes the moment even more special. I remember interviewing Kabir when I was working with Stardust. He is a brilliant storyteller. I dedicate this award to my producer Sangita Sinha and my entire directorial team who had faith in my vision, and the jury members at IIFFT for evaluating this movie in the same light as a mega-star Kartik Aaryan movie like Chandu Champion ; this gives me hope that good content will always find its own audience.”

Notably, From winning a National Movie Award for Ek Duaa to receiving international recognition for Lokkhikantopur Local , Ram Kamal Mukherjee's journey is a testament to his commitment to meaningful storytelling and cinema that transcends geographical and linguistic boundaries.

As per the latest buzz, The movie is produced by Sangita Sinha under the banner of Angel Creations. “I am extremely proud of my director Ram Kamal dada for winning this prestigious award in Toronto. The competition was tough, as regional cinema comes with a lot of financial restrictions, but still, on the basis of pure content and performance, the movie won hearts,” says Sangita Sinha, who also plays a pivotal role as an star in Lokkhikantopur Local .

In further updates, “I am delighted to know that Ram Kamal won the Best Director Award at IIFFT, and he is definitely deserving. His craft has been well appreciated by national and international cine-connoisseurs since his debut movie, Cakewalk . This was my first association with Ram Kamal, and the way he weaved in the character of Labanya with Utpal (Kaushik Ganguly) and Kalyani (Paoli Dam) in the multilayered plot shows his credentials as a filmmaker,” says Bengal's iconic female superstar, Rituparna Sengupta.

title: Those indulging in dharna, hunger strike in educational institutes liable to be ‘expelled': HC
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Kerala high court on Tuesday struck down an interim order passed by a single-judge bench that permitted 16 suspended students of the Students Federation of India (SFI) to appear for examinations beginning November 4 at the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit.
Adding to this, The students have moved the Supreme Court against the high court’s decision. (File Photo) The students have moved the Supreme Court against the high court’s decision.

Meanwhile, The division bench of justices Anil K Narendran and Muralee Krishna S on Tuesday allowed the appeal filed by the university challenging the single judge’s interim order. The university contended that the suspended students lacked the requisite attendance to appear for the examinations and had not cleared their internal exams.

Notably, The students, belonging to the SFI, were suspended on August 13 after they staged a protest on the university campus, including a mock cremation of the vice chancellor. The vice chancellor was also as per reports manhandled during the protest, and attempts were made to damage her car.

As per the latest buzz, In its order on Tuesday, the high court relied on a 2017 division bench ruling of the same court, which shared that anyone indulging in activities such as a dharna, satyagraha or hunger strike in an educational institution was liable to be ‘expelled or rusticated’.

In further updates, “Educational institutions are meant for imparting education and not politics. By their political ambition, the political parties cannot hold to ransom the educational institution or the right of the civilised students to receive education,” shared the 2017 verdict of the High Court in Dr Antony Thomas v VM Muhammed Rafique and others.
On top of that, The high court also underlined that there was a total lack of pleadings in the suspended students’ petition regarding their entitlement to appear for the university examinations.

“By issuing such an interim order, the learned single judge directed the university and its officials to act contrary to the requirements of the relevant regulations, which is legally impermissible in view of the law laid down by the apex court...” the high court shared on Tuesday.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Sandeep Reddy Vanga has hit back at critics who have blamed A-rated films with bloodshed and gore for normalising violence in society. He criticized critics for using real-life tragedies as an excuse to target his and others' work, accusing them of being more interested in settling personal scores than addressing the larger issue.

Adding to this, Sandeep Reddy Vanga slams critics for blaming his films for normalising violence. Sandeep Reddy Vanga slams those targeting violent films The recent chainsaw attack in Andhra Pradesh sparked an online conversation over how violent films such as Animal , Marco and Dhurandhar risk providing criminals with real-life templates to imitate and contributing to the normalisation of violence.

Meanwhile, On Wednesday, Sandeep took to X to respond to the criticism. He wrote, "When someone commits a heinous crime, the first response should be empathy & an attempt to understand the larger problem. Not finding a convenient scapegoat in cinema. It is becoming increasingly clear that your concern is not for the victims or their families, but that you're using a horrific tragedy as a dirty excuse to settle your personal scores."

Notably, He added, "This is especially directed at those failed, frustrated, jobless male/female actors, few directors, producers & parasites, who suddenly appoint themselves as social reformers whenever an opportunity arises to take a dig at someone else's work. A tragedy deserves empathy 🙏, not opportunism. Learn the difference."

As per the latest buzz, Before Sandeep's post, filmmaker Ram Gopal Varma had also come to the defence of films after several X users shared pictures and videos from recent releases such as Animal and KGF, pointing out how these films depict violence without consequences. Responding to the criticism, the filmmaker wrote, “Blaming films for rise in violence is like, blaming Ramayana for rise in kidnappings.”

In further updates, Vanga made his directorial debut with the 2017 Telugu movie Arjun Reddy, starring Vijay Deverakonda. The movie was a major success and was later remade in Hindi as Kabir Singh in 2019, featuring Shahid Kapoor and Kiara Advani. The Hindi remake also emerged as a commercial success, while sparking considerable debate over its portrayal of masculinity, relationships and violence.

On top of that, His next directorial, Animal, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Rashmika Mandanna, Anil Kapoor, Bobby Deol and Triptii Dimri, took his filmmaking style into darker and more violent territory. Centred on a complicated father-son relationship and a man's obsessive need for his father's approval, the movie became a major box-office success, crossing ₹ 900 crore rupees worldwide. However, it also attracted criticism for its portrayal of toxic masculinity, misogyny and graphic violence.

The filmmaker is now awaiting the rollout of Spirit, starring Prabhas and Triptii Dimri in lead roles. The movie also features Vivek Oberoi, Kanchana and Aishwarya Desai in key roles. Its promotional material hints at a story centred on a disgraced cop. Originally slated for rollout in March 2027, the movie is now scheduled to hit theatres on October 29, 2027.

title: Kunal Kapoor says working with Avengers Doomsday movement coach Terry Notary elevated Ramayana cast's work
body: Here's the latest update from the Hollywood/Marvel world:

Kunal Kapoor plays Lord Indra in Ramayana . In the movie, his character is seen fighting Ravana, played by Yash . The star features in several large-scale action sequences, which were shot using green screens. Since this was Kunal's first time working with a green screen, he of late opened up about the experience and credited Hollywood action director Terry Notary for guiding the actors through the action sequences and helping them with their body language.

Adding to this, Kunal Kapoor plays Lord Indra in Ramayana. Kunal Kapoor on working with a green screen In conversation with SCREEN, Kunal opened up about working with a green screen for the first time. He shared, “The thing with the green screen is there’s nothing available to you. There’s no real palace or sunrise. Everything is out of your imagination. You’ve to create pretty much everything in your head. But that can be a lot of fun as well. Because it takes you back to the most important thing as an star — your imagination. It also takes you back to your childhood, where you’d play with imagination. That was a lot of fun."

Meanwhile, Kunal credited Terry Notary for guiding him and the other actors through the movie's action sequences. Terry is best known for his work as a movement coach on Hollywood films, including the Planet of the Apes franchise, X2 (2003), Superman Returns (2006) and Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer (2007). He has also worked on the Russo Brothers' soon-to-release Marvel movie Avengers: Doomsday.

Notably, Kunal shared, “We got very lucky because we had somebody like Terry. He trained all the actors in the Planet of the Apes to imbibe that body language. What I found really fascinating about working with him was he was not just an action director, but a body language expert directing action. That’s very different from working with an action director. Just having that kind of a talent on the movie makes it incredibly easy for everybody else. Because you’re shooting not only an action sequence, but also an important part of a story that’s close to all our hearts. So, when you find talent that looks at it and approaches it like that, it really elevates the work,” he shared.
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kunal K Kapoor (@kunalkkapoor)

In further updates, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra, Ramayana is a two-part adaptation of the epic. It stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Sunny Deol as Hanuman and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. It is set to hit theatres worldwide on November 5, 2026.
On top of that, While Ramayana Part 2 was planned for Diwali 2027, Namit of late revealed in an interview that the movie is postponed to 2028.

title: Ayushmann Khurrana and Rajkummar Rao bring back memories of Bareilly Ki Barfi, dance together at Diwali party
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

In a video that was shared by Ayushmann on his Instagram account, Ayushmann and his Bareilly Ki Barfi co-star Rajkummar Rao grooved together to the title track of Yeh Prem Mol Liya.

Adding to this, Rajkummar Rao and Ayushmann Khurrana danced together in the party. Ayushmann and Rajkummar dance together Ayushmann and Rajkummar danced beside one another, as casting director Mukesh Chhabra, actors Abhishek Banerjee and Aparshakti Khurana cheered them on and joined them after a while. Ayushmann and Rajkummar held hands and were all smiles as they grooved to the song. In the caption, Ayushmann wrote, “Prem waali Diwaali sab ke saath (It is the Diwali of love with everyone).”

Meanwhile, Ayushmann and Rajkummar starred in the 2017 rollout Bareilly Ki Barfi, which went on to become a ticket-window success. Directed by Ashwiny Iyer Tiwari, Bareilly Ki Barfi revolved around Bitti Mishra (Kriti Sanon) and her two suitors, Chirag Dubey (Ayushmann Khurrana) and Pritam Vidrohi (Rajkummar Rao). It was Pritam's transformation from a meek guy to a rowdy suitor that drew praise from followers.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ayushmann Khurrana (@ayushmannk)

As per the latest buzz, Meanwhile, Bhushan Kumar, Guneet Monga, Apoorva Mehta, Amar Kaushik, Sara Ali Khan, Akash Kaushik and Arjun Kapoor were among those present at the party. Earlier, Tahira had shared a glimpse of the celebrations on her Instagram account. Sharing the video, Tahira wrote, “Let there be love and light Diwali celebrations for @ayushmannk and me have always been with our family and friends! Mumbai has become home, and so our friends are our extended family here! We slept at 5 am and danced till our feet hurt...the best feeling."

In further updates, Ayushmann will be seen next in Yeh Prem Mol Liya, directed by Sooraj R Barjatya. The title track, sung by Shreya Ghoshal and Nihal Tauro, was of late rolled out by the makers. It features Ayushmann and Sharvari and plays out against wedding celebrations and family gatherings, giving the song the familiar Rajshri visual language while introducing the new pair. The movie also marks another collaboration between Barjatya and Himesh Reshammiya, who previously worked together on Prem Ratan Dhan Payo.

On top of that, Yeh Prem Mol Liya brings Rajshri’s much-loved Prem character back to the big screen after 12 years. This time, Ayushmann takes on the role, with Sharvari as his leading lady. The movie revolves around a relationship that starts with friendship and gradually grows into something deeper. At the centre of the story is a clash between modern ideas of romance and the traditional warmth of a joint family.

The ensemble cast includes Anupam Kher, Supriya Pathak, Seema Pahwa and Saumya Tandon. Produced by Rajshri Productions in association with Mahaveer Jain Films, the movie is scheduled to arrive in theatres on November 27, 2026.

title: Police detain rail roko protesters demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's arrest in Tamil Nadu
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Tension prevailed near the old railway station in Kanchipuram on Wednesday after members of the Jananayaka Meetpu Kuzhu staged a rail roko protest demanding the arrest of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

Adding to this, Police later detained all the protesters and housed them in a private marriage hall. (PTI, representational image) The protesters alleged that the CEC acted in favour of Prime Minister Narendra Modi by disqualifying 13 crore rupees voters.
Meanwhile, Heavy police and Railway Protection Force personnel were deployed in the area in view of the demonstration.

Notably, More than 350 protesters marched in a rally from near Hotel Tamil Nadu towards the East Railway Station, where a scuffle broke out between the demonstrators and the police when officers attempted to stop their advance.

As per the latest buzz, Defying police barricades, more than 50 protesters sat on the railway tracks and raised slogans against the Prime Minister and the Election Commission, repeating their demand for the arrest of the CEC.
In further updates, Police later detained all the protesters and housed them in a private marriage hall.

On top of that, Members of Makkal Mandram, Communist Party of India, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi, and independent social activists participated in the agitation which caused tension in the area for about an hour.

Earlier on October 17, the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) Parliamentary Party adopted a resolution demanding the immediate removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar from office and an inquiry into his conduct, accusing him of spearheading the systematic disenfranchisement of legitimate voters through the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Adding to this, Visually impaired Hanuman Ansh singer Suneel Lodhi's eye treatment starts. title: ‘Baby Doll’ singer Kanika Kapoor announces separation from husband Gautam Hathiramani
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Meanwhile, Kanika's marriage to Gautam Hathiramani was her second. She was previously married to Raj Chandok in 1999. The couple parted ways in 2012 after 13 years of marriage. From her first marriage, Kanika has three children — two daughters, Aayana and Samara, and a son, Yuvraaj.

title: Ranbir Kapoor reveals he trained with an Indian Olympian archer for 18 months before filming Ramayana
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ranbir Kapoor -starrer Ramayana : Part 1 is all set to hit the big screen on Thursday, November 5. The movie had its premiere at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles on October 27. Following the premiere, Ranbir spoke in an interview about how he prepared for the physical aspects of playing Lord Rama, including learning archery and undergoing special workshops.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor spoke about the work that went into preparing to play Lord Rama in Ramayana. Ranbir Kapoor trained with an Indian Olympian for Ramayana During an interaction with Review Nation, Ranbir shared that he began training for the role nearly a year and a half before filming began. He opened up that he worked with an Indian Olympian to learn the right archery techniques and also attended workshops focused on movement, breathing and physicality.

Meanwhile, Speaking about his preparation, Ranbir shared, "Lord Rama was a great archer. So, about a year and a half before we started filming, I worked with an Indian Olympian on the right technique. I was in New York for some time, and I also took some classes. The deeper part, however, was to understand the essence of who Lord Rama is. You can read as much as you want and see different interpretations, but eventually, what soul are you putting into the character? I could be playing Lord Rama, but the soul is mine. How do I change that? How do I bring a new soul?"

Notably, The star also spoke about working with action director Terry Notary, known for his work on films such as the Planet of the Apes franchise, X2 (2003), Superman Returns (2006)and others. Ranbir opened up that the workshops conducted by Terry went beyond combat training and focused on helping actors understand movement and body language.

As per the latest buzz, "Terry Notary had workshops where he taught us breathing techniques, how to walk, how to climb a tree and things like that. As actors, we are so lucky and grateful that we get to learn new skills with new movies. But Ramayana will always be special because it is the most beloved story with beloved characters. So doing all of this was awesome," Ranbir shared.

In further updates, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra, Ramayana: Part 1 is a cinematic adaptation of the Indian epic and the first instalment of a planned two-part saga. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, while Sai Pallavi essays the role of Sita and Yash portrays Ravana. The movie also stars Sunny Deol as Hanuman and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. Ramayana: Part 1 is scheduled to rollout worldwide in cinemas on November 5, 2026.

title: Ramayana box office prediction: With ₹160 crore projected start, Ranbir Kapoor-Yash film dwarfs Jawan and Animal, but no match for Dhurandhar 2, RRR
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

It may be the biggest Indian movie ever, getting the widest rollout in Indian cinema history, but alas, Ramayana is not on course to set the biggest opening for an Indian movie. In fact, if the current trends hold, it may not even break into the top five biggest openings by Indian films. Despite this, Ramayana is on course for a massive start at the ticket-window, just not as big as a movie of this scale would have warranted.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama in Ramayana. Ramayana advance booking update Advance bookings for Ramayana began globally on Dussehra, 15 days before the movie’s wide rollout. There was an early push, and overseas pre-sales took off immediately, but in India, ticket booking hit a roadblock. There was disagreement between the exhibitors and the movie’s distributors over revenue sharing, which meant that most screens did not open up bookings till just five days ago. However, Ramayana gained momentum as rollout week approached. By Wednesday morning, with less than 24 hours to go for the rollout, Ramayana had grossed ₹ 77 crore rupees in pre-sales in India for its opening weekend. The opening day alone accounted for around ₹ 33 crore rupees of this. Overseas, the movie has collected $5.6 million in advance bookings, including $1.5 million for the paid previews in North America. This takes the movie’s global advance booking to ₹ 125 crore rupees. But only about ₹ 70 crore rupees of it is for the opening day (including paid previews)

Meanwhile, Ramayana has collected ₹ 33 crore rupees in gross pre-sales for its opening day in India, with a day to go before rollout. The movie has a shot at crossing ₹ 40 crore rupees by the end of the day. This could translate into an ₹ 80 crore rupees net opening day for the movie in India. Surprisingly, the Hindi version is looking to dominate the proceedings, contributing around ₹ 55-60 crore rupees to the total net. Despite Yash ’s presence, the Kannada version does not look to open at record levels. Overseas, the North American paid previews have painted an encouraging picture for the Nitesh Tiwari movie. According to trade insiders, the movie could earn $1.6 million in paid previews and over $5 million on day 1. This would translate to a global start of ₹ 160 crore rupees gross. Some conservative estimates put the figure closer to ₹ 150 crore rupees, while some optimistic ones still hope the movie will inch toward the ₹ 200-crore rupees mark, even if that now looks increasingly difficult.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ramayana: Rise of a Legend (@ramayanamovie)

As per the latest buzz, Ramayana is getting the widest rollout ever for an Indian movie, with Sony distributing it in 70,000 screens worldwide. As a result, many trade insiders had expected the movie to have a bigger opening overseas. But so far, that does not seem to be materialising. Ramayana will likely miss a ₹ 200-crore rupees opening day and stay behind all-time record holders Pushpa 2 ( ₹ 274 crore rupees), RRR ( ₹ 223 crore rupees), and Baahubali 2 ( ₹ 214 crore rupees). Makers of Ramayana may be disappointed that it also looks set to miss Dhurandhar 2’s Bollywood record of ₹ 205 crore rupees, set earlier this year. The movie also looks set to miss the top 5, which is rounded off by Kalki 2898 AD ( ₹ 176 crore rupees). It may, however, pip KGF Chapter 2 ( ₹ 159 crore rupees).

In further updates, Ramayana will still easily soar past the opening day of the previous Ramayana adaptation, Adipurush. The Prabhas-starrer opened at ₹ 127 crore rupees in 2024. It will also beat the opening-day collections of other Bollywood blockbusters like Shah Rukh Khan’s Jawan ( ₹ 129 crore rupees) and Ranbir Kapoor’s Animal ( ₹ 116 crore rupees).

On top of that, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The first part is scheduled for worldwide rollout on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2028.

title: Aneet Padda wraps her arms around Ahaan Panday in new glimpse from her 24th birthday bash; gives ‘sister vibes’ in pic with Alia Bhatt
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Aneet Padda celebrated her 24th birthday on October 13, and glimpses from her fairytale-themed bash soon surfaced online. Nearly a month later, the star has now shared a fresh set of pictures from the celebrations. While the birthday moments offer a peek into the festivities, her pictures with Alia Bhatt and Ahaan Panday have particularly caught followers' attention.

Adding to this, Aneet Padda keeps Ahaan Panday and Alia Bhatt close in her late birthday post. Aneet Padda shares pictures from her 24th birthday bash On Wednesday, Aneet posted on Instagram to share pictures from her 24th birthday bash, which she celebrated on October 13. One of the pictures showed the star sharing a warm hug with her Saiyaara co-star and rumoured boyfriend, Ahaan Panday. The adorable moment caught followers' attention, while another picture of her hugging Alia Bhatt had followers drawing comparisons between the two and calling them sisters. Aneet also gave a glimpse of her birthday look and the princess castle-shaped cake she cut for the celebration. Director Mohit Suri was among the guests at the bash.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Aneet Padda (@aneetpadda_)

Notably, Sharing the pictures, Aneet penned an emotional note reflecting on the moments, people and relationships she misses as she grows older. She spoke about regrets, unexpressed love, calls she never made and little achievements she forgot to celebrate. The star also remembered her late grandfather, saying she finds it strange that life goes on without him and that she will now spend her birthdays without him.

As per the latest buzz, Aneet also credited her family and friends for making her birthday special. She recalled how her parents called, her sister gifted her something she had long wanted, and her childhood best friend reminded her of their days at 17. She also thanked her new friends and extended family for making her feel loved.

In further updates, She added, "And I think how blessed am I to be loved like this, to turn 24 with so many beautiful things to hold close, so many people to love and miss? Sometimes I spend so much time missing what was that I forget to look around and see how much there still is. And there is so, so much love, grief, joy, hope and magic in this little life. I really don’t know what I did to deserve it. Something about birthdays makes me cry and I’d save every tear and thank God for it on my knees."

On top of that, Aneet concluded, "I know I’m late, but also not really. It’s not exactly about a birth-day after all. Maybe it’s when everything I’ve been too busy living to feel catches up with me. All the love received, all the love lost and all the love still left to give. I want to hold everyone closer and tell them what they mean to me, and I still don’t think it’d be enough. This year I wished for all of you to be happy. I hope you are, I hope you’re all so, so happy. I hope you know I really truly do love you. I wish I could discover every way there is to show it, and I have a lifetime to try. But for now, this messy, ridiculously late post is all I could come up with. I love you. So much. Thank you, for the tears and the smiles."

Followers were thrilled to see Ahaan and Aneet's adorable picture. One of the comments read, "Best woman with the best man in the world." Another commented, "They look so adorable." Another comment read, "Loved the sixth pic." Followers also loved Aneet's picture with Alia and wrote, "you and Alia literally look like sisters."

title: Namit Malhotra confirms Ramayana Part 2 has been postponed to 2028, hints at a trilogy
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

With Ramayana : Part 1 set to hit theatres this Diwali, those who watched it at the LA premiere are now awaiting the rollout of the sequel. While the second instalment was earlier scheduled to rollout in 2027, producer Namit Malhotra has verified that it has been pushed to 2028. He has also hinted that the makers could revisit their plans and consider expanding the movie into a trilogy, depending on the audience's response to the first part.

Adding to this, Namit Malhotra confirms Ramayana Part 2 has been pushed to 2028. Namit Malhotra reveals Ramayana part 2 shifted to 2028 In an interview with E! News, Namit opened up that while Ramayana was initially envisioned as an Indian movie for a global audience, its scope evolved during production. He shared the makers have now created two master versions of the movie, with the English version featuring a separate edit and a rewritten script to make it a distinct presentation for international audiences.

Meanwhile, Explaining why Part 2 has been pushed to 2028 instead of 2027, he shared, "So the idea was now that we've got so much excitement that the world has had, we want to take a little bit more time to make sure that when we present the grand finale, we have a little bit more time to do what we did on Part One. That extra year is what I genuinely believe we need to do justice for a movie of this size. When you see part 2 coming in, that will be a whole other story. We didn't want to do a rush job or get ahead of ourselves. We want to deliver the finale in the most grand way that it deserves."

Notably, In another interview with Review Nation, Namit hinted that Ramayana could potentially become a trilogy. He opened up that the movie was initially planned as a trilogy, but the makers later decided to tell the story in two parts. However, with filming still underway, he refrained from sharing further details, adding that the team might revisit its plans depending on audience reactions and feedback.

As per the latest buzz, He added, "I feel like we may sit back on the drawing board and see if there's anything else that we want to add or subtract, depending on how the world has received it. Because, you know, while we say that, we also have two different versions of the same movie, with two different runtimes on part one itself. So, depending on which way the next round of feedback goes, I'd love to not have to make two different versions. I'm sure Nitesh would also like to stick to one version."

In further updates, Helmed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman and Yash as Ravana. title: Mita Vashisht says Shah Rukh Khan saved her life on Dil Se sets, recalls near-fatal incident
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Mita Vashishth has fond memories of working with Shah Rukh Khan , recalling his warmth and kindness on the sets of Dil Se. The two had previously worked together in The Idiot before reuniting for Mani Ratnam's movie. In a recent interaction, Mita shared several anecdotes from the shoot, including an incident in which SRK saved her life.

Adding to this, Mita Vashisht recalls time spent with Shah Rukh Khan while shooting Dil Se. Mita Vashisht recalls how Shah Rukh Khan saved her life In an interview with Screen, Mita recalled how Shah Rukh warmly welcomed her when they reunited for Dil Se. She shared he was affectionate and protective throughout the shoot, particularly during a fight sequence that never made it to the final cut of the movie. Recalling how he would place his palm behind her head whenever he pushed her against a stone wall to prevent her from getting hurt, Mita described him as a wonderful co-star. She also opened up that a small stone accidentally slipped from her hand and cut Shah Rukh's head during another part of the sequence, but he remained kind towards her.

Meanwhile, Mita then recalled another scene in which she was carrying an AK-47 and had to make Shah Rukh cross a stretch blindfolded. She shared she was positioned behind him in the line as they prepared for the shot in Dalhousie, where the weather was freezing cold. She added, "The shoes we had been given had plastic soles and we couldn’t properly feel the ground beneath our feet. Mani sir kept saying, ‘Go back, go back, go back.’ So I kept stepping backwards, very slowly, taking tiny steps. But at one point, I suddenly found myself looking up at the sky and feeling as though I was falling. I had actually reached the edge of a steep ridge and was about to fall."

Notably, She further recalled how Shah Rukh's quick reflexes saved her from falling off the ridge. She shared, "But Shah Rukh’s reflexes were extraordinary. In a split second, he grabbed the front of my jacket and pulled me back up. One moment, I was falling backwards with an AK-47, and the very next moment, his hand was grabbing my jacket and pulling me to safety. He actually saved my life that day. With the weight of the gun and the steep slope, I could have fallen all the way down, with nothing to stop me. I don’t know what might have happened, but I genuinely believe something terrible was prevented because of his fast reaction."

As per the latest buzz, Rolled out in 1998, Dil Se is a romantic thriller written and directed by Mani Ratnam. The movie stars Shah Rukh Khan, Manisha Koirala and Preity Zinta in the lead roles. It follows Amar (Shah Rukh), an All India Radio journalist who falls in love with the mysterious Meghna (Manisha), unaware of the troubled past she is hiding. Its music, composed by AR Rahman, including the iconic song Chaiyya Chaiyya, remains popular to this day. Mita Vashisht played a member of the militant group associated with Meghna. The movie also featured Raghubir Yadav, Piyush Mishra, Sabyasachi Chakrabarty and Sanjay Mishra in supporting roles.

title: Delhi ACP Manasvi Vashistha, suspended after cops' protest, is IIT graduate, former Dhankhar PSO
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

From serving as the personal security officer (PSO) to former Vice-President Jagdeep Dhankhar to being at the centre of a police protest over his transfer, suspended Delhi Police Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Manasvi Vashistha has had a varied career spanning central armed police forces and several assignments in the national capital.

Adding to this, Security personnel stand guard outside the Delhi Police Headquarters (PHQ) as protesting officers from Shahdara district assemble to demand the rollback of transfer orders for ACP Manasvi Vashistha and SHO Inspector Arun Kumar, in New Delhi, Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. (PTI) A 2019-batch officer of the Delhi, Andaman and Nicobar Islands Police Service (DANIPS), Vashistha was suspended by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) on November 2, hours after more than 100 police personnel, including women officers, gathered outside the Police Headquarters to protest against his transfer and that of Shahdara station house officer (SHO) Inspector Arun Kumar.

Meanwhile, Vashistha had earlier served as the PSO to Dhankhar until the latter resigned as Vice-President in 2025. He was also part of the Delhi Police Security Unit and was involved in security arrangements for the AI Summit and the visit of Russian President Vladimir Putin, according to sources.

Notably, An engineering graduate from the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Kharagpur, Vashistha joined the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) in 2016. He served with the force for around four years, with postings in Jammu and Kashmir and Bihar, before joining DANIPS as part of the 2019-20 batch.
As per the latest buzz, Born and brought up in Jaipur, Vashistha comes from a family of doctors. He studied mechanical engineering at IIT Kharagpur between 2009 and 2013.

In further updates, Following his initial training and posting in Delhi, he was transferred to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in 2022, where he served as Deputy Superintendent of Police in Diglipur and Havelock. He returned to Delhi in December 2024 and subsequently held various assignments in the Delhi Police.

On top of that, In December 2025, he was posted as ACP, Gandhi Nagar, where he served for around three months. He was later assigned to the Delhi Police Security Unit before being posted again as ACP, Gandhi Nagar, in March 2026.

The sequence of events leading to Vashistha's suspension started on October 23, when an advocate, Lalit Bansal, suffered a serious head injury during a confrontation between lawyers and police personnel at Shahdara police station over a parking issue.
