title: Salman Khan sings Teri Sexy Beauty, casually drops new Maatrubhumi song at 5 in the morning, fans confused by hip love song in tragic war drama
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

In this age of algorithmic tracking and maximising campaign traction, things like song launches are carefully planned and orchestrated. The drop times are carefully planned and discussed to get more eyeballs. Not for Salman Khan , though. On Wednesday morning, the Bollywood superstar took to social media and, without prior notice, shared a video of his new song, Teri Sexy Beauty. And all this, at 5 AM, before half the country had even woken up.

Adding to this, Salman Khan in the music video of Maatrubhumi song Teri Sexy Beauty. Salman Khan croons Teri Sexy Beauty On Wednesday, Salman shared a teaser of the song on Instagram around 5 AM. In the caption, the star used wordplay about catching an early-morning flight as a cheeky reference to the song’s lyrics. “Departure time 5:12 am…. Flight on time, 2 pegs down taking off with my sexy beauty… pata nahi kahaan mai land karoon (don’t know where I will land),” Salman wrote, adding the hashtag: #TeriSexyBeauty Out Now. The star referred followers to his Instagram bio for the link to the full song on YouTube.

Meanwhile, The song, part of Salman’s soon-to-release movie Maatrubhumi , has been composed by Himesh Reshammiya and sung by Salman and Muskaan, with Sajid Khan providing additional vocals. Sajid has also written the song. The music video features Salman alongside the movie’s female lead, Chitrangada Singh .
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Salman Khan (@beingsalmankhan)

As per the latest buzz, The YouTube description of the song read: “Love, masti and a little madness take centre stage in Teri Sexy Beauty, this fun-filled track brings a refreshing dose of romance, playful chemistry and carefree moments, celebrating the lighter side of love.” However, many followers were amused and confused as to how this hip, irreverent song fits in Maatrubhumi, a tragic war drama. “Fun song but what is it doing in that movie,” asked one confused fan.

In further updates, Others were confused about the song dropping at 5 in the morning. One fan wrote, “Did he post it by mistake or is it just Salman being Salman?” Another comment read, “Salman bhai matches my sleep cycle.”

On top of that, Produced by Salma Khan under the banner of Salman Khan Films, Maatrubhumi: May War Rest In Peace is directed by Apoorva Lakhia and also stars Chitrangada Singh in a pivotal role. The movie was earlier titled Battle of Galwan before being renamed earlier this year. Originally based on the 2020 Galwan Valley clash between Indian and Chinese troops, the movie as per reports dropped all references to China after reshoots.

Originally slated for rollout in April this year, the movie was later postponed. The makers debunked reports that claimed the movie was shelved earlier this year. No official rollout date has been revealed since its postponement.

title: Shraddha Kapoor says she didn't sign any film after Stree 2's success despite being offered good money in wait for ‘perfect story’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Shraddha Kapoor has opened up about a career decision she made after the massive success of Stree 2 . The star, who is now gearing up for her next movie, Eetha, of late held an Instagram Q&A session, where she shared advice about navigating careers in the best way possible. Responding to the question, she reflected on a choice that required patience and conviction.

Adding to this, Shraddha Kapoor talks about not signing any movie after Stree 2. (Instagram) Shraddha Kapoor on not signing any movie after Stree 2 On Tuesday, a fan asked Shraddha for advice for young girls on navigating their careers. Responding to the question, the star shared, "I would share about myself. After Stree 2, I was offered a lot of films and money as well, but I had decided that until I get that perfect story, I won't sign anything. My heart shared that I will have to keep that patience, and I did that."
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Onpost (@onpost.in)

Notably, She added, "Of course it gets difficult to wait for something you really want, but right now I feel proud that I took the decision to wait. So I would say listen to that voice in your heart; sometimes it becomes difficult, but it's totally worth it."

As per the latest buzz, Stree 2 emerged as one of the biggest blockbusters of 2024, taking the success of Maddock Films' horror-comedy universe to new heights. Directed by Amar Kaushik, the movie starred Shraddha Kapoor and Rajkummar Rao in the lead roles, alongside Pankaj Tripathi, Aparshakti Khurana and Abhishek Banerjee. The movie registered a massive opening, collecting around ₹ 55 crore rupees on its first day, including paid previews, and maintained a strong run in the following weeks. It crossed the ₹ 500 crore rupees mark worldwide within days of its rollout.

In further updates, Apart from the cast's performances, the movie also received praise for its storyline and comedy. Akshay Kumar's surprise cameo became another major talking point. The movie went on to collect ₹ 857 crore rupees worldwide, becoming the highest-grossing horror-comedy movie in Indian cinema.

On top of that, Shraddha is now awaiting the rollout of Eetha. Directed by Laxman Utekar, who has also co-produced it with Dinesh Vijan and Karishma Sharma under the banners of Maddock Films and Kathputli Creations, the movie stars Shraddha in the titular role of Lavani artist Vithabai Bhau Mang Narayangaonkar. The cast also includes Randeep Hooda, Mohammed Zeeshan Ayyub, Siddharth Jadhav, Ishtiyak Khan and Anant Joshi.

The movie draws inspiration from incidents documented in the Marathi book Tamasha: Vithabaichya Ayushyacha. Talking about playing the titular character, Shraddha shared, "It’s a story about a woman whose art, courage and individuality make her unforgettable. The more Laxman sir told me about the character, the more I felt connected to her world. Playing this role has been an incredibly exciting experience, and I am thrilled for audiences to discover her journey on the big screen. This is also my grand reunion with Maddock Films after we made magic with Stree and Stree 2, which is thrilling to say the least. The entire team has put in so much hard work, and I cannot wait for audiences to experience the world of Eetha.”

title: Ramayana producer Namit Malhotra admits many in India ask why are they making another adaptation, compares film to Avatar, The Odyssey
body: Here's the latest update from the Hollywood/Marvel world:

Ramayana producer Namit Malhotra has admitted that many in India are wondering what the need is for another adaptation of the epic. The filmmaker has talked about the movie's scale and ambition, saying it tells its story on a scale never seen before.

Adding to this, Namit Malhotra is the producer of Nitesh Tiwari's epic two-part adaptation of Ramayana. Namit Malhotra on Ramayana's scale Directed by Nitesh Tiwari , Ramayana is the biggest Indian movie in terms of scale and budget. After its world premiere in Los Angeles last week, Ramayana held a special screening in Mumbai on Tuesday, attended by the cast and crew, as well as members of the movie fraternity.

Meanwhile, There, Namit spoke to news agency PTI about what he hopes to achieve with the movie. "In India, there are a lot of questions like, 'Why are they making the Ramayana when there have been so many Ramayanas? We already know the story.' And I'm like, 'Listen, we're making it because we want to show you the version of this story that you've never seen.' No television show, no street play, no Ram Leela has ever shown you the Ramayana on this scale and with this spectacle that we are making...Much like an Avatar or an Avengers movie or think about Spider-Man or The Odyssey. We're putting Ramayana right up there next to all of those spectacles," Namit Malhotra told PTI.

Notably, Ramayana, made on a reported budget of ₹ 4000 crore rupees, is one of the most expensive movie productions in the world, not just in India. With VFX from eight-time Oscar-winning studio DNEG, it is being marketed as India's first movie equivalent of Hollywood blockbusters. For its global rollout, the makers have partnered with Sony Pictures, which is giving it the widest rollout for any Indian movie - in 70,000 screens.

As per the latest buzz, Talking about the movie's global ambitions, Namit added, “If you think about the West, they are the most potent audience for anything that's got a grand epic spectacle. And that's just not how Indian films have been made. So while India makes terrific Indian movies, whether it is 'Baahubali', 'Dhurandhar', or any of the big, super-duper hit films, they are not spectacles the way Hollywood thinks of spectacles. We are first trying to narrow that gap down and saying, 'If you can do it, we can do it too.' There's no reason for us to have any discrepancy. So, every person in Hollywood should acknowledge that India can also do something as good, if not bigger, than what they do.”

In further updates, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit's Prime Focus and Yash's Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, and Yash as Ravana. The first part is scheduled for worldwide rollout on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2027. The films will rollout in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam across India.

On top of that, Sony Pictures will handle global distribution, excluding India, while Dharma Productions will distribute the movie in the Hindi-speaking market. The movie is also planned for a worldwide IMAX rollout.

title: Panchayat's Chandan Roy recalls how a boy asking for selfie in his village made him realise the show was a hit
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Chandan Roy moved to Mumbai after leaving his full-time journalism job to pursue his dream of becoming an star. After spending a year taking up small television roles, he got his big break with the web series Panchayat , which premiered in 2020. Its rollout coincided with the Covid-19 pandemic, which helped the show reach a wider audience and become one of the most popular show on OTT.

Adding to this, Chandan Roy plays the role of Vikas in Panchayat. In an exclusive interaction with Hindustan Times, Chandan spoke about the exact moment he realised Panchayat had become a hit and that his life was about to change. He also opened up about the fear of being typecast and what he learnt from sharing screen space with veteran star Raghubir Yadav.

Meanwhile, When Panchayat rolled out, Covid was going on. I had gone back to my village. I was holding a sack of flour behind my uncle, who was driving his bike. There, a guy came running up to me. He stopped us and shared, "Bhaiya, I just watched your show Panchayat; you did such great work in it." I thought Panchayat would only be watched in big cities like Mumbai and Delhi, but when this kid in a small town like Mahnar came running to me, I felt that something big had happened because Panchayat had reached all the way here. My uncle was also astonished. That kid took a selfie with me, and then I was stopped by another person during that ride.

Notably, Initially, when you don't have work and money, and you have to run your kitchen, you don't pay attention to what the character is, whether you even speak in the entire movie or if you have a proper scene. But when you get recognition, you can choose whether you want to do a character or not. So, now I am at a stage where I can select or reject a character according to my preference. Now, I tend to avoid characters that I feel will typecast me. For example, I really dislike this character type – 'Hero ka dost'. I feel even if he is the hero's friend, he should have a proper background story.

As per the latest buzz, I never do this because I think my work should be very original, and I should not copy another star's traits. However, when you work with very senior artists, you definitely observe how they approach a character, how they behave on camera, or how they interact with people on set. So, no doubt, I learn all those things. For instance, I find Raghubir sir's method very beautiful: even today, he prepares with his script as if he's appearing for a board exam. He holds a pencil in his hand, checking, listening and reading every line over and over again. Whenever you go to his room, his script is open on his bed, even at this age and after doing so much work.

In further updates, Chandan stars in short-movie Aakhri Ride , which is presented by Anurag Kashyap and Vasan Bala. It is written and directed by Yashoda Parthasarthy and Vijesh Rajan and produced by Ranjan Singh, Vishesh Agrawal, Rajan EPK and Anurag. It is streaming on the youtube channel Oh Short Flips.

title: Ranbir Kapoor weighs in on AI's impact on filmmaking, says it can never replace human touch
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ranbir Kapoor and Yash are currently busy promoting their much-awaited movie, Ramayana . Since the rollout of its teaser, the movie's VFX and grand world-building have been topics of discussion, with followers weighing in on both its positive and negative aspects. Amid the debate, Ranbir and Yash of late discussed the use of AI in filmmaking and shared why they believe that while the technology can aid the process, it can never replace the performing arts.

Adding to this, Star Ranbir Kapoor is portraying Ram in the movie Ramayana ‘AI can be used to better filmmaking’ In conversation with BBC News about the impact of AI on films, Ranbir shared, "Art is always more personal when there is a human touch to it. I think AI like VFX or camera lenses, can be used as a tool to better your filmmaking. But from the medium we come from – of storytelling, of art, of performing art -- and I don’t think AI can ever replace that."

Meanwhile, Yash also weighed in on the debate and shared, "We have to be responsible enough to understand that humans are involved in it, and we need to be very cautious in where all we apply this technology. We are survivors. We will come up with some idea or we will create something which even a machine would have to struggle with."

Notably, In another interaction, Ranbir addressed the criticism that Ramayana has been receiving over aspects such as its VFX and music. Speaking at an India International Movement to Unite Nations (IIMUN) event, Ranbir admitted that he remains unbothered by the criticism because his intentions are clear.

title: Arunachal gets new DGP as IPS officer Rajesh Kumar takes charge amid Siang dam protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Union home ministry on Tuesday appointed 1995-batch IPS officer Rajesh Kumar as the new director general of police (DGP) of Arunachal Pradesh, a day after he was prematurely repatriated from the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) to his parent cadre.

Adding to this, The change comes at a time when a section of the tribal community in Arunachal Pradesh has been protesting against the proposed 11,200-megawatt multipurpose hydroelectric project on the Siang River, considered one of India’s largest. (HT File Photo) The appointments committee of the Cabinet on Monday cleared the Union home ministry’s proposal to repatriate Kumar prematurely to his parent AGMUT cadre with “immediate effect” from the CRPF, where he was serving as Special DG.

Meanwhile, In an order issued on Wednesday, the home ministry posted Kumar as the new DGP of the border state, succeeding the incumbent and his batchmate, Shiv Darshan Singh Jamwal, who has been transferred to Delhi.

Notably, The change comes at a time when a section of the tribal community in Arunachal Pradesh has been protesting against the proposed 11,200-megawatt multipurpose hydroelectric project on the Siang River, considered one of India’s largest.

As per the latest buzz, The project, envisioned as one of India’s largest hydropower initiatives, has faced sustained opposition from sections of the indigenous Adi community, particularly residents of the proposed project-affected areas.

In further updates, The opposition stems primarily from apprehensions over the submergence of ancestral villages, displacement, loss of agricultural land and forests, and the possible disruption of the community’s traditional way of life.

On top of that, The project has also assumed strategic significance for the Centre, which views it as important in the context of China’s proposed massive hydropower project on the Yarlung Tsangpo River in Tibet, which enters India as the Siang.

On Monday, Arunachal chief minister Pema Kandu had shared in a note that no decision has been taken without consent on construction of the dam will while appealing to protests to withdraw their 36-hour shutdown call in Upper Siang region.

title: Bombay High Court asks BMC to restore Dia Mirza’s Diwali video: “India is a secular country”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

A division bench comprising Justice Girish Kulkarni and Justice Dr Neela Gokhale expressed displeasure over the row and the remarks made against Mirza. The court shared it was “disturbed by the stray comments made by some politicians” and reminded those raising objections that “India is a Secular country.”

Adding to this, The video was recorded by Mirza at the BMC’s request as part of an awareness campaign following the court’s directions on firecrackers and air pollution. The civic body had also roped in other public figures to spread awareness about celebrating Diwali while reducing air and noise pollution.
Meanwhile, During the hearing, the bench questioned the objections to Mirza’s participation in the campaign based on her religion.

Notably, “A festival is for everyone to celebrate... No individual can be isolated from celebrating any festival in this country... how can you object to someone's participation just because that person is from some other religion? Aren't we a secular country,” the judges observed.
As per the latest buzz, The court also noted that Mirza had acted in accordance with its directions and shared that the approach of some corporators and politicians was incorrect.
In further updates, “She acted as per the directions of the court,” the bench shared, adding that the issue should not be given “any other angle.”
On top of that, Justice Gokhale further stressed that the matter was about the environment and public health.
“Everyone is breathing the same air, be it anyone,” she observed, adding, “It's not that barring firecrackers is taking away your right to celebrate the festival.”

title: Manoj Bajpayee, Boman Irani and Divya Dutta’s Last Man in Tower to premiere on Hindi Zee 5 on November 6
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The movie is set in a Mumbai housing society where redevelopment becomes the source of conflict among residents. Bajpayee plays Yogesh Mishra, a retired physics teacher who refuses to vacate his apartment despite the lucrative offer being accepted by the rest of the society.

Adding to this, As Yogesh stands against the redevelopment plan, his decision puts him at odds with neighbours and people he once considered friends. The story explores the personal consequences of his decision while looking at the different reasons that drive the residents to support the redevelopment.

Meanwhile, Divya Dutta plays Sangita Puri, a housewife whose desire for a better life for her special-needs son puts her in conflict with Yogesh. Boman Irani plays developer Dharmen Shah, who is attempting to move the redevelopment project forward.
Notably, Speaking about his character, Manoj Bajpayee shared that Yogesh's ambiguity was one of the reasons he was drawn to the movie.

As per the latest buzz, “What drew me to Last Man in Tower was the complexity of Yogesh Mishra. He is a man who stands firmly by his beliefs, yet the story leaves you questioning whether he is right or wrong. As an star, I found that ambiguity fascinating because it allowed me to explore the many layers of a character who is stubborn, vulnerable and deeply attached to his home and the memories it holds,” he shared.

In further updates, The star also connected the movie's redevelopment conflict to Mumbai's changing landscape. “In a city like Mumbai, where redevelopment has become part of everyday life and familiar buildings are constantly making way for new ones, the movie looks at the human side of this change - what it means for families, the memories they leave behind and the uncertainty or excitement of starting afresh,” Bajpayee added.

On top of that, Divya Dutta shared she was drawn to the movie because of the way it approaches the motivations of its characters. “What drew me to Last Man in Tower was the way it explores human behaviour and the choices people make without viewing them through a simple lens of right and wrong. Everyone has their own circumstances, aspirations and reasons for acting the way they do, which makes the conflict deeply relatable,” she shared.

Talking about the response to her character, Dutta added, “While audiences may not have agreed with her aggression, they understood where she was coming from and what shaped her choices. As an star, knowing that people could connect with her, even when they didn’t necessarily agree with her, is incredibly rewarding.”

title: Shah Rukh Khan thanks Ed Sheeran for King song Tu Mil Jaaye; singer reveals how their Mannat meeting for Sapphire music video led to Bollywood collab
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

British popstar Ed Sheeran 's first Bollywood song happened almost by chance, thanks to a meeting at Shah Rukh Khan 's home in Mumbai. The singer has now shared how a visit to Mannat to shoot a cameo for his music video eventually brought him together with composers Sachin-Jigar and led to Tu Mil Jaaye, his first song for a Hindi movie, which also stars Deepika Padukone . The track, which also features Arijit Singh, is part of SRK's soon-to-release movie King.

Adding to this, Ed Sheeran reveals Shah Rukh Khan's role in his Bollywood debut, says he recorded King song after meeting Sachin-Jigar. Ed Sheeran reveals how the collaboration came to be Ed shared the story on Instagram along with a video of himself recording his vocals for the song. He also spoke about how his friendship with Shah Rukh grew over the years and recalled the star's wish to have him sing for one of his films. “When I first met Shah Rukh, he shared I must make a song to be in his next movie and also be my first Bollywood song,” he shared. “We've got to know each other over the years and I love him.”

Meanwhile, The idea finally took shape during Ed's last visit to India. He had dropped by Mannat to movie a cameo for Sapphire, his 2025 song with Arijit Singh. Shah Rukh introduced him to Sachin-Jigar during the visit, and things moved quickly from there. Sheeran opened up that he wrote and recorded his portion of Tu Mil Jaaye that very night. “Last time I was in India I went to his house to get him to shoot a cameo in the Sapphire music video for me and @arijitsingh,” he wrote. “He introduced me to @sachinjigar that day and I wrote and recorded my verse for Tu Mil Jaaye for his movie King that night.”

Notably, View this post on Instagram The singer was equally happy about having Arijit Singh on the track, especially since the two had already worked together on Sapphire. “I love that Arijit is singing on it with me too, all my favourite people on one project. King is out December 24th and Tu Mil Jaaye is out everywhere now x,” he concluded.

As per the latest buzz, Shah Rukh also shared Ed's video on his Instagram Stories and thanked him for being part of the movie. The star gave a special mention to the Hindi portions of the song, writing, “Can't thank u enough my friend for doing the song, especially the Hindi bits. Love u @teddyphotos.”

In further updates, Tu Mil Jaaye was rolled out on November 2, coinciding with Shah Rukh's 61st birthday. Featuring Ed and Arijit, the song also includes an English rap by the British singer. It quickly caught viewers' attention, crossing 60 million views across platforms within its first 24 hours.

On top of that, The song registered 36.3 million views and more than 430,000 likes on YouTube in a single day. With that, it became the most-watched song from an Indian movie on the platform in 24 hours. It also overtook Jawan's Zinda Banda, which had previously held the record with 34.6 million views.

King brings him back in a different avatar, with a sizeable cast including Suhana Khan, Abhishek Bachchan, Jackie Shroff, Arshad Warsi and Raghav Juyal, among others. Rani Mukerji, Deepika Padukone and Kareena Kapoor Khan are also set to make special appearances.

title: Last Man in Tower trailer: Manoj Bajpayee takes on an entire housing society in this gripping redevelopment drama
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Imagine standing your ground to protect your home, only to have your entire neighbourhood turn against you. That's the dilemma at the heart of Last Man in Tower, featuring Manoj Bajpayee , Divya Dutta and Boman Irani . Based on the 2011 bestselling novel of the same name by Booker Prize-winning author Aravind Adiga, the movie is directed by Ben Rekhi and backed by Rana Daggubati's Spirit Media.

Adding to this, Last Man in Tower trailer: Manoj Bajpayee's fight to save his home puts him against Divya Dutta and Boman Irani. Trailer breakdown of Last Man in Tower The trailer was unveiled on November 3 in which Manoj Bajpayee plays Yogesh Mishra, a retired physics teacher who refuses to give up his Mumbai apartment even after the rest of his housing society agrees to redevelopment. While his neighbours see the offer as a chance to move into better homes and improve their lives, Yogesh isn't ready to walk away from a place filled with years of memories. For him, leaving the apartment means leaving behind a life he has built over the years.

Meanwhile, His stand brings him up against Sangita Puri (Divya Dutta), a housewife who sees the redevelopment as a chance to secure a better future for her special-needs son. She has her own reasons for wanting the deal to go through, and Yogesh's refusal only adds to her frustration. What starts as a disagreement over a building soon becomes a deeply personal clash between two people who see their futures very differently.

Notably, The situation gets more complicated with developer Dharmen Shah (Boman Irani) pushing to take the project forward. As the dispute drags on, the once-friendly housing society begins to change. Neighbours who have spent years living alongside each other find themselves on opposite sides, and Yogesh is gradually pushed away by the very community he is trying to hold on to.

As per the latest buzz, Manoj Bajpayee, who plays Yogesh Mishra, shared it was the character's conflicting nature that made him take up the role. Talking about what appealed to him, he shared, “What drew me to Last Man in Tower was the complexity of Yogesh Mishra. He is a man who stands firmly by his beliefs, yet the story leaves you questioning whether he is right or wrong. As an star, I found that ambiguity fascinating because it allowed me to explore the many layers of a character who is stubborn, vulnerable and deeply attached to his home and the memories it holds. In a city like Mumbai, where redevelopment has become part of everyday life and familiar buildings are constantly making way for new ones, the movie looks at the human side of this change - what it means for families, the memories they leave behind and the uncertainty or excitement of starting afresh”.

In further updates, Divya Dutta, meanwhile, spoke about how the movie looks at people and their choices without judging them. She was particularly pleased that audiences could understand Sangita's motivations, even if they did not agree with her behaviour. She shared, “What drew me to Last Man in Tower was the way it explores human behaviour and the choices people make without viewing them through a simple lens of right and wrong. Everyone has their own circumstances, aspirations and reasons for acting the way they do, which makes the conflict deeply relatable. I’m especially happy with the response to my role. While audiences may not have agreed with her aggression, they understood where she was coming from and what shaped her choices. As an star, knowing that people could connect with her, even when they didn’t necessarily agree with her, is incredibly rewarding.”
On top of that, Director Ben Rekhi spoke about the experience of bringing the movie to the screen, crediting the team behind it, including producer Rana Daggubati and screenwriter Sooni Taraporevala.

He shared, “It’s been a deeply fulfilling experience bringing Last Man in Tower to life with an incredible team top to bottom, from Rana Daggubati producing, to Sooni Taraporevala scripting, all based on Aravind Adiga’s incredible book. The most rewarding part has been witnessing the power of Manoj and Boman - two giants of cinema - working together for the first time in this movie. Last Man in Tower is an urgent story about holding onto community and family through turbulent times, a story that has only become more relevant with time”.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The sight of Amitabh Bachchan greeting followers from behind bulletproof glass outside his Juhu home has left the movie industry worried. The star has been stepping out every Sunday for decades to meet the people who gather outside Jalsa, but his November 1 appearance was unlike anything followers had seen before. At 84, Bachchan needed a layer of bulletproof glass between himself and the people who had come to see him. The incident has now become part of a larger security concern raised by the All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA), which has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi seeking urgent protection for Bollywood personalities.

Adding to this, From Salman Khan to Tiger Shroff: AICWA flags gang threats, seeks PM Modi's intervention for Bollywood. What AICWA has told PM Modi In a letter dated November 3, 2026, AICWA president Suresh Shyam Lal Gupta has asked the Prime Minister to intervene and ensure the safety of actors, filmmakers and their families. The association has pointed to a series of shootings, attacks and extortion threats involving members of the movie industry, arguing that the situation can no longer be taken lightly.

Meanwhile, The letter also recalled Bachchan's Sunday tradition, which draws followers from across India and even overseas. His son, Abhishek Bachchan, was present beside him during the recent appearance. Expressing concern over what the star had to do simply to meet his followers, the association wrote, “For more than four decades he has met his followers there every Sunday, and people from across India and abroad come just to see him. At the age of 84, he never imagined he would have to protect himself like this in his own city. His son Abhishek Bachchan, who rarely comes out, stood beside him to protect his father.”

Notably, The association shared the image had sent a troubling message about the safety of people in the industry. It added, “People have heard of bulletproof cars. Never before had they seen a superstar step out of his home behind bulletproof glass just to meet the people who love him. This image will be remembered in the history of Indian cinema, and the whole industry was shaken by it.”

As per the latest buzz, The AICWA has cited several incidents to explain why it believes security around the movie industry needs to be strengthened. These include the murder of Baba Siddique in Bandra, the firing outside Salman Khan 's residence, the knife attack on Saif Ali Khan at his home and the firing outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty's Juhu residence.

In further updates, The letter also mentions repeated firing incidents targeting comedian Kapil Sharma's cafe in Canada and the recent shooting involving Tiger Shroff in Juhu. The association is particularly concerned about the latter incident, which it says took place in a crowded part of Mumbai, with several people present.

On top of that, Pointing to the seriousness of the attack, the letter shared, “Tiger Shroff was fired upon in Juhu, one of Mumbai's most prominent VIP areas, in the presence of a large crowd. Two persons were hit by bullets... Tiger Shroff has no known row and no known enmity with anyone. He was targeted in broad daylight for one reason: to spread terror.”

The association believes there is a larger pattern behind these incidents, with extortion being a possible motive. According to the letter, gangsters are targeting Bollywood because of its visibility and global reach, using threats against well-known personalities to demand money and make themselves known. It also refers to reports that Tusshar Kapoor was targeted with an extortion demand of ₹ 5 crore rupees.

title: Ranbir Kapoor brushes off Ramayana criticism, says what matters is people who value his intentions
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ranbir Kapoor and Yash -starrer Ramayana is among the most anticipated films of the year. However, ever since the teaser was rolled out, several aspects of the movie, including its music and VFX, have faced criticism online. During a recent IIMUN (India International Movement to Unite Nations) event, Ranbir addressed the criticism surrounding the movie and shared why he chooses not to be bothered by online trolling.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor's Ramayana will rollout in theatres on November 5. 'Don't be bothered by what people are saying' Speaking about online trolling, Ranbir shared, “What's relevant today is this beauty of trolling online. It goes back to the good old song ‘Kuchh to log kahenge, logon ka kaam hai kehna (People will say something, it's their job to say something or the other)'. I think that's a great philosophy to actually follow in life. Don't be bothered by what people are saying. What matters is the people who matter, the people who care for your work, your intention, and your kindness. That's what matters the most,” shared the star.

Meanwhile, Director Nitesh Tiwari also shared his thoughts on the criticism and shared that the team had given its best to the movie. “If your conscience is clear, and if our effort was hundred per cent, then what else do you need?” he shared.

Notably, Earlier, Yash had made headlines after requesting followers to support Ramayana and avoid nitpicking its VFX. At a grand pre-rollout event in Hyderabad in October, the star lauded producer Namit Malhotra, Global CEO of DNEG (Double Negative), for backing the ambitious project and taking Indian cinema to a global platform.

As per the latest buzz, He shared, “Namit has gambled his reputation and money to put this movie on a global platform. Please don't try to find small faults in the VFX, this and that. It will never happen again if we lose people like him now. It will take more years; we will go back in time. Let's see the movie with an open mind. He has always taken every feedback and criticism and tried to do it better. I request you from my side, for once, if you like the movie, let's come together and show the world.”

In further updates, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. The movie also features Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman and Ravi Dubey as Lakshman. Produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, the ambitious two-part saga is being made on a budget of around ₹ 4,000 crore rupees. The first instalment is scheduled to rollout in theatres on November 5, while the second part is expected to arrive in 2027.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Rahul Bose REACTS to Kay Kay Menon’s hate-spewing character in Shaurya being hailed as a HERO: “The world will change, but I won’t”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood Hungama exclusively spoke to Rahul Bose, who also starred in Shaurya as an Army defence lawyer who ultimately brings Brigadier Rudra Pratap Singh to justice. When asked how he feels about Kay Kay Menon's character being perceived as a hero by a section of the audience, the star explained, “With changing times, the context changes and values change. But my core values have never changed and will never change. There’s no question of feeling. The idea is that bas apna santulan rakho , don’t change your basic values of non-violence and love, etc. The world will change one way and then the world will change another way, but I won’t. For instance, one day we are told that tomatoes are good for your health. The next day, we are told to avoid tomatoes as they're unhealthy. A day later, we are asked to avoid tomatoes altogether!”

Adding to this, Rahul continued, “As far as I am concerned, in these days and times, when things seem to have changed so radically, it’s important to know yourself completely, hold on to that reality and let everything else change. But the reality is that some things about you just need to remain the same. So, I have not moved one inch from who I was and what I am. And I’ll stay that way.”

Meanwhile, Rahul Bose directed Everybody Says I'm Fine (2001) and Poorna (2017). Does he have plans to helm one more movie? Rahul verified, “Yes. I am writing an action movie actually! It’s a clever movie with lot of humour, though it’s not of the Udta Teer variety. It is something 100% India has not seen before. But it’s very massy.”

title: From running banquet chains to Bollywood debut at 48: Rupinder Walia on journey to Udta Teer, becoming a star in his kids' eyes | HT Exclusive
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

For Rupinder Walia, acting was always the dream, but financial security was a priority too. While he pursued his passion for theatre from the age of 20, he simultaneously built a successful banquet and event management business, knowing how uncertain a career in Bollywood could be. Nearly three decades later, at 48, he finally made his big-screen debut with Udta Teer . Playing Sodhi, a Haryanvi-speaking Sikh cop in Ayushmann Khurrana 's team, Rupinder brings a generous dose of humour to the movie, making his character one of its most entertaining elements.

Adding to this, Rupinder Walia made his Bollywood debut with Udta Teer at 48. In an exclusive interview with Hindustan Times, Rupinder opened up about his journey from theatre to films, how he landed his role in Udta Teer, why he never wanted to move to Mumbai to struggle for work, and his kids' reaction to the movie.

Meanwhile, Rupinder's association with acting goes back to when he was 20. He trained at the Shri Ram Centre of Art and Culture in Delhi, where he completed a two-year diploma in acting, and continued performing in theatre for several years. However, he also had a business to run. He shared, “I have a chain of banquets and an event management company through which I organise several government and private events. I have my banquet chain in Haryana and Northern India, and we organise big fat weddings.”

Notably, Despite being passionate about acting, Rupinder was always clear that he wanted financial independence before entering the movie industry. “I come from a middle-class family. This business I have built over time, working since I was 20. I was aware that this movie line is very uncertain. Today, OTT platforms have taken over, and we see different kinds of cinema being made, but when I was young, the industry was ruled by stardom and even getting character roles was difficult,” he shared.

As per the latest buzz, Rupinder added that he was never interested in television and did not want to move to Mumbai without having a financial cushion. “I always wanted to be financially stable because I didn't want to come to Mumbai and struggle. So I used to satisfy my desire to act by performing in theatre plays and running my business alongside. Today, by God's grace, I don't have to accept a role I am not comfortable with just for financial reasons. I won't do any role for money. Everyone should maintain their financial stability.”
In further updates, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Rupinder walia (@rupinderwaliaofficial)

On top of that, He also believes that the emergence of OTT platforms and changes in the casting process have made things easier for aspiring actors. “Now there are OTT platforms as well, and casting directors call you right here in Delhi. There is no need to go to Mumbai. You can just shoot your audition on your phone and send it. If they like it, they will call you. I think the door-to-door struggle has ended. For an star, earlier there were embarrassing moments of standing in a queue outside a casting director's office. Coming from a middle-class family, I sometimes found it very awkward. But that has also ended now. I can send my audition from the comfort of my home,” he shared.

Rupinder credits his long association with theatre for helping him land the role in Udta Teer. “Akash Kaushik and I were in the same theatre group at one point, so we knew each other. He had seen me speaking Haryanvi in several plays, so my introduction with him goes back years. He had something in mind, and one day, surprisingly, he came to my house and shared, 'I am doing a movie with you. Get ready, I am taking you beyond theatre to the big cinema.' Then the casting team auditioned me,” he revealed.

In the video, producer Namit Malhotra opened up that Hans agreed to come on board Ramayana without even looking at the movie's complete pitch deck.

Adding to this, AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer have collaborated for the first time for Ramayana. How Hans agreed to compose music for Ramayana The video shows Rahman and Hans working together on the movie's music, with musicians from both India and the West coming together to create a symphony. Speaking about the movie's music, Hans shared, "Together we are setting off on a journey that has never been done before, to be able to make music that is thousands of years old about the Gods and traditions that make India so important for us in the West."

Meanwhile, Ramayana producer Namit Malhotra spoke about how Hans agreed to compose music for the movie without even seeing its pitch deck. He shared, "I met Hans in New York. I had made my entire pitch deck and all the world-building. I ran six or seven slides, and he shared, 'Namit, it is okay. I don't need to see it.'" Namit went on to talk about how musicians from India and the West came together for the project.

Notably, Rahman also spoke about how he and Hans divided the work. While he focused on certain songs and themes, Hans worked on others, eventually bringing the two together. He explained that the process involved constant exchanges between them as they worked towards finding what best suited the movie.
As per the latest buzz, In conversation with Hindustan Times in a recent interaction, Rahman had opened up about his experience of working with Hans Zimmer on the movie, calling it a blessing.

In further updates, He shared, “Usually I prefer solo work because I'm bad at being precious about my work. I'd just say, 'You do everything and I'll watch!' But in this case, him coming onto the project is such a blessing because it changes the narrative. If someone in New Zealand or Europe sees Hans Zimmer's name, they will watch. If they just see Indian names, they might think it's just another Indian movie, but they'll be curious to see what he has done collaborating on this. It's a great move by the producer.”
On top of that, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana will rollout in theatres on November 5.

title: King's Tu Mil Jaaye becomes most-watched Indian film song in 24 hours with 36 million views; beats Jawan's Zinda Banda, Adipurush's Jai Shri Ram
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Shah Rukh Khan 's birthday celebrations got even bigger, thanks to his soon-to-release movie King. The first song from the movie, Tu Mil Jaaye , was rolled out on November 2, on the occasion of the superstar's 61st birthday, and has wasted no time making headlines. The romantic track, which features the special appearance of Deepika Padukone , has clocked record views in its first 24 hours, becoming the most-watched song from an Indian movie in a single day.

Adding to this, King song Tu Mil Jaaye creates history! Shah Rukh Khan beats his own Jawan record with Deepika Padukone. Tu Mil Jaaye beats Zinda Banda, Ram Siya Ram The song has crossed 60 million views across platforms in just a day. Its YouTube numbers alone total 36.3 million views and more than 430,000 likes. This puts it ahead of some of the biggest Indian movie songs rolled out in recent years.

Meanwhile, Interestingly, the previous record belonged to Shah Rukh himself. Zinda Banda, from his 2023 movie Jawan, had garnered 34.6 million views on YouTube in its first 24 hours. Tu Mil Jaaye has now comfortably moved past that figure. It has also beaten the opening numbers of Gujju Pataka from the 2022 movie Satyaprem Ki Katha (34 million), Jai Shri Ram (32.2 million) and Ram Siya Ram (32.1 million), both from the 2023 movie Adipurush and Sikandar Naache (31.9 million) from the 2025 movie Sikandar.

Notably, While Tu Mil Jaaye has set a new record among Indian movie songs, standalone music releases continue to hold their ground in the overall 24-hour viewership rankings. Badshah's Paagal leads the list with 75 million views, followed by Guru Randhawa's Nain Bengali, which recorded 71.4 million views. B Praak's Filhal 2 - Mohabbat is next with 51 million views, while Guru Randhawa's collaboration with Pitbull, Slowly Slowly, clocked 38 million views, keeping it ahead of the new King track.

As per the latest buzz, The song brings Shah Rukh and Deepika back together, making their reunion one of its biggest talking points. Arijit Singh and Madhubanti Bagchi have lent their voices to the romantic number, composed by Sachin-Jigar and penned by Kumaar. International pop star Ed Sheeran is also part of the track's artist lineup. The video offers a mix of romance, action and dramatic dialogues, giving followers a glimpse of the world of King.
In further updates, Deepika made her Bollywood debut opposite Shah Rukh in Om Shanti Om and has since shared screen space with him in Happy New Year, Chennai Express, Pathaan and Jawan.

On top of that, December 24 will see Shah Rukh Khan return to the big screen with King, marking his first theatrical rollout since Dunki in 2023. King brings him back in a different avatar, with a sizeable cast including Suhana Khan, Abhishek Bachchan, Jackie Shroff, Arshad Warsi and Raghav Juyal, among others. Rani Mukerji, Deepika Padukone and Kareena Kapoor Khan are also set to make special appearances.
Directed by Siddharth Anand, King is produced by Gauri Khan's Red Chillies Entertainment along with Siddharth and Mamta Anand's Marflix Pictures.

title: Ramayana 3 on the cards? Namit Malhotra says makers may revisit plans after audience feedback
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The producer reveals that the first instalment has two different runtime versions and says the team is assessing whether an extended cut could be rolled out.

Adding to this, In conversation with international media during the movie’s recent Los Angeles premiere, Malhotra shared the original plan involved three parts, but the creative approach subsequently changed. He also left room for the possibility of further additions once the films reach audiences. “So we started out the movie, we were going to make it in three (parts), then we decided to make it in two. We're still in the middle of filming, so you know, I'm not going to give any spoilers for anything - but you know, who knows the way, once we get all the response and all the feedback, we may sit back on the table and the drawing board and see if there is anything else that we want to add or subtract, depending on how the world has received it,” Namit shared.

Meanwhile, Malhotra also opened up that the makers currently have two versions of Ramayana: Part 1 , each with a different runtime. The team is assessing audience feedback to determine whether one version can work for viewers worldwide or whether an extended cut could be considered. He went on to continue, “While we say that, we also have two different versions of the same movie, but two different run times on one - on part one itself. So, depending on which way the next round of feedback goes, I'd love to not have to make two different versions. I'm sure Nitesh would also prefer that, that if you could just stick to one, one version for the world.”
Notably, So there is still a chance of 3rd Part confirm by Namit Malhotra🛐
As per the latest buzz, #RanbirKapoor #Yash #SaiPallavi https://t.co/KwvKx7NbJt

title: No individual, group can occupy a designated protest site indefinitely: Supreme Court
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Supreme Court on Tuesday shared no individual, group or organisation could claim an indefinite right to occupy a designated protest site, underlining that others too have an equal constitutional right to use the same public space to raise their grievances.

Adding to this, The court is also examining the row over the Delhi Police’s decision to denotify Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site and shift demonstrations to Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground. (PTI File) The observations came as the court heard a clutch of petitions arising from the police action during the July protests led by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), including allegations of mass detentions, police excesses, internet restrictions and the closure of metro stations.

Meanwhile, The protests, which saw a proposed march towards Parliament and incidents of violence, also triggered a separate challenge by Delhi’s traders, who shared the prolonged demonstrations had disrupted business and affected their livelihoods.

Notably, “Even the right to protest at a designated site has to be for a certain period. You cannot occupy a protest site for all time to come…where will farmers, traders, journalists go? Everyone has a right to protest. Designated sites must be given for a designated period,” a bench, comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, observed.
As per the latest buzz, The bench made it clear that permission to hold a protest at an identified site could not translate into an open-ended licence to occupy it.

In further updates, “You cannot occupy a protest site indefinitely. You cannot prevent other people from protesting, saying ‘I can protest and you cannot’,” shared the court, adding that the order granting permission must spell out the reasons for allowing or refusing a protest and, if allowed, the duration for which the site could be used.

On top of that, Among others, the court was hearing a petition filed by the Kirana Committee Delhi and other traders’ bodies, represented by senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, who shared businesses in parts of the capital had suffered because of the demonstrations, particularly during the festive season. He told the bench that the Ramlila Ground was close to Connaught Place and that the surrounding stretch was home to millions of residents as well as several shops and commercial establishments.

Rohatgi urged the court to consider a solution that would protect the right to trade and earn a livelihood, including that of small traders, daily-wage workers and transport operators. He sought a prohibition on protests and dharnas in Delhi for the next two months, whether held with or without permission.

title: Ramayana: Bombay High Court grants anti-piracy protection to Ranbir Kapoor starrer ahead of November 5 release
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The court issued a dynamic ad-interim injunction against unauthorised recording, circulation and online distribution of the movie.

Adding to this, Godpower Media, which holds the domestic and territorial intellectual property and exploitation rights for the movie, approached the court seeking protection for several aspects of the project, including its script, character designs, footage, musical compositions, lyrics and audio recordings. The company as per reports expressed concerns over potential copyright violations, pointing out that unauthorised trailer footage had previously surfaced online despite non-disclosure agreements being in place for exclusive preview screenings.

Meanwhile, Taking note of the concerns, Justice Madhav Jamdar observed that the plaintiff had a "real and well-founded apprehension" that the movie could be subjected to illegal recording, streaming and piracy. The court also considered the substantial financial investment involved in the project. According to the details presented, Ramayana: Part 1 has an estimated budget of Rs. 2,000 crore rupees, while the two-part saga is shared to involve a combined investment of Rs. 4,000 crore rupees.

Notably, The court consequently passed a dynamic ad-interim injunction restraining unidentified entities, referred to as "John Doe" defendants, along with pirate websites and digital intermediaries, from recording, hosting or communicating the movie to the public without authorisation.

As per the latest buzz, The dynamic nature of the injunction allows the makers to notify internet service providers and digital platforms, including Google LLC, about infringing URLs and mirror websites that may emerge. The order enables swift takedown of such links and blocking of domains found to be facilitating unauthorised access to the movie. Legal representatives for Google and other major platforms as per reports recorded "no objection" to the directive and indicated that they would comply upon receiving the necessary notifications. The matter is scheduled to be heard next on December 16.

In further updates, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in association with Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana: Part 1 features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Goddess Sita, Yash as Ravana, Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman.
On top of that, The first instalment of the Nitesh Tiwari directorial, is scheduled to rollout worldwide in cinemas on November 5, 2026, across multiple Indian and international languages.

title: Yash says son Yatharv struggled to accept him as Ravana in Ramayana, as he's ‘Rama in real life’, recalls difficult conversation
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Nitesh Tiwari 's Ramayana is one of the most anticipated films of the year. The makers of late held the movie's grand world premiere in Los Angeles, and now the team is busy promoting it worldwide. During the promotions, star Yash opened up about his son Yatharv's reaction to him playing Ravana in Ramayana.

Adding to this, Yash reveals his son's reaction to him playing Ravana in Ramayana. Yash says son Yatharv questioned him for playing Ravana In a chat with television presenter Suma Kanakala on her YouTube channel, Yash revealed his son was upset about him playing Ravana and mentioned that his children grew up listening to the Ramayana from their grandparents. He shared, "For a son, his father is his hero. Since he knows the story [of the Ramayana], he asked me, ‘You are Ravana?! How can you be Ravana? Aren’t you Rama?’ So, I shared, ‘Yes, I am Rama in real life, but in the movie, I am playing Ravana.’ But he was like, ‘Then you are the bad guy.’ So, I explained to him about cinema and acting, showing him drawings and all of that."

Meanwhile, He added that when his son asked who he should root for while watching the movie, Yash found it to be a complicated question and added, "My followers might also have the same doubt, wondering, ‘Why is Yash doing this role?’ Especially since, in scenes like Sita Apaharan, I should not be liked. Then I told my kid in the most distinct way, ‘When we listen to the story, it is Rama whom everybody has to follow. Ravana might look glamorous, fancy, or powerful. But ultimately, if you have to win, you have to understand the essence of Lord Rama. However, in the movie, you can root for me. But don’t take it personally.'"

Notably, Yatharv further asked Yash whether he would die or lose in the movie. The Kannada superstar had to explain to his son that he was only playing a character. Yash admitted that the conversation caught him off guard, as he had not considered how his son might react to his role while working on the movie.

As per the latest buzz, He shared he had thought about his followers but had not anticipated his son asking him such a question. Yash added that he found it difficult to explain to Yatharv that the character he played was different from who he was in real life, and hoped that his son would understand this as he grew older.

In further updates, Helmed by Nitesh Tiwari and backed by Namit Malhotra, Ramayana is based on the epic poem by Valmiki, which chronicles the life and trials of Prince Rama. The two-part movie is mounted on a massive budget of ₹ 4000 crore rupees and stars Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi, Sunny Deol, and Ravi Dubey in lead roles. The movie also features Anupam Kher, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Adinath Kothare, Arun Govil, Indira Krishnan, and Lara Dutta in key roles.

On top of that, The first part of the movie is scheduled to rollout in theatres on November 5, 2026, and the second part is scheduled for Diwali 2027. The movie will rollout in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam across India. Sony Pictures will handle global distribution, excluding India, while Dharma Productions will distribute the movie in the Hindi-speaking market.

title: Delhi Police protest: SOP, courtroom security among 5 demands raised by protesting cops
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Delhi Police ACP Manasvi Vashishta , who led Monday's protest by around 500 police personnel outside the force's headquarters, has been suspended, a day after the protesting officers put forward five demands, including a grievance redressal committee and an SOP to deal with confrontations involving lawyers.

Adding to this, Transferred ACP Manasvi Vashishta alongside fellow Delhi Police personnel during a gathering outside the Police Headquarters (PHQ) on Jai Singh Road in New Delhi, India. (Sanchit Khanna/HT Photo) The protest followed the transfer of Vashishta and Arun Kumar, the station house officer (SHO) of Shahdara police station, after lawyers called for an indefinite strike over the police handling of an assault case involving advocate Lalit Bansal.
Meanwhile, The protest continued for over 10 hours, with a delegation meeting senior officers, including Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar, twice during the day.

Notably, The dispute stems from an altercation between two sides on October 23 in east Delhi’s Shahdara, during which Bansal sustained a head injury. An FIR was subsequently registered at the Shahdara police station on a complaint filed by advocate Amulya Ratan.

As per the latest buzz, Following the transfers, police personnel gathered outside the Delhi Police headquarters on Monday, pressing for their demands amid growing tensions between the police force and the legal fraternity.

In further updates, The protesting personnel submitted five demands, including that the FIR registered on Vashishta’s complaint against lawyers should not be quashed, that a grievance redressal committee be set up, and that standard operating procedures be framed to deal with confrontations involving lawyers.
On top of that, They also sought restrictions on the number of lawyers entering a police officer’s office at one time, and security for police personnel inside courtrooms.

“Our demands are clear. We need to meet CP sir. There needs to be an SOP (standard operating procedure) to deal with such matters. If this happens to us, how will we fight to save the people of the city” an earlier HT report quoted Vashishta as saying, amid chants of “Bharat Mata Ki Jai” and “Police Ekta Zindabad".

title: Panchayat actor Chandan Roy says his struggles in Mumbai helped him play desperate cabbie in Aakhri Ride | Interview
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Chandan Roy , who became a household name with his portrayal of Vikas in Panchayat, is now winning hearts with his latest short movie, Aakhri Ride , presented by filmmakers Anurag Kashyap and Vasan Bala. In the movie, Chandan plays a cab driver in Mumbai, and through his character’s struggles, the audience gets a glimpse of the city’s harsh realities and how they can push people to the brink of desperation.

Adding to this, Chandan Roy in a still from short-movie Aakhri Ride, which is presented by Anurag Kashyap and Vasan Bala. In an interaction with Hindustan Times, Chandan looked back at his early days of struggle, recalling how his dream of becoming an star led him to pursue journalism before eventually moving to Mumbai to follow his passion. The star also reflected on his nine-year journey in the city, how his career has evolved over the years and how Mumbai has gradually become home for him.

Meanwhile, Hailing from the small village of Mahnar in Bihar, Chandan had been interested in acting since his school days. However, with limited exposure and no access to the internet, he had to find his own way towards the world of cinema. He eventually chose to pursue mass communication, believing it would keep him close to cameras, lights, microphones and the entertainment industry.

Notably, Explaining the thought process behind that decision, Chandan recalled, “I had no money, and one has to do a lot of buttering to the bosses, and I just couldn't do that. I was a bit carefree. But thank God, I got a desk job. I thought, instead of going somewhere else to work and earn money, wouldn't it be better if I joined media? Because here we would have cameras, lights, microphones, and we would stay very aware of what's happening in Bollywood.”

As per the latest buzz, He shared that he saw mass communication as a way to remain connected to cinema while also finding opportunities to earn a living. “There was no one to guide me either. Mass Communication felt somewhat closer to cinema. I was thinking I could be seen on TV. All these thoughts were going through my head. In a small town with no internet, we made our decisions by reading newspaper clippings. So, for that boy at that time, I think it was his best decision,” he shared.

In further updates, Reflecting on completing nine years in Mumbai, Chandan shared that he has gradually found comfort in the city, calling it home, but his approach towards work remains unchanged. “Today marks nine years of my time in Mumbai. Believe me, the boy who arrived nine years ago with a small suitcase — I still feel the exact same way today,” he shared.

On top of that, The star explained that growing up in Bihar instilled in him a strong work ethic, something that continues to define his life in Mumbai. “I come from a very small town in Bihar, and hard work and manual labour are taught deeply there. Even now in Mumbai, I feel—you came here to work, earn, and make a name for yourself. Every morning I wake up with this exact energy. So that attitude is still there today,” he shared.

During the conversation, Chandan also spoke about what convinced him to take up Aakhri Ride. The star shared that the decision came down to the story, the filmmakers, and, most importantly, the association with filmmaker Anurag Kashyap.

title: Satluj director Honey Trehan calls new censor board advisory for filmmakers ‘cowardness and dictatorship’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

On October 26, the Central Board of Movie Certification ( CBFC ) issued a new advisory for filmmakers looking to certify their films. Some of the new guidelines raised eyebrows, with the board making it clear that revealed titles and rollout dates will not be taken into consideration during the process. Director Honey Trehan , whose Diljit Dosanjh-starrer Satluj, previously titled Panjab ‘95, did not get certification, called the new diktat ‘cowardness and dictatorship’.

Adding to this, News of the new CBFC advisory began circulating widely on Monday, inviting a range of opinions. Honey re-posted a poster of his movie Satluj shared by Variety India on his Instagram Stories with ‘New CBFC guidelines for filmmakers’ written on it. Giving his opinion on the same, he added, “New Guidelines shows and underlines the Cowardness & the Dictatorship in the country not the Democratic approach towards the freedom of speech.”

Meanwhile, New CBFC guidelines for filmmakers were issued in September, and the new advisory was rolled out in October. 18 new members were revealed to constitute the board this year, for the first time since 2017. Preity Zinta, Pankaj Tripathi, Suniel Shetty, Pallavi Joshi, Ricky Kej, and Supriya Yarlagadda are among its members. The advisory states that filmmakers must submit the final version of their movie, complete with titles, graphics, and sound, for certification. They also shared that the revealed title and rollout dates will not be considered.

Notably, This comes after Honey’s Satluj was stuck in the CBFC certification process for nearly three years. There was a standoff between the makers and the board, as the board refused to comply with the requested changes. The movie, originally titled Ghallughara, was renamed Panjab ‘95 and eventually dropped, uncut and silently, on Zee5 under the name Satluj in July. The movie was taken down within hours of its rollout.

As per the latest buzz, Tamil Nadu chief minister Vijay’s final movie, Jana Nayagan , was also stuck with the CBFC for months when it was sent to a revising committee at the last minute before its intended theatrical rollout in January for Pongal. The makers faced off the CBFC in court but received no relief. The movie eventually hit screens in July after the makers complied with the changes asked by the board. A few other films across the country have also had scenes removed and titles changed during the certification process.

In further updates, Despite having a Master's degree in Journalism and over a decade of experience in print and digital media as a field reporter and sub-editor at organisations such as The Times of India and Reader's Digest, Neeshita Nyayapati remains a movie buff first and a Chief Content Producer second. She fell in love with movies in childhood and believes nothing matches the magic of watching a good movie that moves you with a warm tub of popcorn in hand. title: Armaan Malik defends Ramayana song Mangal Rang from criticism, says interpretation of music is subjective
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The track Mangal Rang from the Ranbir Kapoor -starrer Ramayana became the subject of debate on social media. Several listeners questioned its musical treatment, arguing that the composition carries Sufi qawwali influences they felt were misplaced in a movie based on the Hindu epic. Others compared it to AR Rahman's earlier tracks, such as Kun Faya Kun from Rockstar.

Adding to this, Singer Armaan Malik spoke about Ramayana song Mangal Rang row. ‘Listener interpretation of music is always going to be subjective’ While the Hindi version of the song is sung by Arijit Singh and Shreya Ghoshal, Armaan Malik has lent his voice to the Kannada version, titled Mangala Sangama, alongside Bela Shende. In a recent interaction with News18, Armaan spoke about the criticism surrounding the song and shared that the interpretation of music is always subjective. Mangal Rang depicts the wedding of Lord Rama and Sita.

Meanwhile, In conversation with News18, he shared, “The entire music team was completely united in one single goal – ensure the sonic experience reflected the pure love and divinity portrayed onscreen by Ranbir (Kapoor) and Sai Pallavi. How a listener interprets the music is always going to be subjective and that’s the nature of art. But as an artist, my only focus was the deep devotion of the moment and ensuring we delivered that with the utmost respect.”

Notably, Armaan has long hoped to lend his voice to a song featuring Ranbir Kapoor. In previous interviews, he had spoken about wanting to sing for actors such as Ranbir and Shah Rukh Khan. With Mangala Sangama, one of those dreams has finally come true. Talking about it, he shared, “It’s a huge personal milestone. We all grow up watching certain icons define cinematic romance and emotion, and Ranbir has undoubtedly been that figure for my generation. What makes this even more special is the journey behind it."

As per the latest buzz, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, while Sai Pallavi portrays Sita, and Yash plays Ravana. The movie also stars Ravi Dubey as Lakshman and Sunny Deol as Hanuman. The movie's music brings together AR Rahman and Oscar-winning composer Hans Zimmer.

In further updates, The movie, which is scheduled to rollout in cinemas worldwide on November 5, is also breaking ticket-window records. The movie's advance booking opened on Dussehra, a full 15 days before its global rollout and now, just two days ahead of its theatrical rollout, the movie has crossed the ₹ 100-crore rupees mark in worldwide pre-sales.

title: Shah Rukh Khan's King earns ₹665 crore in pre-release deals; would need to out-earn Jailer 2, Chhaava just to break even
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

The promotional campaign for Shah Rukh Khan ’s King has begun. On his birthday, November 2, the superstar shared the movie’s first song with the world. With this, the countdown to King ’s rollout - seven weeks out - has begun. And while it is too early to talk about the movie’s box-office prospects, reports say it is already breaking the bank in terms of pre-rollout business.

Adding to this, Shah Rukh Khan's King will rollout on Christmas this year. King earns ₹ 665 crore rupees in pre-rollout business King, directed by Siddharth Anand , marks Shah Rukh’s reunion with the director after their 2023 smash hit Pathaan. Naturally, the anticipation for the movie is sky-high. As a result, the movie has secured major distribution deals, as well as digital and music rights. Phars Films acquired the movie’s overseas rights, as per reports for a record minimum guarantee of ₹ 175 crore rupees. No Indian movie has ever crossed ₹ 100 crore rupees. Now, Pinkvilla has reported that the movie's Indian distribution rights have been sold to Pen Marudhar for ₹ 250 crore rupees. This is among the highest for any Hindi movie as well.

Meanwhile, In addition, the report states that Netflix has bought the movie’s streaming rights for ₹ 150 crore rupees, while the satellite and music rights have been sold for ₹ 25 crore rupees and ₹ 65 crore rupees, respectively. The Netflix deal comes with a theatrical performance rider, which means the streaming rights figure could rise or fall depending on how King performs at the ticket-window. But in case the figures hold, King has collected ₹ 665 crore rupees globally before its rollout.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by T-Series (@tseries.official)

As per the latest buzz, King was mounted on a massive ₹ 300-crore rupees budget, equal to Shah Rukh’s last grand rollout - Jawan. However, reports from Sacnilk and Pinkvilla state that during production, the budget ballooned up to almost ₹ 400 crore rupees. In addition, sources say that Red Chillies Entertainment, the movie’s producers, are spending almost ₹ 50 crore rupees on promotion and marketing. After including Shah Rukh’s notional fee, King’s landing cost could balloon up to ₹ 550 crore rupees. This means the movie will have to cross this mark in its net earnings to break even. The global distribution fee of ₹ 425 crore rupees is another threshold the movie must meet for it to be profitable for distributors.

In further updates, Given that Shah Rukh’s films usually have a 60-40 ratio of domestic to overseas gross earnings, this would mean King would have to earn ₹ 400 crore rupees net ( ₹ 500 crore rupees gross) domestically and ₹ 150 crore rupees net ( ₹ 300 crore rupees gross) overseas to be profitable. This comes out to a global haul of around ₹ 800 crore rupees, the same amount that Rajinikanth’s Jailer 2 has collected so far, or what Vicky Kaushal’s Chhaava managed last year.

On top of that, Directed by Siddharth Anand, King will rollout in theatres on December 24, 2026, making it a major Christmas rollout. The movie marks Shah Rukh's reunion with Anand after their collaboration on 'Pathaan', which was rolled out in theatres in 2023. The movie is Shah Rukh's first rollout in over three years, since Rajkumar Hirani's Dunki hit the screens. King marks the star's first on-screen collaboration with his daughter, Suhana Khan. It also features Deepika Padukone, Rani Mukerji, and Abhishek Bachchan in key roles.

title: Ranbir Kapoor tells Western media he doesn't like the term Bollywood as it derives from Hollywood, wants to be a 'representative of Indian cinema'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Ranbir Kapoor has made his stance clear on the use of the term ‘Bollywood’ to describe Hindi cinema, or sometimes all of Indian cinema. In an interview with a British media outlet, Ranbir agreed he was not a fan of the term and would prefer to be known as an Indian star rather than a Bollywood star.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor spoke about not liking the term Bollywood. (AFP) Not Bollywood, but Indian cinema Ranbir is promoting his soon-to-release movie, Ramayana , for which he was of late in London along with castmates Sai Pallavi and Yash. There, the star spoke to ITV where the host asked him why he was not a fan of the ‘umbrella term Bollywood’ used to describe Indian films. Ranbir responded, “I think it's just a term used as a derivative of Hollywood. Because it was Bombay at that time, so it became Bollywood, and the Telugu industry became Tollywood, and they had all these different-sounding names.”

Meanwhile, The star clarified that he would want to be known as someone from Indian cinema instead. “I would like to be a representative of Indian cinema. We come from a country where we have different cultures, different languages, different states. But at the end of it, we are all striving to make art. And art is something that gets people together. There are no borders in art. You tell a good, authentic story that is rooted in your culture and tradition; it always speaks to the world. We have seen that with Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, with films from Korea, and with Life Is Beautiful. The ambition is that, but you are not blindly just trying to cater to a global audience. You are still trying to be really authentic in your storytelling and culture,” added Ranbir.

Notably, Ranbir is currently awaiting the rollout of Ramayana, the most expensive Indian movie ever made. Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The first part is scheduled for worldwide rollout on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2027. The films will rollout in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam across India.

title: Amitabh Bachchan's bulletproof enclosure, Shah Rukh Khan waving to fans from afar at Mannat: New face of celeb fan meets amid threats?
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

For decades, Amitabh Bachchan 's Sunday ritual of meeting followers outside his Mumbai home in Juhu has been one of Bollywood's most cherished traditions. But his latest appearance on November I came with an unusual addition: a transparent bulletproof enclosure around the veteran star as he waved to the crowd, while son, star Abhishek Bachchan, stood close by, keeping a watchful eye on the surroundings. Shah Rukh Khan too, this year changed his usual spot for waving to and greeting followers. Notably, this time the position was quite far, in the back.

Adding to this, Salman Khan, Amitabh Bachchan The added security comes in the wake of the firing incident involving star Tiger Shroff in Mumbai last month, in which gunmen opened fire at his car in Juhu. Tiger has since had bulletproof protection installed on his car's windshield. Star Salman Khan, meanwhile, had bulletproof glass fitted on the balcony of his Galaxy Apartments residence in Mumbai's Bandra in January last year, from where he traditionally waves to followers on Eid and his birthday. He had also imported a bulletproof car in 2024 amid threats to his life.

Meanwhile, Star Ronit Roy, who runs a star and private security agency, believes such a measure is a basic protocol for “a legendary star like Mr Bachchan. It should have been done much earlier. The moment stars step out of their homes, the risk and threat factor shoots up. Precautions are necessary.”

Notably, Yusuf Ibrahim, who has worked as a security consultant to celebs like Alia Bhatt and Shah Rukh Khan, adds, “With the way things are right now, prevention is better than cure. But I believe this is a temporary phase, this won't be permanent. The law will do whatever needs to be done, and those responsible (for the tension) will be brought to justice.”

As per the latest buzz, Advertising guru Prahlad Kakkar, meanwhile, views the development as "unfortunate". He says. “It’s unfortunate that the criminal elements in our society have managed to create such paranoia among stars that the most important interaction they have, with their followers and supporters, is now happening with restrictions. Going forward, unless we do something about it, I don’t see this changing. The threat is not just national but international, and it is becoming a complex problem.”

In further updates, Recalling how stars would once make time for followers on movie sets, he adds that this accessibility is still prevalent in the South, unlike Bollywood, where “the star system has become cast in stone”.
