title: Orry calls Sara Ali Khan 'fake friend' for disappearing during his difficult time, claims Amrita Singh hurled abuses at him and never apologised
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Social media personality and Khatron Ke Khiladi star Orhan Awatramani, popularly known as Orry , is friends with several Bollywood celebrities, including star Sara Ali Khan . However, their friendship hit a rough patch, leading to a fallout. Now, in a conversation with Neha Dhupia and Angad Bedi on their show Double Date, Orry has opened up about what went wrong between them.

Adding to this, Orry opens up about the fallout with Sara Ali Khan and Amrita Singh. Orry talks about the fallout with Sara Ali Khan When Neha asked him to name the most famous person he had unfollowed on social media, Orry replied, "Sara Ali Khan." When she asked him to elaborate, he shared, "I'm very public about it. Her mother scolded me a lot, so I unfollowed her too."

Meanwhile, Orry went on to describe their friendship and explain why he felt let down. He shared, "There are fake friendships. This girl was my childhood friend. We were friends through college and then even 10 years after college. I was there for her through so much. We were in Goa when she got into a big case. I stood by her through all of that, never left her side. But for one time in life when she had to be there for me, she disappeared."

Notably, He added, "In that moment, it was such a tough phase for me, and she didn't check on me once or call me once. I was like, when your life was under fire, and everyone told me to leave her side and not get caught up, I stood by her side. I took care of you, your mother and your brother and stood by them. And when the tables flipped, and you had to be there with me for once, you couldn't even give me a phone call. I just thought if I pretended to be friends with you, then whatever you did and whatever abuses your mother threw at me and shared about me to others, it made that okay. And it's not okay, and I never got an apology after that."

As per the latest buzz, Orry and Sara Ali Khan's friendship as per reports hit a rough patch in August 2025 after he shared pictures of the star on her birthday that some social media users considered unflattering. The situation drew further attention when Orry later shared a reel titled "3 worst names", in which he mentioned "Sara", "Amrita" and "Palak" without using their surnames. Shortly afterwards, Sara and her brother Ibrahim Ali Khan unfollowed Orry on Instagram, adding to speculation that the friends had fallen out. Orry also took a dig at Sara's acting career during a social media exchange.

In further updates, Orry had previously spoken about the fallout in a January 2026 interview with Hindustan Times. Discussing his equation with Sara, he shared their friendship could move forward only if he did not have to overlook what he claimed had happened to him because of her mother. At the time, Orry also suggested that an apology from Amrita Singh could potentially change things. "If Amrita Singh were to apologise, I could maybe see myself letting it go in the future," he had shared.

title: Nora Fatehi's team issues statement, clarifies she is ‘not an accused’ in Sukesh Chandrashekhar case: ‘Summoned as a witness'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Nora Fatehi 's legal team has clarified that she is neither an accused nor alleged to have committed any offence in the Sukesh Chandrashekhar case. The clarification comes after the Economic Offences Wing (EOW) matter was listed before the Rouse Avenue Court in Delhi on November 2, where Nora was summoned as a witness.

Adding to this, Sukesh Chandrashekhar, Nora Fatehi In a statement on Tuesday, her legal team shared, “The EOW matter concerning Sukesh Chandra Shekhar was listed today before the Rouse Avenue Court, Delhi, where Nora Fatehi was summoned as a witness. Her advocates appeared before the Court and submitted that she had received the summons at a very short notice and was unable to attend due to prior professional commitments. An application seeking exemption from personal appearance was filed, following which the matter was adjourned to 6 November 2026, with fresh summons issued for her appearance.”

Meanwhile, “It is clarified that Nora Fatehi is neither an accused nor alleged to have committed any offence in these proceedings. She has been summoned solely as a witness to assist the Court,” they added.

Notably, The case pertains to allegations that Sukesh, while lodged in Delhi's Rohini Jail, impersonated senior government officials and extorted approximately ₹ 200 crore rupees. The Delhi Police's Economic Offences Wing investigated the case and filed a chargesheet under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA).

As per the latest buzz, Nora was earlier questioned by the EOW in connection with her alleged association with Chandrashekhar and his wife, Leena Maria Paulose. Her statement was recorded under Section 164 of the CrPC, following which she was named as a prosecution witness in the supplementary chargesheet. She had told investigators that her interactions with Chandrashekhar were through his wife.

title: Ramayana advance booking storms past ₹100 crore days before release; Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film eyeing Dhurandhar 2, RRR-level start
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

The Ramayana is now entering its home stretch in terms of advance bookings. Just two days before its grand worldwide rollout, the movie has crossed the ₹ 100-crore rupees mark in pre-sales worldwide. This is a mark very few Indian films have crossed, highlighting the anticipation and hype around the rollout of the Nitesh Tiwari movie.

Adding to this, Ramayana: Part One is set to rollout worldwide on November 5. Ramayana advance bookings set records Advance bookings for Ramayana opened on Dussehra, 15 full days before its global rollout. But after a strong start on day 1, the pace plateaued. This was largely because, over the next 10 days, only the Hindi version had many shows open. Most of the single-screen and smaller centres did not open till last week. This was because the movie’s distributors - Dharma Productions - were in negotiations with the exhibitors for a higher revenue share. Then, last Friday, the stalemate ended, and more screens were added over the weekend.

Meanwhile, That was reflected in the manic growth in Ramayana’s pre-sales worldwide over the last three days. By Tuesday morning, the number of screens for the movie had increased to over 5000. Over 1500 of these were added in the last 24 hours alone. By the morning of November 3, two days before its rollout, the movie had grossed ₹ 58 crore rupees in pre-sales in India. This included an impressive ₹ 27 crore rupees from the opening day itself. What is truly impressive about Ramayana’s advance-booking trend is that the entire weekend is seeing huge demand for tickets, not just on opening day. The second and third days have so far contributed ₹ 25 crore rupees in gross pre-sales. Day 4, Sunday, has few shows open now, but is steadily catching up as well.

Notably, Ramayana has now sold almost 15 lakh tickets in pre-sales across India. The premium formats - including IMAX - are driving sales, accounting for almost one-fourth of total sales, despite holding just 4% of screens.
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sony Pictures UK (@sonypicturesuk)

title: ‘Disagreement is your right, not talking about dam construction now’: CM Pema Khandu amid protests against Siang project
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Arunachal Pradesh chief minister Pema Khandu on Monday evening shared no decision has been taken on the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) and all concerns surrounding the construction of the mega dam would be addressed through open dialogue, transparency and meaningful public consultation.

Adding to this, Charred remains of the vehicles after a protest against the proposed large-scale dam on the Siang River turned violent in Pasighat, in East Siang on Saturday. (ANI video grab) The chief minister’s remarks come amid intense opposition from sections of the indigenous Adi community, particularly residents of the proposed project-affected areas, over apprehensions that the dam may result in submergence of ancestral villages, cause displacement and loss of agricultural land and forests, and possibly disrupt the community's traditional way of life. The state government, however, maintains the project is a strategic safeguard against China’s massive hydropower development upstream, on the Yarlung Tsangpo River in Tibet.
Meanwhile, The opposition Congress has also demanded the scrapping of the project and called for a 36-hour bandh from Monday, disrupting normal life in the Upper Siang district.
Notably, In a detailed statement, Khandu shared neither the Centre nor the state government had finalised the construction of the proposed 11,000-MW project.

As per the latest buzz, "Let me be clear. We are not talking about dam construction at this stage," he shared, adding that the government was considering only a Pre-Feasibility Report (PFR) to assess the project's viability and potential implications.

In further updates, He maintained that preparing the PFR would not amount to granting approval for construction. "I want to assure you that your voices, your land, your homes and our beloved 'Aane Siang' remain at the heart of every consideration. Your concerns will be addressed through open dialogue, transparency and meaningful public consultation," he shared.
On top of that, "In a democracy, every voice matters, and disagreement is your right," he added and appealed for peace and cautioned against violence, blockades and attacks.

The chief minister shared the project, declared a National Project in 2008, gained strategic significance following China's commencement of construction of a massive hydropower project on the Yarlung Tsangpo River in Tibet in July 2025.

title: Surat court issues warrant against Anurag Kashyap for failing to appear in case over 'anti-Brahmin' remarks
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

A Surat city court on Monday issued a bailable warrant against filmmaker-star Anurag Kashyap for failing to appear before it in a case pertaining to his alleged offensive remarks made on social media against the Brahmin community last year.

Adding to this, Anurag Kashyap was accused of making 'anti-Brahmin' remarks in 2025. Surat court issues warrant against Anurag Kashyap Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate JV Chauhan issued the bailable warrant against Kashyap and kept the matter for further hearing on December 24.

Meanwhile, The order was passed after the 54-year-old filmmaker, known for helming critically acclaimed Gangs of Wasseypur and Black Friday, among other Hindi movies, failed to appear before the court despite summonses being issued against him, including via a newspaper.

Notably, The court in May directed registration of a case against Kashyap under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) sections 192 (promoting enmity between different groups), 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of peace), and 352 (2) (circulating false rumours) on an application filed by lawyer Kamlesh Raval, a legal advisor to Hindutva outfits Bajrang Dal and Vishwa Hindu Parishad.

As per the latest buzz, As part of the judicial proceedings, the court issued a summons to Kashyap, but he failed to appear before it. When he remained absent on Monday, the court issued a bailable warrant against him, Raval shared.

In further updates, A bailable warrant allows the accused person to secure rollout by furnishing bail as specified by the court. “We initially filed an application and requested his presence (in court) for verification, but he failed to appear. The trial court subsequently initiated proceedings against him. A summons was then issued, yet he did not show up. The court directed that a public summons be published in a newspaper. We arranged for this to be printed in a prominent newspaper (in its Mumbai edition), but he still failed to appear,” Raval maintained.

On top of that, The applicant had sought legal action against Kashyap for his remarks dated April 16, 2025, wherein he posted “an objectionable message on social media (X) that cast a slur upon the entire Brahmin community.”

In his plea, the petitioner shared that when an individual named Aaditya objected to Kashyap's post, the filmmaker responded angrily with a post berating him and asking, “What have you achieved by being a Brahmin?” Raval claimed that by making such comments, Kashyap attempted “to disparage the Brahmin community, and this post constitutes an insult to the entire Brahmin community.”

title: VFX expert Arun Kumar calls for law to mandate bold labelling of AI on social media amid Janhvi Kapoor, Keerthy Suresh flagging misuse | HT Exclusive
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The boom in artificial intelligence (AI) has affected the movie industry in more ways than one, even before the technology has been fully integrated into movie production. Misuse is rampant, with numerous actors such as Janhvi Kapoor , Sunainaa and Keerthy Suresh expressing shock and warning of legal action after seeing their likeness being used in objectionable deepfake videos or photos. And the conversations around ‘is that CGI or sloppy AI’ are never-ending every time a promotional poster or video drops.

Adding to this, Janhvi Kapoor had of late called out those using AI to morph her visuals from the Chuttamalle song in Devara. ((Image used for representative purpose only)) Speaking exclusively to Hindustan Times, VFX expert and dean of communications, movie and gaming at Pearl Academy, CB Arun Kumar, discusses the moral concerns surrounding the use of AI and calls for laws mandating proper labelling of AI-generated content on social media. He also calls blanket criticism of the technology foolish.

Meanwhile, Arun points out that even before the existence of AI and sophisticated deepfakes, people would use body doubles, Photoshop and later VFX techniques like cloning and morphing to generate fake content. AI has now, unfortunately, become another tool in their arsenal for making a quick buck. “There are already plenty of legal ways to take down that kind of objectionable content,” he adds.

Notably, However, the issue now lies in AI making it difficult for viewers to distinguish between what’s real and what's fake. “Even on a legal platform like Instagram, the AI content disclaimer is a tiny, hidden message that viewers might not easily see,” explains Arun, adding, “We need stricter laws that mandate clear, bold labelling of AI content so it can no longer pretend to be news, like some disaster clips that proliferate on the internet. The real problem arises when the audience can no longer tell what’s real and what is fake.”

As per the latest buzz, However, Arun believes that blanket criticism of AI is foolish. “It’s important to distinguish between blanket criticism of AI and speaking up about the illegal use of it trained on an artist’s work without their consent. The former is foolish; the latter is a genuine legal and moral concern. Taking the Luddite position that all AI is evil and all the work it creates is stolen from humans is simply meaningless,” he says.

In further updates, Arun points out that throughout history, human progress has depended on our ability to copy and produce the work of other humans, much like art students learn by studying and copying work of masters. “All human art is based on the foundations of work done earlier. Legally, an exact copy is a forgery only if the artist claims it is the original artist's work. If I paint the Mona Lisa or The Starry Night and say it is a reproduction I made. It would be just that, a reproduction. The value still only resides in the original artwork preserved in a museum,” he reasons.

On top of that, However, he acknowledges that not just actors but even digital artists are bearing the brunt of AI's rise in different ways. “The work they create painstakingly is no longer worth as much commercially. Many graphic artists who work in media, business, movie, TV, architecture or fashion could find their work being compared to AI slop. The reality is that the AI revolution is putting them out of work because it can do the work faster. True artists who can use AI as another tool in their pipeline will survive and thrive,” he predicts.

Arun says that so far, 2026 has made him excited, curious, slightly concerned, but still deeply optimistic for the future of the industry. “There is nothing we can do about AI; it’s already there. Pandora’s box is open. Those who bury their heads in the sand like ostriches are likely to be swept away by the tides of time. We all have to learn to live with it and thrive,” he rounds off.

title: Bombay High Court protects Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's mega-budget Ramayana from illegal uploads, piracy and streaming
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:

The makers of Ramayana are taking steps to keep their big-budget movie safe from piracy ahead of its theatrical rollout. The Bombay High Court has granted their plea for interim protection, restraining unidentified individuals and digital platforms from recording, uploading or streaming the movie without authorisation. The court has also directed internet service providers and social media platforms to take down pirated content once the makers bring it to their notice.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor's ₹4,000 crore rupees Ramayana gets Bombay High Court protection against online piracy. (AFP) The order came on Monday, with Justice Madhav Jamdar hearing a copyright infringement suit filed by Godpower Media Private Limited. The company holds the movie's copyright and exploitation rights across India and overseas territories.

Meanwhile, As reported by Bar and Bench, the court was informed that the first part of Ramayana has been mounted on a budget of ₹ 2,000 crore rupees, with the two films together costing ₹ 4,000 crore rupees. Godpower Media also flagged an earlier breach, telling the court that footage from both trailers had been secretly recorded and circulated online. This was despite the makers keeping the preview screenings invite-only and requiring attendees to sign non-disclosure agreements.

Notably, With Ramayana set for a worldwide theatrical rollout on November 5, the company approached the court to prevent any further leaks or unauthorised sharing of its content. Its plea seeks protection not only for the movie itself but also for the script, characters, footage, lyrics and sound recordings.

As per the latest buzz, Justice Madhav Jamdar acknowledged the concerns raised by Godpower Media, noting that there was a real risk of the movie or parts of it being recorded and shared online without permission. “Prima facie, the plaintiff (Godpower) has real and well-founded apprehension that the movie or parts of it will be recorded and uploaded, streamed, or communicated to the public on various platforms,” Justice Jamdar observed, as per the report.

In further updates, The court's order covers not just known offenders but also unidentified individuals who may attempt to circulate the movie illegally. The dynamic injunction against John Doe defendants is particularly important because it allows action against pirates even when their identities are unknown. The court has also taken note of the practice of pirated content resurfacing through mirror websites after original links are taken down. ISPs and social media platforms have been directed to block or remove such links once Godpower Media sends them written notice.

On top of that, Lawyers representing Google LLC and other social media platforms did not oppose the company's request and told the court that they would act on complaints of piracy. Godpower Media will have to share the URLs carrying unauthorised copies or clips of the movie with the concerned platforms and internet service providers, who will then be required to block or remove the content.

Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana: Part 1 stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Sunny Deol as Hanuman and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. The movie is produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash's Monster Mind Creations.

Please allow them the privacy, compassion and space they need to grieve the loss of their father,” she shared.

title: Delhi HC issues notice to CBFC, Centre over Sunny Deol's Suryaa as doctors flag violence against healthcare workers in the teaser
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Sunny Deol ’s soon-to-release movie Suryaa : Ant Se Aarambh Tak has run into legal trouble ahead of its theatrical rollout, with a group of doctors approaching the Delhi High Court over its teaser. They have alleged that the movie paints doctors in private hospitals in a negative light and could encourage hostility towards healthcare professionals. Taking up the petition, the court has sought responses from the Centre, the Central Board of Movie Certification ( CBFC ) and the movie's producers. The matter will be heard next on November 16.

Adding to this, Delhi High Court seeks government, CBFC response over Suryaa teaser amid doctors' concerns over violence. Why doctors have objected to the teaser According to a report by The Print, Justice Amit Mahajan has issued notices to the CBFC, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, producer M M Moviez and Zee Entertainment Enterprises Limited. During the hearing, advocate Varun Singh, who appeared for the doctors, urged the court to stop the teaser from being shown online. The court, however, chose not to pass any immediate order on the request.

Meanwhile, The petition has been filed by four Delhi-based doctors, Dr. Nishant Soni, Dr. Ashish Tomar, Dr. Ravi Bhatia and Dr. Shivam Vatsal, who are associated with different corporate hospitals. Office bearers of D.O.C.S (Doctors of Corporate Society) are also part of the plea. The doctors have approached the court, alleging that the authorities failed to act on their complaints about the teaser. They have cited the "inaction of authorities" as one of the reasons for filing the petition, arguing that the way the movie portrays the medical profession could have real-world consequences. The plea maintains that the threat posed by such "unverifiable and defamatory content is not speculative."

Notably, They have also raised concerns about the safety of doctors, pointing out that medical professionals often face anger and even attacks from patients' families, especially when treatment does not go as expected. The petitioners fear that portraying doctors as dishonest and money-minded could deepen mistrust between patients and healthcare workers, worsening an already difficult situation.

As per the latest buzz, The petition states that Suryaa is a Hindi adaptation of the 2018 Malayalam movie Joseph, directed by M. Padmakumar. The original movie tells the story of a retired police officer who stumbles upon an organ-harvesting racket linked to the alleged misuse of brain-stem death declarations at a private hospital. Rolled out on October 19 on Zee Music Company's YouTube channel, the trailer describes the movie as "inspired by unbelievable true events" and promises to uncover the "shocking truth" about the medical system.

In further updates, The petitioners believe this could give audiences the impression that the incidents shown are real, even though the movie is fictional. They have also raised objections to the depiction of private hospitals allegedly obtaining consent for organ donation after declaring patients brain-stem dead. The doctors have further questioned the portrayal of medical professionals as people who overcharge patients, push unnecessary tests and earn commissions.

On top of that, They argue that such representations, especially when presented as inspired by true events, could create mistrust towards doctors and hospitals. Their concerns also extend to the response the teaser has received online. The petition points to comments on its YouTube page, alleging that some viewers have gone as far as issuing threats and calling for violence against doctors.

The doctors have also sought a wider review of the movie and its promotional content, asking the authorities to step in under the Cinematograph Act and the Information Technology Act. They want the teaser taken down from online platforms until it has been examined by the concerned authorities. The petition also calls for changes to the movie and its promotional material, if needed, and a clear disclaimer stating that the story is fictional. The doctors have further urged the authorities to introduce guidelines that bring online teasers and trailers under the movie-certification process.

title: Amitabh Bachchan recalls Jaya Bachchan’s cute nickname for him, but says his father eventually put a stop to it
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Amitabh Bachchan and Jaya Bachchan are among the most iconic couples in the Hindi movie industry. The height difference between the two stars has often been a talking point. Of late, during an episode of Kaun Banega Crorepati, which featured Ranbir Kapoor , Ravi Dubey and Sai Pallavi as guests to promote their soon-to-release movie Ramayana, Amitabh shared a funny anecdote about how Jaya would tease him by calling him ‘lambu ji (Mr Tall)’. However, his father, poet Harivansh Rai Bachchan, did not approve of the nickname and soon put a stop to it.

Adding to this, Jaya Bachchan and Amitabh Bachchan have been married since 1973. ‘She used to call me lambu ji’ The conversation began with a discussion of the height differences between members of the Bachchan family and those of Ranbir Kapoor’s family. Ranbir also spoke about how he had imagined the height dynamics between himself, Amitabh, Alia Bhatt and Jaya Bachchan.

Meanwhile, Sharing the anecdote about Jaya, Amitabh shared that she had called him ‘lambu ji’ for several years. However, his father eventually asked her not to address him that way and suggested that she either use his name or call him by another name. Jaya then began addressing him by his name. He shared, "For many years, she used to call me lambu ji. Later, she was asked not to address me that way. Babuji shared, ‘Look, don’t call him that. Either use his name or call him something else.’ After that, she started calling me by my name."

Notably, Ranbir admitted that he had often imagined himself and Alia as a taller and shorter version of Amitabh and Jaya. He shared, "I would always picture it in my mind that I would be a little tall like Amit ji, and Alia would be a little short like Jaya aunty, so the height differences would look nice in those photographs… I always used to think about this."

As per the latest buzz, Amitabh was amused by the comparison and remarked that there was a considerable difference in their heights. Ranbir then turned the conversation towards Amitabh and Jaya, asking how much taller the star was than his wife. Amitabh opened up that he stood at 6 feet 2 inches, while Jaya was approximately 5 feet 3 or 4 inches tall. Ranbir then joked that his own height was somewhere around Jaya's.

In further updates, Amitabh and Jaya's relationship goes back to the early 1970s. The two met on sets of Hrishikesh Mukherjee's Guddi. While Jaya was smitten early on, Amitabh as per reports fell in love with her later during the filming of Ek Nazar in 1972.

On top of that, The two went on to share screen space in films such as Zanjeer, Abhimaan, Chupke Chupke and Sholay. After Zanjeer became a massive hit, they tied the knot in June 3, 1973. They have since been married for more than five decades and have two children, Shweta Bachchan Nanda and Abhishek Bachchan and three grand children -- Navya Naveli Nanda, Agastya Nanda and Aaradhya Bachchan.

Meanwhile, Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Ravi Dubey are gearing up for the rollout of Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana. Ranbir plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi portrays Sita and Ravi Dubey essays Lakshman. Yash will be seen as Ravana, while Sunny Deol plays Hanuman.

title: ₹8000 crore box office gross, 10 blockbusters, most number 1 films: How Shah Rukh Khan left contemporaries behind to become the ‘King’ of Bollywood'
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

In the 90s, when the question arose about who would take over the mantle of Bollywood’s top star from Amitabh Bachchan , the three Khans stood up. Born within a few months of each other, these three actors began their careers around the same time and had their breakthroughs as leading heroes simultaneously. For the next half-decade, the names Shah Rukh , Salman, and Aamir were almost always used together. Any rising star was dubbed the ‘fourth Khan’. But then came a time when Shah Rukh broke free, earning the moniker "King Khan."

Adding to this, Shah Rukh Khan has been the most successful Indian star in the last three decades. (AFP) In a career spanning almost four decades, Shah Rukh has established himself as one of the most successful actors in the history of Hindi cinema. With a ticket-window gross of almost ₹ 8000 crore rupees and an enviable overseas record, he truly has been the numero uno star of the Hindi movie industry. A look at how that incredible career has stacked up in numbers.

Meanwhile, Shah Rukh debuted in films in 1992, four years after both Salman and Aamir had made their respective debuts. By this time, the other actors had solo hits to their name. Shah Rukh, on the other hand, began in two-hero films (Deewana, King Uncle) and then even played the villain (Darr, Anjaam). Yet he was able to bridge the gap and soon draw level with Aamir and Salman. Throughout the 90s, the three Khans were the top leading actors in Hindi films, with SRK and Salman ahead of Aamir.

Notably, The tide turned as the century turned. From 2000-07, Salman faced fluctuating fortunes at the ticket-window. He had a spate of flops and only intermittent successes in No Entry and Partner. Aamir became more selective and gave four years to a single movie - Mangal Pandey, which did not fare too well. Shah Rukh, on the other hand, had his golden run, giving era-defining hits like Mohabbatein, Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham, Devdas, Kal Ho Naa Ho, Veer Zaara, and Om Shanti Om, all in succession. During this period, he collected a staggering ₹ 1326 crore rupees at the ticket-window, more than what Aamir and Salman made combined.

As per the latest buzz, 2008-09 was when the scenario changed again. Aamir’s Ghajini established the 100-crore rupees club, while Salman entered his ‘bhai’ era with Wanted and Dabangg. Over the next six years, the two actors drew level with Shah Rukh. SRK still had the big hits such as Chennai Express and Happy New Year, but Salman and Aamir had greater cultural impact with seminal films like Dabangg, Ek Tha Tiger, 3 Idiots, and PK. The ticket-window earnings were similar for all three actors.

In further updates, And then came the worst phase of Shah Rukh’s career. After 2015, none of Shah Rukh’s films was a clean hit. He had the odd success in Dilwale or Raees, but they did not do the numbers his contemporaries did. Around the same time, Aamir was ruling the roost with Dangal, while Salman was also smashing ticket-window records with Sultan and Bajrangi Bhaijaan. Even Akshay Kumar, with a spate of hits, out-collected Shah Rukh at the ticket-window during this time.

On top of that, The Covid pandemic changed the dynamics of how Indian audiences consume cinema. The arrival of OTT meant theatres were challenged for the first time. Both Salman and Aamir faced challenges as their films, Laal Singh Chaddha and Radhey, tanked at the ticket-window. Akshay Kumar faced similar challenges with a string of flops before he recovered. Shah Rukh, on the other hand, spent the first few years of the post-pandemic era on hiatus before smashing records in 2023.

Despite working in only three films since 2020, he is the second-highest-grossing Indian star during the period, behind a Dhurandhar-led Ranveer Singh. His ₹ 2671 crore rupees gross during this period far outstrips Salman ( ₹ 902 crore rupees) and Aamir ( ₹ 359 crore rupees). In the process, he has taken his lifetime cumulative ticket-window haul to a staggering ₹ 8000 crore rupees, drawing level with Salman Khan. Aamir is still at around ₹ 6600 crore rupees, but with fewer films.

title: A.R. Rahman becomes the new face of Brooke Bond Taj Mahal Tea; Oscar-Winning composer launches ‘Awaken Your Masterpiece’ campaign
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The composer features in a new campaign movie that explores how a purposeful pause over a cup of tea can help overcome creative blocks and rediscover inspiration.

Adding to this, Known for his contribution to Indian music and his work across international projects, Rahman joins the brand in a partnership centred on creativity, dedication and the pursuit of excellence. Taj Mahal Tea, which has been associated with the idea of fine craftsmanship for over six decades, has built its identity around the phrase ‘Hazaaron Mein Ek’ and its iconic ‘Wah Taj!’ signature. The association with Rahman brings together the worlds of music and tea, with the brand drawing parallels between the composer’s creative process and its own approach to selecting and blending tea leaves.

Meanwhile, The new campaign, ‘Awaken Your Masterpiece’, explores the role of taking a purposeful break during the creative process. In the campaign movie, Rahman is seen experiencing a creative block before turning to a freshly brewed cup of Taj Mahal Tea. The pause inspires him to rediscover his creative flow, eventually leading to an uplifting melody and a joyful ‘Wah Taj!’. Through the movie, the brand highlights how moments of stillness can help creators regain clarity and find inspiration.

Notably, Commenting on the association, Ishtpreet Singh, VP Beverages, HUL, shared, "Over decades, Taj Mahal Tea and music have been inseparable, a bond that began with the legendary Ustad Zakir Hussain and the iconic 'Wah Taj!'. As we carry that legacy forward, there could be no better custodian than A.R. Rahman, an artist whose genius is truly one in a thousand. Just as his music comes from finding the perfect note among countless possibilities, every cup of Taj Mahal is crafted from tea leaves carefully selected from thousands, blended to create a taste that stands apart. That is what makes Taj Mahal Tea Hazaaron Mein Ek 'Wah Taj!'."

As per the latest buzz, Speaking about the creative direction behind the campaign, Harshad Rajadhyaksha and Kainaz Karmakar, Group Chief Creative Officers, Ogilvy India, shared, "Music and Taj Mahal Chai have been inseparable. It has been a beautiful journey of building a brand with music at its core and we're thrilled to partner with A R Rahman this year. The brand story of finesse and the search for excellence sits really well with everything that A R Rahman stands for. The campaign is led by our team, Fritz Gonsalves and Jayesh Raut. The movie is shot by Prakash Varma (Nirvana films), who has been an integral part of the visual language of the brand for over a decade now."

In further updates, The campaign continues Taj Mahal Tea’s association with music, which previously featured legendary tabla maestro Ustad Zakir Hussain. With Rahman now joining the brand, the latest initiative seeks to extend that legacy by celebrating creativity and the pursuit of artistic excellence.

title: Shah Rukh Khan turns 61: A back injury forced him to quit sports for theatre; his first role was as a monkey in Ram Leela
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Shah Rukh Khan’s journey from Delhi to Mumbai and his rise to become one of Hindi cinema’s biggest stars continue to inspire aspiring actors. But the superstar, who has sustained his stardom for decades, did not always dream of becoming an star. In fact, he was more drawn to sports and played cricket, football and hockey. A back injury, however, forced him to give up his sporting ambitions and eventually led him to theatre. That interest in acting opened the doors to television and, later, films.

Adding to this, Shah Rukh Khan once opened up about his journey to becoming an star. As Shah Rukh Khan celebrates his 61st birthday today, we look back at this lesser-known chapter of his life and how an unexpected turn of events set him on the path to becoming an star.

Meanwhile, In a 1994 interview with The Week, the star spoke about the circumstances that led him to pursue acting. He shared, "I am quite educated. I gave up the idea of being an engineer. I did the economics course. I could have done my MBA after that. I was good enough for that, with my marks.... I gave that up and enrolled for mass communication. To me, it was important that I should know all the aspects of a newspaper."

Notably, Talking about his love for sports and how he eventually turned to acting, he shared, "I was good at cricket, football and hockey. I used to play at the state level; but I hurt my back. So I joined acting. I used to do that in school. Somewhere along the line I felt this is the aspect of creativity that I like. I can write a little. I have done a lot of theatre for six years, semi-professionally. It was important for me to keep myself in this kind of field. I did my first role in a Ram Leela as a monkey. I have always enjoyed it. I feel that an star is an overgrown kid. So, I am still living my childhood. To be a child all your life is the greatest boon."

As per the latest buzz, Shah Rukh studied economics at Hansraj College in Delhi. During his college years, he developed an interest in theatre and joined Delhi's Theatre Action Group (TAG), where he trained under theatre director Barry John.
In further updates, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Amar Talwar (@amarthetalwar)

On top of that, Shah Rukh began his acting career on television in the late 1980s. Although he had first started shooting for Lekh Tandon's Dil Dariya, production delays meant that Fauji, which went on air in 1989, became his television debut. He later appeared in Aziz Mirza's show Circus, followed by other shows such as Umeed and Wagle Ki Duniya.

Shah Rukh's big-screen debut came with Deewana in 1992, in which he starred alongside Rishi Kapoor and Divya Bharti. The movie was a box-office success and collected him the Filmfare Award for Best Male Debut.

title: AR Rahman calls composing Ramayana music an honour, jokes about not everybody liking his work
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

AR Rahman brought his Wonderment Tour to India with a sold-out concert at Mumbai’s Jio World Garden on Sunday, November 1. The singer-composer performed in front of 10,000 people, bringing them some of his greatest hits. During the three-hour concert, Rahman also spoke about composing the music for the soon-to-release movie Ramayana , while taking a jibe at the criticism of its soundtrack.

Adding to this, AR Rahman performed at Mumbai's Jio World Garden as part of his Wonderment Tour. (Photo by FleckMedia) Rahman talks Ramayana and criticism On Sunday evening, Rahman played some of his biggest hits in a three-hour show in Mumbai, the first of his India leg of the Wonderment Tour. In the middle of the concert, Rahman had his team perform Mangal Rang, the track from Ramayana rolled out last month. Before the song was performed, the composer spoke about the movie. “The biggest Indian movie is set to come out, Ramayana,” he shared, adding, “It's an honour to serve my country, to serve such belief in India.”

Meanwhile, In conversation with the audience from the stage, Rahman added, “With whatever little talent I have, I'll use that to bring beauty into the music and the soundtrack. They say now, if everybody likes your work, get out from that place.”

Notably, Rahman’s comment came after mixed responses to Mangal Rang and other songs in the Ramayana soundtrack. Many have shared the songs are similar to Rahman’s earlier compositions, while others have shared that the upbeat vocals and beats in Jai Jai Ram evoke a sports track. Many have even compared Mangal Rang to Kun Faaya, Rahman’s composition from Rockstar, saying a Sufi-esque track looked out of place in Ramayana.

As per the latest buzz, Last week, while speaking with Hindustan Times, Rahman had addressed the reactions. “We do so much work, filtration, ideation, and iteration that there's no energy left to look at feedback! We just put it out because it's been tried and tested so much. My son keeps telling me, 'This is what they shared yesterday, now they're apologising...' I say fine, I've done my work sincerely and hope people celebrate it,” he had shared.

In further updates, The music for Ramayana is composed by Rahman alongside Hans Zimmer, who is making his Indian movie debut. Talking about collaborating with the legendary composer, Rahman had told Hindustan Times: “Him coming onto the project is such a blessing because it changes the narrative. If someone in New Zealand or Europe sees Hans Zimmer's name, they will watch. If they just see Indian names, they might think it's just another Indian movie, but they'll be curious to see what he has done collaborating on this. It's a great move by the producer.”

On top of that, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Ramayana and directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is a two-part movie starring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Yash as Ravana, and Sai Pallavi as Sita. Part One releases worldwide on November 5, ahead of Diwali. The second part is slated for rollout around Diwali 2027.

AR Rahman, meanwhile, performed at Jio World Garden, Mumbai on November 1. Following this, he will perform at the Backyard Sports Club, Gurgaon on November 21, as part of his Wonderment Tour. The three-hour musical experience brings together some of his most iconic 90s compositions alongside his contemporary work, with a large-scale live production and international ensemble.

title: After ₹342-crore box office run, Hanuman Ansh makers issue stern warning over film rights, say no individual can claim independent authority
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

The team behind Hanuman Ansh has issued a strong statement clarifying who has the authority to handle the movie's rights, publicity and official communication. Swambhu Media Network Pvt. Ltd. has shared that no individual can independently represent the movie or make decisions on its behalf. The clarification comes amid reports and discussions surrounding the movie, which is based on the life of Neem Karoli Baba, also known as Maharaj ji. The production house has made it clear that all decisions concerning the movie must follow the agreements signed between its producers. It has also warned against any unauthorised claims or dealings made in the movie's name.

Adding to this, Hanuman Ansh makers name four official producers, warn against unauthorised award claims and business deals. Who are the official producers of Hanuman Ansh? Swambhu Media Network has named Namrata G Singh, Dr. Vishal Chaturvedi, Ragini Sona and Anupriya Nagar as the four official producers of Hanuman Ansh. According to the company, all rights related to the movie, including theatrical, OTT, television, music, gaming and licensing rights in India and overseas, are governed by agreements between the producers.

Meanwhile, The statement further says that decisions involving publicity, award nominations, business partnerships and commercial rights cannot be taken independently by any one person. Such matters require approval from the producers and must be handled through the company's official channels. The company has also clarified that any independent agreements, public statements or claims regarding awards made without the required approval will not be recognised or considered binding.

Notably, View this post on Instagram The statement read, “The Company is aware that an individual is representing themselves as authorised to deal with the rights in the Movie. No individual holds that authority. All rights in the Movie (theatrical, streaming, broadcast, music, gaming, licensing, etc.), in India and Internationally, are dealt with only through the process set out in the inter-se agreements executed amongst the Producers.”

As per the latest buzz, To avoid confusion over who can speak on behalf of the movie, Namrata G Singh and Dr. Vishal Chaturvedi have been appointed the only Executive Directors authorised to look after its public relations, marketing, awards and strategic partnerships.

In further updates, The production house has also addressed the movie's cast and crew, asking them to seek approval before making public appearances or speaking about the project. This includes interviews, podcasts, YouTube shows and other promotional platforms. Anyone wishing to participate in such engagements must first get in touch with the authorised team and receive formal confirmation.

On top of that, “No party acting alone has authority to deal in the Movie. Any such dealing is invalid and not binding on the Company or the Producers. Any statement, award claim or business arrangement made outside this process is not recognised by the Company. Those who engage outside it do so entirely at their own risk,” it further read.

Explaining why the movie's rights and association need to be protected, Executive Directors Namrata G Singh and Dr. Vishal Chaturvedi shared, “Hanuman Ansh belongs to Maharaj ji’s devotees across the world. Our duty is to protect it, and to give every partner one clear and verified door to the Movie.” The company has further warned that it will take necessary action across territories against any attempt to misuse the movie's name, credits or intellectual property.

title: CBFC issues new advisory for filmmakers: No incomplete movies allowed, titles subject to change, release dates not considered
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The Central Board of Movie Certification rolled out a new advisory dated October 26, 2026, for filmmakers seeking certification. Signed by Rajendra Singh, chief executive officer of the CBFC , the new advisory makes it clear that incomplete works will not be encouraged, titles are subject to change, and revealed rollout dates will not be taken into consideration.

Adding to this, The CBFC will no longer encourage incomplete films and encourages filmmakers to plan their submissions in advance. This comes after 18 new members were revealed to constitute the board, for the first time since 2017. Preity Zinta, Pankaj Tripathi, Suniel Shetty, Pallavi Joshi, Ricky Kej, and Supriya Yarlagadda are among its members.
Meanwhile, ( Full list of the 18 members of the newly formed CBFC: Preity Zinta, Pankaj Tripathi, Suniel Shetty, others )

Notably, In the advisory, the CBFC mentions that films submitted for certification must be in their final form, including final graphics, background score and music, accessibility features, and more. Applications with incomplete prints, placeholder graphics, and missing elements will be treated as non-compliant. Such applications will be delayed or rejected. The date on which the application is approved as complete will be regarded as the date of receipt of the application.

As per the latest buzz, Irrespective of the title used during promotions and submitted in the application, the CBFC advisory states that it shall not be considered final. The title is also liable to scrutiny, review and modification by the examining or revising committee. This is per guidelines issued under Section 5B(1) of the Cinematograph Act, 1952 (as amended from time to time) and Rule 25 of the Cinematograph (Certification) Rules, 2024.

In further updates, The same holds true for any revealed rollout date. The advisory states that the revealed rollout date will not be taken into account while processing films. The certification will follow due process, procedure and timelines under the extant Act and Rules. Filmmakers have been reminded that examination, review and certification by the examining and revising committee fall under this due process. The CBFC will not be liable for any self-imposed rollout schedules, says the advisory.
On top of that, Filmmakers have been asked to submit applications well in advance of any intended rollout date to give the CBFC proper time to examine the movie and issue directions for any changes.

Tamil Nadu chief minister Vijay ’s Jana Nayagan’s delayed certification is one of the highly-publicised incidents of a tussle between filmmakers and the CBFC, with the filmmaker even taking the board to court but receiving no relief. Diljit Dosanjh’s Satluj, formerly titled Punjab ‘95 was never cleared for rollout and was quietly dropped on Zee5. It was taken down within hours. The CBFC issued new guidelines in September,

title: Amitabh Bachchan greets fans at Jalsa behind bulletproof glass amid security threats; Abhishek Bachchan stays close by during Sunday tradition
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

title: Exclusive| Dia Mirza on cracker free Diwali video being taken down by BMC: Video was recorded in the interest of public awareness
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Dia Mirza The BMC had appealed to citizens to avoid bursting firecrackers and celebrate an environment-friendly Diwali following a Bombay High Court directive amid rising air pollution in the city. As part of the campaign, the civic body roped in several celebrities, including Dia Mirza, Madhuri Dixit and cricketer Ajinkya Rahane, to record video messages urging people to celebrate a pollution-free festival.
Adding to this, In a post on X, Ameet Satam wrote, “We don’t need lessons on how to celebrate Diwali from Dia Mirza Our traditions are deeply rooted in our culture.”

Meanwhile, In conversation with us Dia says, “Diwali celebrates the triumph of light over darkness, knowledge over ignorance, and hope over despair. The video was recorded in the interest of public awareness, with the intention of encouraging a healthier and more mindful celebration. Air pollution is a matter of public health, and every effort towards reducing it is a step towards a better environment for all.”

Notably, Last week after The Bombay High Court urged celebrities to support Maharashtra’s anti-firecracker campaign without payment, Dia had told us, “I have never charged any money for any public service campaigns. No idea who has been paid hefty amounts. The point is, celebrities are willing to work with civil society and governments if there is a priority to solve the very solve-able issue of pollution. Every time we speak up against cracker use we get attacked. I have been focusing on drawing attention on air quality for over a decade.”

title: EXCLUSIVE: Amit Sadh calls his Pratap character “Mike Tyson of police force”; admits BO success matters to him more than ever: “I am told even Instagram followers’ matter. Toh yeh toh box office hai yaar!”
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

How has the response to the trailer been? The trailer is crucial as it’s always the first step. It is the most important asset, almost like a visiting card for a movie. In that regard, it has done pretty well. People have liked the trailer. They can see it’s a content-driven movie, so it’s very satisfying.

Adding to this, You play a brash cop in Pratap . Interestingly, you played a somewhat similar police officer in the web series Breathe as well. How did you ensure that the two characters didn't look similar? Interesting question! The first thing director Sachin Saraf told me when we met was, ‘I loved what you have done in Breathe, but this character is different’. I replied, ‘Of course. That’s why I am meeting you’!

Meanwhile, What we also need to understand is that Pratap is a story written for cinema. And I am sure you understand the difference between a character written for a movie and one written for a web series. There’s a difference. Pratap is different from my character in Breathe. He has different complexities. That was the fun part. If it were the same, I would definitely not have done it. And here’s a guy who is larger-than-life. In fact, he’s the Mike Tyson of the police force! I just finished watching his documentary. So, that name is on top of my mind, but that’s the best parallel I can draw.

Notably, How did you arrive at Pratap 's look? We have rarely seen you sporting a moustache... I had one in Kai Po Che (2013) and also in Super 30 (2019). And yes, that was the idea. I like building my characters. The audience has loved that aspect of my preparation.

As per the latest buzz, I like getting into the physicality of a character. I wanted him to look strong and tagda , but not chiselled. But that’s all the paintwork of an artist or an star. At the end of the day, we have to respond to the script. So, that’s what I was doing, and I worked according to what my director wanted from me.

In further updates, Do you follow the ticket-window and check the collections of your films on a daily basis? For sure. Apni movie ke liye toh karna hi padega na ? If you work in an office, you won't say, ‘I'll work whether or not I get my salary’! Of course, you'll check whether your salary has been credited on the first day of the month.

On top of that, A lot of money is riding on the movie. This is a double-edged sword for me right now and also a beautiful moment in my career. I am at a crossroads, and here I have a chance to come out and bring an interesting kind of storytelling to the audience. I hope they become curious about me, my personality, my past and my present, so that they decide to watch the movie in cinemas. So, yes, it will matter.

Nowadays, I am told that even Instagram followers matter. Toh yeh toh ticket-window hai yaar ! People who cast actors based on Instagram followers, that's their destiny. But ticket-window matters. The producers have to make money for things to move forward. Otherwise, I'll go back in the food chain. Ultimately, what we make has to sell. So, it does matter a lot, especially now.

title: Sanjay Gupta's wife urges people to excuse daughter after she showed middle finger to paparazzi, calls it 'expressions of grieving children’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta died at the age of 59 after suffering a fatal head injury in an accidental fall at his home in Versova, Mumbai. Hours after his death, a video from his funeral surfaced online, showing his daughter, Dalai, giving the middle finger to paparazzi waiting outside. Now, the filmmaker's wife, Anuradha Lekhi Gupta, has addressed the widely shared video.

Adding to this, Sanjay Gupta's daughter faced criticism for showing middle finger to paparazzi. Sanjay Gupta's wife addresses daughter Dalai's widely shared video At the funeral, as the family was preparing to leave, Sanjay's daughter was seen sitting in the front seat of the car, covering her face with her jacket as paparazzi gathered around the vehicle. She was soon seen showing them the middle finger before briefly smiling and covering her face again. The video drew mixed reactions online, with some users criticising her gesture while others urged the paparazzi to give the grieving family space and respect their privacy.

Meanwhile, On Monday, filmmaker Milap Zaveri posted on Instagram and put up a post by Anuradha Lekhi Gupta, which read, "A part of our lives has been lost forever, and nothing can ever fill the void or make up for this loss. On behalf of our family, I wish to express my heartfelt gratitude to all our family members, friends, Sanjay's followers and our friends in the media for the love, condolences and strength you have extended to us during this difficult time. Sanjay suffered a fatal head injury in an accidental fall, which led to his untimely demise. Sanjay loved his family and children immensely. Our children are adolescents who have suddenly lost their beloved father."

Notably, She further addressed the criticism surrounding her daughter, Dalai, and the widely shared video. She wrote, “Having grown up away from the glare of the limelight and the intrusive nature of paparazzi culture, they were deeply distressed by the sudden intrusion into their privacy at such a difficult time. In their grief and anguish, some of their reactions may have been directed towards certain members of the media. I sincerely regret any hurt this may have caused.”
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Milap Zaveri (@milapzaveri)

In further updates, Anuradha also issued an appeal, urging people to be sensitive towards her children's emotional state. She added, "I humbly request everyone to understand these reactions for what they truly are: the expressions of grieving children struggling to come to terms with an irreparable loss. I request you to kindly excuse them, and appeal to everyone to delete any content that may leave lasting emotional scars on their young minds. Please allow them the privacy, compassion and space they need to grieve the loss of their father."

On top of that, Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta, best known for directing films such as Kaante, Shootout at Lokhandwala, Shootout at Wadala and Kaabil, died on October 30 at his Mumbai residence. He was 59. Sanjay suffered a fatal head injury after accidentally falling at his home. His family discovered him the following morning and rushed him to a nearby hospital, where he was declared dead. His sudden demise has left the movie industry shocked, with several actors and filmmakers mourning his loss.

title: Amitabh Bachchan slams media outlet for twisting his Lord Krishna invocation
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

New Delhi, The usually restrained Amitabh Bachchan on Monday took on a media outlet for misrepresenting his words in the praise of Lord Krishna, saying in an angry post that 10 per cent of his 50 million follower base is enough to strike back and is just waiting for his signal.

Adding to this, Amitabh Bachchan slams media outlet for twisting his Lord Krishna invocation His post on October 29 was simply an invocation to Lord Krishna, Bachchan wrote on social media platforms. He had shared then, "Go bring your elephants, we will also... Haathi ghoda palki, Jai Kanhaiya Lal ki."
Meanwhile, The media outlet reported it saying that Bachchan was challenging his opponents by telling them, "Bring your elephants and horses."

Notably, "For Krishna Kanhaiya, in the form of prayer, it's often chanted -'Haathi ghoda palki, Jai Kanhaiya Lal ki ' And the media, by disrespecting it, prints it for their own publicity...," a furious Bachchan responded in Hindi.
As per the latest buzz, This, he shared, was not only a "grave insult" to the 'Jai Shri Krishna' invocation but also a deliberate attempt to twist his words.

In further updates, "Listen up, media folks, with your ears wide open... There is a 50 million-strong follower base, media folks. The day I give the signal, just 10 per cent of them are ready and waiting to strike. ."

On top of that, The 84-year-old superstar, one of the earliest in the industry to take blogging seriously, posts everyday without fail. The posts, sometimes ambiguous, are often greetings, personal details, movie nostalgia or a diary of how his day went. He often refers to his over 50 million followers across platforms as extended family, or ef.

"The more you twist my words and condemn them, the 100 times greater capacity the Ef has lying in wait to do the same. ... It's just a matter of them speaking up," he added on X in his post in the early hours of Monday.

title: ‘Protests are democratic right’: RSS opts for measured response to Oppn stir
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

As the Opposition intensifies protests against the government and chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities, leaders of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), the ideological fount of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), reiterated the public’s right to protest with a caveat that any such campaign should not be against national interest.

Adding to this, INDIA bloc leaders and people during the INDIA bloc's' Vote Bachao Desh Bachao' protest rally against alleged electoral irregularities and demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi (HT Photo) A senior RSS functionary shared the Sangh, which has of late concluded its centenary celebrations, did not want the youth to see the government as an adversary. “The Sangh believes in dialogue. For years the Sangh was politically and socially victimised, but we did not stop engagement with society,” the functionary shared, explaining the Sangh’s measured stance.

Meanwhile, “There can be concerns that need attention whether these are limited to a set of people or a state, but while the government’s accountability is fixed, society too must do its bit by not allowing vested interests to vitiate and mislead our youth,” he shared.

Notably, The cautious response follows internal feedback received about the union government’s handling of the students’ protest over paper leaks in July where the police were accused of using disproportionate force to disperse students as they tried to march to Parliament on July 20. The subsequent police action gave the Opposition leverage to attack the government in and outside Parliament.
As per the latest buzz, With assembly elections approaching across five states, including Uttar Pradesh and Punjab, the RSS is keen to prevent youth discontent from consolidating.

In further updates, To be sure, the RSS has not commented on the November 1 rally by Opposition parties at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan that has been branded by the BJP as a “calculated conspiracy to plunge the nation into anarchy, in the name of democracy”.

On top of that, But a day before the big gathering in the heart of the national capital, the RSS, which is meeting for its annual Akhil Bharatiya Karyakari Mandal Baithak in Indore, reiterated its position on the ongoing protests and the Opposition’s campaign.

Sunil Ambekar, the chief spokesperson of the Sangh, in response to a question on whether the organisation’s outreach towards the Gen Z was delayed, shared, while citizens have every right to question issues of national concern, national interest is paramount.

title: Shah Rukh Khan's superstardom has survived a newfound reclusive nature, the Dilip Kumar-Rajinikanth blueprint may ensure it sustains
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Superstardom in Indian cinema is a curious thing. Retroactively, Dilip Kumar and Ashok Kumar have been called that, but Rajesh Khanna was the first Bollywood star for whom the term was used. And within five years of him being called that, the star was struggling to land hits. In a decade, he was almost obsolete. Since then, sustaining superstardom has been key. Many Indian superstars have faltered in their 50s, unable to adapt to changing times and losing their grip on the masses.

Adding to this, King will be Shah Rukh Khan's first rollout since he turned 60 last year. Strangely enough, Shah Rukh Khan has had no such trouble. Despite facing a turbulent time at the ticket-window, followed by a period of uncharacteristic reclusion, he remains the audience’s favourite. As he turns 61 today (November 2), the star sits at a crucial juncture in his career. It is what he does next that will determine how this superstardom continues, and he has just the blueprint he needs.

Meanwhile, SRK’s fame was built on love. Amitabh Bachchan was respected, Rajinikanth inspired awe, and Chiranjeevi was aspirational. But Shah Rukh was loved, quite like Rajesh Khanna had been in his day. The love he got from audiences of all ages and social sections was unparalleled. Women, in particular, have been his strongest supporters since the 90s. That love was independent of what he did at the ticket-window. It was for SRK, the man. They saw in him an ideal friend, an ideal lover, a devoted husband, a caring father, and a charming man all round. Hence, when the films began to falter and fail around 2016-17, Shah Rukh’s stardom did not dim.

Notably, Most other stars would have found it hard to get audiences to theatres had they returned from a five-year break with their last rollout being Zero. But Shah Rukh gave Pathaan and Jawan, two ₹ 1000-crore rupees hits. And it was on the back of his followers' support. Many went to watch these films just for SRK. No agenda! That unwavering loyalty is hard to manufacture. In the five years since his son Aryan Khan’s arrest and rollout, Shah Rukh has become a media recluse. A man who loved interviews has given none to Indian media. In the age of podcasts and long-form interviews, he has none in India. His only exchanges with followers are now only on X (Twitter). And yet, this reclusion has not dented his stardom a bit.

As per the latest buzz, Strangely enough, the love for SRK , the man, extends despite his occasional failings. Most of Shah Rukh’s supporters are liberal millennials. They see in him a left-to-centre progressive figure. And yet, his followers are not just willing to stand by him but also to excuse him for ‘transgressions’ they would not allow others to commit. It doesn’t matter whether SRK endorses a gutkha brand or does not post in support of student protests. All is forgiven for King Khan, it seems.

In further updates, Stardom can survive flops when it is built on love for the man, and not just the craft. But SRK, the brand, is built on cinema. And it is cinema that will determine if his legacy in work can continue to be a story of success. It has been three years since his annus mirabilis - 2023- which gave him Pathaan, Jawan, and Dunki (the last with an asterisk). Now, he must again mount a comeback - with Siddharth Anand’s King. There are no other movies in the pipeline. King’s success, or failure, will determine how Shah Rukh navigates his stardom in his 60s. And he need not look far for inspiration.

On top of that, He idolises Amitabh Bachchan, but if Shah Rukh has followed a blueprint for stardom, it’s one of Dilip Kumar. The Tragedy King began as a romantic hero in the 1940s, before establishing himself as a dramatic star. Shah Rukh would do the same four decades later. He even did the same kind of films, playing lovable, tragic heroes. In his 50s, Dilip Kumar faced his first failure as films such as Bairaag and Sagina flopped. Dilip Kumar took a five-year hiatus and returned with a bang in Kranti, an action potboiler. Shah Rukh did the same with Pathaan and Jawan. In his 60s, Dilip Kumar, the once-lovable romantic star, turned action hero, starring in mega films that featured large ensemble casts. Both Vidhaata and Karma were blockbusters, while Mashaal and Saudagar were also big hits. For a while, in the mid-80s, Dilip Kumar, 65, was a bigger box-office draw than Bachchan at his peak. This is what Shah Rukh would aspire to do. But there is a chance of failure too.

Rajinikanth is an example. After lording it over Tamil cinema in the 1990s and 2000s, Rajinikanth faced setbacks in his 60s. The back-to-back failures of Kochadaiiyaan and Lingaa led people to say that the superstar was ‘finished’. He roared back with Kabali and 2.0, before re-establishing himself as Tamil cinema’s top star in his 70s with hits such as Jailer, Coolie, and Jailer 2. Rajinikanth transformed the kind of roles he took on. He was now the vengeful grandfather, the retired jailer, the veteran cop. There was no romance with women in their 30s (or even 40s). He was still the hero, but close to his age.

title: Divya Dutta recalls how Shah Rukh Khan guided her on Veer Zaara sets | Interview
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

As Shah Rukh Khan celebrates his 61st birthday today, followers across the world are marking the occasion, from lighting up the Burj Khalifa to gathering outside his Mumbai home, Mannat . The star, who has been Bollywood's defining romantic hero for decades, has given audiences several memorable love stories, with Yash Chopra's Veer Zaara remaining one of his most cherished romantic dramas. In an exclusive interaction with Hindustan Times, Divya Dutta , who played a pivotal role in the movie, looks back at working with Shah Rukh, calling it a career-high and recalling how the superstar guided her during a scene.

Adding to this, Divya Dutta played a pivotal role in Shah Rukh Khan-starrer Veer Zaara. 'Veer Zaara was a huge high for me' Speaking about how Veer Zaara was a dream come true for her, Divya shared, "It was my childhood dream to work with Yash Chopra — I used to day dream about it without knowing how it would ever happen. Being on his set in Veer Zaara was a huge high for me. That was the movie that brought me my first major commercial recognition where people knew my name."

Meanwhile, Talking about the joy of working with her 'absolute favourite', Shah Rukh, in the movie, Divya shared, "It was also my first movie with Shah Rukh, who happens to be my absolute favourite. It was a complete joy working on those sets and learning so much. Plus, I got to share screen space with Zohra Sehgal — she was the epitome of grace, chutzpah, and mischief. Sharing the screen with someone as full of life as her was unforgettable."

Notably, When asked if she had a specific memory of Shah Rukh Khan from the sets of Veer Zaara, Divya recalled how the star guided her during a shot. She shared, "During Veer Zaara, I was so excited just to be there. I remember filming a shot where I wasn't facing the camera properly. Shah Rukh was rehearsing his lines nearby, and he gently came over and whispered, 'This was just a rehearsal; in the actual take, be a little more camera-aware'."

As per the latest buzz, She added, "When I thanked him, he shared, 'Yeah, look out for yourself, because I won't be on every set to guide you.' It felt so wonderful that a superstar like Shah Rukh Khan was looking out for me. Both Shah Rukh and Manoj Bajpayee have that magnanimity in them, and that is what people around them always remember." Divya of late starred in Netflix's Gajab Raat with Manoj Bajpayee.

In further updates, Veer Zaara was directed by Yash Chopra and written by Aditya Chopra. Rolled out on November 12, 2004, the movie starred Shah Rukh Khan as Veer Pratap Singh, an Indian Air Force pilot, and Preity Zinta as Zaara Hayaat Khan, a young Pakistani woman. Their lives become intertwined after Veer rescues Zaara, and the story follows their love, separation and sacrifice over two decades.

title: Amitabh Bachchan slams reports ‘twisting’ his words, portraying his post as challenge to enemies; issues strict warning
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Amitabh Bachchan hit back at media reports for allegedly misinterpreting his recent social media post and portraying it as a challenge to his opponents. The star clarified that his reference to elephants, horses and a palanquin in an earlier post was part of a devotional chant dedicated to Lord Krishna, rather than a message directed at his critics.

Adding to this, Amitabh Bachchan slams reports claiming he challenged his enemies. Amitabh Bachchan slams media reports On October 29, Big B had shared pictures and videos from his Sunday darshan and written in Hindi, "Now watch how they turn this into a headline!!!! Don't try to scare us, my friend. If you stop writing about us, that's no problem. We have our own newspaper running here now. You do one, and we'll do a hundred!!!! Go on! Bring your elephants and horses... We'll bring ours too – Haathi ghoda palki, Jai Kanhaiya Lal ki! (an elephant, a horse and a palanquin, glory to Lord Krishna!) ...!!!!"

Meanwhile, On November 2, Big B took to his blog to criticise media reports for 'twisting his words' and portraying his earlier post as an 'open challenge' to his enemies. He wrote in Hindi, "In praise of Lord Krishna, people often chant the following prayer: 'Hathi ghoda palki, Jai Kanhaiya Lal ki (An elephant, a horse and a palanquin – glory to Lord Krishna!)' But the media has disrespected this devotional chant and, to promote itself, published headlines suggesting: 'Look, Amitabh is challenging his opponents, saying, 'Bring your elephants and horses; we will fight with our weapons and will not be afraid!'"

Notably, He called it a "gross insult" to a chant celebrating Jai Shri Krishna and added, "second, a deliberate twisting of words to make it seem as though I am challenging my opponents. Listen carefully, members of the media! We have a following of 50 million people. The day I give the signal, even just 10 per cent of them will be ready to take action. Our EF has the capacity to do a hundred times more than the criticism you direct at us by twisting our words. They are only waiting for me to give the word."

As per the latest buzz, Big B then shared the headline of a Hindi news report, which translates to, "Amitabh Bachchan takes a dig at opponents over their threats, vents his anger through a cryptic post – 'Go on, bring your elephants and horses'."

In further updates, He further called the reports an insult to religion and wrote, "Have you seen this? An insult to religion, and...- Betuka – Absurd, nonsensical or silly, Hasyaspad – Ridiculous or laughable (invoking derision) and Asangat – Inconsistent or illogical. These are the people who are considered the country's fifth column. The other four columns are regarded with respect and honour in our traditions. The fifth is called so because its members are given respect and a place of honour in society by the people of the country!"

On top of that, The star concluded, “Respect??? Nothing could be more ridiculous... If we make a mistake – and mistakes do happen – we immediately apologise and try to correct it. But here, it seems they believe that being this way is their birthright...I was about to speak about the affection and love of a person who is in pain before going to sleep. But I will not call myself a victim. The right to speak about my pain belongs to me alone. It is not something meant for you, the media.”

A bomb threat email allegedly targeting veteran star Amitabh Bachchan's bungalow in Mumbai was reported to the Mumbai Police last week. The threatening email was received by a school in Mumbai's Bandra-Kurla Complex (BKC) area. The police have launched an investigation into the matter.

title: Ramayana advance booking blazes past ₹75 crore as release day approaches; Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film now outpacing Animal, KGF 2
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

As the rollout day approaches for Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana , the advance bookings have finally opened in full flow. For about 10 days, a deadlock between the makers and exhibitors over revenue sharing had curtailed the advance bookings. But over the weekend, that was resolved, opening up more screens, including the crucial single screens. This has seen the movie register huge jumps in advance bookings in India, while the overseas numbers continue to impress.

Adding to this, Ramayana will rollout worldwide on November 5. How Ramayana advance bookings are faring Advance bookings for Ramayana opened on Dussehra, 15 full days before its global rollout. But for the next 10 days, only the Hindi version had extensive shows. And there, too, most of the single-screen and smaller centres were yet to open. But on Friday, the stalemate between the exhibitors and distributors ended as terms were reached. Since then, more theatres are opening pre-sales for the movie across India each hour.

Meanwhile, By Monday morning, the number of screens for the movie had increased to 3,500, with 1,000 added in the last two days. By the morning of November 2, three days before its rollout, the movie had grossed ₹ 37 crore rupees in pre-sales in India. This included an impressive ₹ 22 crore rupees from the opening day itself. The remainder is spread over its extended weekend. The Hindi version continues to lead the way, but the Kannada and Telugu versions are rapidly gaining ground now. As of Monday morning, the Kannada version had sold tickets worth almost ₹ 4 crore rupees, while the Telugu version had also crossed ₹ 2 crore rupees.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ramayana: Rise of a Legend (@ramayanamovie)

As per the latest buzz, Ramayana has now sold almost 9 lakh tickets in pre-sales across India. The premium formats - including IMAX - are driving the sales, accounting for almost one-fourth of the sales, despite holding just 4% of the screens. This pace is faster than the lead actors' previous big hits. Ramayana is now outpacing both Ranbir Kapoor 's Animal and Yash 's KGF Chapter 2. However, it remains behind Dhurandhar 2, RRR, and Pushpa 2 so far.

In further updates, What has helped Ramayana’s case is the pre-sales buzz overseas. In North America, the movie will have paid previews on November 4, the eve of its rollout. The 24 hours after its world premiere saw the movie register a 27% jump in collections. By Monday morning, the movie had collected $3.9 million in overseas advance bookings, including over $1.5 million for the US paid previews alone. This takes the movie’s worldwide advance-booking gross to ₹ 75 crore rupees three days before its rollout.

On top of that, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The first part is scheduled for worldwide rollout on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2027. The films will rollout in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam across India.

Sony Pictures will handle global distribution, excluding India, while Dharma Productions will distribute the movie in the Hindi-speaking market. The movie is also planned for a worldwide IMAX rollout.
