title: Amitabh Bachchan mourns friend Sanjay Gupta's death, says unable to understand why all of this is happening
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood filmmaker Sanjay Gupta died at the age of 59 on Saturday morning, leaving the movie industry in shock. Several celebrities took to social media to pay tribute to him and mourn his death. Amitabh Bachchan , who worked with Sanjay on Kaante, also remembered the filmmaker with a heartfelt note.

Adding to this, Amitabh Bachchan mourns Sanjay Gupta's death. Amitabh Bachchan mourns the demise of Sanjay Gupta On Sunday, Big B took to his blog to mourn Sanjay's demise. Without naming the filmmaker, he wrote in Hindi, "A friend, a fellow artiste and a true devotee of art has left us at such a young age! I am unable to understand how all of this is happening."

Meanwhile, He further wrote, "Our dear companions from the world of art are being snatched away from us. What wrong have they done to deserve such a fate? People say that all the powerful planets in the solar system have turned unfavourable at the same time. Please have mercy on us! Those who are raining their wrath upon us – is this really fair? May all the planets in the solar system retreat to their respective homes and stay apart from one another. Perhaps then they will stop troubling all of us!"
Notably, Amitabh Bachchan worked with Sanjay in Kaante. The heist action thriller also featured Sanjay Dutt, Suniel Shetty, Lucky Ali, Mahesh Manjrekar, and Kumar Gaurav in lead roles.

As per the latest buzz, The filmmaker was found dead at his home in Versova on Saturday morning. According to the police, he appears to have fallen inside the house late on Friday night, sustaining a severe head injury. His wife and two children found him lying in a pool of blood when they woke up in the morning. They rushed him to a hospital, where he was declared dead.

In further updates, The Versova police have registered an accidental death report (ADR) in connection with the incident and are investigating to establish the exact sequence of events. According to the police, CCTV footage from the house shows that at around 2 am, Gupta, who was sitting in the drawing room, went to the kitchen, where he as per reports lost his balance and fell against a wall.

On top of that, The filmmaker was cremated on Sunday, with many Bollywood personalities paying their final respects at the funeral. Several Bollywood actors, including Sanjay Dutt, Anil Kapoor, Ajay Devgn, Vivek Oberoi and Hrithik Roshan, also took to social media to pen emotional tributes to the filmmaker.

Sharing the song, he wrote, "This era of love is bestowed upon the fortunate ones... Where roses bloom amidst the fragrance of gunpowder...Of Love and other Battles...This December, #LoveLikeAKing #TuMilJaaye song out now! #KING."

Meanwhile, The song shows Shah Rukh deeply in love with Deepika, listening intently to everything she has to say. The video opens with glimpses of their romance, interspersed with action sequences featuring Shah Rukh taking on his enemies using hand-to-hand combat and guns. One sequence also shows the star setting an entire place ablaze and ruthlessly killing his enemies with a sword. title: Yash says viewers will be able to relate with both Rama and Ravana in Ramayana, calls it the right time to showcase Indian film to the world
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Yash is excited for audience to see Ramayana , where he takes on the character of Ravana. The star, who has also co-produced the movie, is busy promoting the movie with the cast and crew these days. In a new interaction with Today Stars, Yash was seen with co-stars Ranbir Kapoor, Ravie Dubey and Rakul Preet Singh as they all shared their experience of working on this movie.

Adding to this, Yash at the Los Angeles premiere of Ramayana at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles. (Photo by VALERIE MACON / AFP) (AFP) What Yash shared about Ramayana Talking about Ramayana, Yash shared, “The interpretations of Ramayana is different in each state, different in each language. There are many interpretations and the beauty of our culture is that we see the story from everybody's point of view. Through Ravana's eyes also people have tried to depict the story. So, I feel the beauty of this story is very relatable. There are two aspects of it, when we want to achieve something we learn and dedicate ourselves to some skill. When we get it we become very powerful. After that, to maintain it is also important. In this story, Ravana is a learned scholar, musician and a warrior. But there are elements where the decisions that are made have a domino effect. That is beautifully depicted. One can relate to Rama, one can relate to Ravana… but how Rama has handled situations in life, that is something. To show that, we need Ravana.”
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by The World Of Ramayana (@worldoframayana)

He shared, “This is the right time to show Indian films to the world platform, like Korean cinema is really making a mark, so India deserves it. So we had that vision and everyone came together.”

title: Over 50 protesters briefly detained over ‘violations’ during INDIA bloc's Delhi rally
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Delhi Police shared over 50 protesters were briefly detained near Minto Road on Sunday for violating restrictions, even as the INDIA bloc’s rally, which drew tens of thousands of participants, unfolded peacefully and without any untoward incident.

Adding to this, Security personnel seen deployed at Connaught Place ahead of the INDIA bloc’s ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ march. (Sanchit Khanna/HT Photo) Police shared they made detentions after the rally as a few protesters went towards Minto Road, where restrictions were in place.

Meanwhile, More than 2,500 paramilitary personnel were deployed to ensure peace during the march. Police shared permission was granted for the Ramlila Maidan rally, not for the march from Connaught Place to the protest ground.
Notably, “With large crowds, we didn’t stop the march. We ensured that it navigated peacefully,” shared a police officer, part of the arrangement, who did not wish to be named.

As per the latest buzz, Police shared paramilitary deployment was retained in the New Delhi district area, with suspicion that protesters “swaying “ from the march and heading towards CP or other areas.
In further updates, The nearly 12-acre Ramlila Maidan, which can accommodate around 50,000 people, has eight entry and exit gates. One gate was reserved for the VVIPs.

On top of that, According to the security plan, the entire Ramlila Maidan was divided into eight regions and 14 zones. A deputy commissioner of police (DCP) or additional DCP-rank officer was in charge of each region and an assistant commissioner of police-rank officer of each zone. They were assisted by at least 25 inspectors and personnel between the ranks of sub-inspectors and constables.

Body-worn cameras and anti-riot measures were in place to deal with violence or untoward incidents. An additional 10 companies of the paramilitary forces and Delhi Police personnel were kept in reserve.

title: Cockroaches, Batman, cut-finger garlands: Protesters bring colour to INDIA bloc's anti-CEC march
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

By 11 am on Sunday, the Inner Circle of Connaught Place was already crowded with people ahead of the march to Ramlila Maidan, some 2km away, as part of the “Chalo Dilli” protest planned at noon. There were students, activists, political groups from across the country and even ordinary people, carrying placards and chanting slogans.

Adding to this, A man wearing a cockroach costume and others INDIA bloc's 'Chalo Dilli' protest rally in New Delhi. (PTI) Standing near H-Block, 38-year-old Rakesh Solanki shared, “We are here to ensure the chief election commissioner resigns.” He had travelled all the way from Uttar Pradesh’s Badaun and was part of a group who called themselves the Cockroach Volunteers.

Meanwhile, “We are the real cockroaches. We stood our ground, were on the ground on every protest call, got beaten up, and detained by police,” he told HT as the crowds made their way to the Minto Road junction.

Notably, The Congress-led INDIA Bloc rally drew tens of thousands of people. Starting 1.30pm they marched from Minto Road to Ramlila Maidan . The entire way people could be heard chanting slogans against CEC Gyanesh Kumar.
As per the latest buzz, While there are no official figures for attendance, local police officials estimate over 50,000 people were present in the area.
In further updates, But the mood was not of anger with people dressed up in costumes and contingents of tribal workers in traditional attire, performing cultural dances.

On top of that, A 21-year-old college student from Mumbai, who introduced himself as ‘Takshroach’, shared he was wearing a full cockroach costume. “I came dressed as a bat on October 10. I order these costumes so I get noticed and can convey what I have come for. To believe in the electoral process is extremely important and that faith needs to be restored,” he shared.

Earlier, around A-Block in the Inner Circle, wearing a bright orange dress Ramayan Singh Rathiya, a worker with the Chhattisgarh Adiwasi Congress, shared, “My troop and I, around 200 of us, have come to represent our traditions and our people. We reached Delhi yesterday and have been preparing for the dance for a week.”

title: INDIA bloc's protest keeps shoppers away, Connaught Place bears the brunt before Diwali
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:
The Opposition and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) blamed each other on Sunday as traders in Connaught Place reported poor sales on the last Sunday before Diwali in light of the INDIA bloc protest.

Adding to this, Some retail shops remained closed at Connaught Place amid protest. (HT Photo) In conversation with reporters, hours ahead of the protest, Union minister and senior BJP leader JP Nadda accused the Opposition of disrupting business ahead of the festive season. “It is the festive season. Throughout the year, small traders, street vendors, shopkeepers wait for it for some earnings during these festivals. But Rahul Gandhi does not care about stoves burning in traders’ homes. He only wants to ignite the fire of his politics,” he shared.

Meanwhile, Hours later, leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha and senior Congress leader Rahul Gandhi accused the BJP of pressuring shopkeepers to shut their stores, despite rally participants having been urged to support local traders.

Notably, “We told everyone that when you come here for the march and the mega rally, buy things, do some shopping. But, while coming to CP here, we found out that the BJP has forcibly shut down every single shop. So, you should know who is causing the loss to the traders, and how it’s happening,” the Congress leader alleged, in conversation with the media.

As per the latest buzz, In a post on X, Union home minister Amit Shah shared, “Delhi’s traders pleaded that the rally be held after Diwali, otherwise there would be heavy losses in business, but Rahul Baba just had to hold the rally on the very day the Sikh massacre took place. More than ₹ 25,000 crore rupees trade occurred in these three days as whole North India comes to the wholesale market of Delhi to purchase goods... I want to tell Congress that you have caused losses to small traders and now your electoral account will not open for the next three elections.”
In further updates, Traders in CP shared the rally had affected business as parking was occupied by participants and customers opted to stay away amid apprehensions of restrictions and congestion.

On top of that, “Once again, CP is bearing the brunt of these rallies, creating an atmosphere of uncertainty and fear among customers,” shared Atul Bhargava, president of the New Delhi Traders Association.

Bhargava shared repeated disruptions were worsening an already difficult situation for traders during the festive season and arguing that rallies and processions through commercial areas are affecting traders’ right to livelihood.

title: Ram Gopal Varma defends violence in films amid scrutiny after Andhra Pradesh chainsaw attack; internet says cinema has responsibility
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The entire nation is in shock after the news that a 15-year-old and another student were injured by a chainsaw and are critical after Friday’s attack in Andhra Pradesh’s Anantapur district. After the incident, several users on social media questioned whether the recent A-rated films with a lot of bloodshed and gore play a key role in normalising such violence.

Adding to this, Ram Gopal Varma has defended violence in films. What RGV shared Filmmaker Ram Gopal Varma came to the defense of films after several X users posted pictures and videos from recent releases like Animal and KGF to point out how these films show violence without consequence. Ram Gopal Varma wrote, “Blaming films for rise in violence is like , blaming Ramayana for rise in kidnappings.”
Meanwhile, But the internet was not having the defense, and quickly responded in the comments with their own reason as to how cinema does have a role to play in shaping young minds in a society.

Notably, One user wrote, “Stop pretending cinema has zero social responsibility by bringing in historical references. That's not going to wash away or lessen your role. Some of the most cruel and gruesome murders are made to look so chill and heroic in movies that even our 8-year-olds are growing up like monsters.. It's time you guys take some shame and responsibility for what you put out there and do your part in curbing this.”

As per the latest buzz, Another shared, “Nobody is saying films directly cause crime but pretending cinema has zero influence on society is equally stupid. Cinema shapes perceptions, normalises behaviour and influences what audiences celebrate.”

In further updates, "I tend to disagree. We become what we consume. People underplay how deeply media, in all forms, shapes behaviour & choices. This is due to a psychological blind spot known as the 3rd-person effect— the belief that other people are easily persuaded by media while we stay immune," read another response.

On top of that, “In a country like India, where cinema has an enormous influence on people's mindsets, attitudes & perceptions, pretending that films cannot shape or reinforce social behaviour is nothing but intellectual dishonesty. You can deny it all you want but masses do get influenced by it,” shared a second user on X.
Two Class 10 students were attacked with a chainsaw by a man who allegedly barged into their classroom at a government high school in Raptadu, Anantapur district, on Saturday.

title: Sanjay Gupta death: Ajay Devgn says the director had so much more cinema left in him, Anil Kapoor admits he is ‘deeply saddened and heartbroken’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood filmmaker Sanjay Gupta has died at the age of 59. His sudden death on Saturday morning has sent a shock waves through the movie industry. Following his death, several actors and friends visited his home in Mumbai to pay their last respects. Many others took to social media to remember him and pay their tribute.

Adding to this, Anil Kapoor shared a picture with Sanjay Gupta. What Anil Kapoor wrote Anil Kapoor paid an emotional tribute on X. He worked with filmmaker Sanjay Gupta in two films: Musafir (2004) and Shootout at Wadala (2013). He wrote, "Deeply saddened and heartbroken by Sanjay's passing. We shared a special bond, both personally and through the films we worked on together. There was always an understanding between us that I truly cherished. Sanjay had his own unique voice and vision as a filmmaker, and the memories of working with him will always remain close to my heart. Going to miss you, Sanjay. Rest in peace, my friend."

Meanwhile, Meanwhile, Ajay Devgn wrote, "Gone far too soon. Sanjay had so much more cinema left in him, so many more years and stories ahead. Truly heartbreaking….praying for strength and peace for his family."

Notably, Vivek Oberoi also recalled memories of working with Sanjay and shared, "I am deeply shocked and heartbroken by the sudden and untimely demise of Sanjay Gupta. This loss is truly unimaginable and very difficult to process.

As per the latest buzz, Having worked together, this news feels deeply personal. It is never easy to accept the loss of someone you have shared a journey, conversations and memories with. Some news leaves you numb, and this is one of those moments.

In further updates, I will always cherish the time we spent working together. You will be missed, Sanjay. My heartfelt condolences to his family and loved ones. May God give them the strength to cope with this irreparable loss.

On top of that, The Versova police have registered an accidental death report (ADR) in connection with the incident and are probing to ascertain the exact sequence of events. The police were informed in the morning about the death of Sanjay Gupta.
The police shared the CCTV footage of the house shows that around 2.00 am. Gupta, who was sitting in the drawing room, went to the kitchen and later lost his balance and fell against the wall.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor has compared Elon Musk's Tesla Roadster car with the Pushpaka Vimana from the Ramayana. What Ranbir shared During the chat, when the host shared how the weapons that were used during that time were so amazing and could beat modern creations. She also lauded the VFX work done by Academy Award-winning studio DNEG (Double Negative) for the same. Nitesh shared that it was great to reimagine those creations on screen. Ranbir added, “Elon Musk of late invented a flying car. I think India did it 5,000 years ago!”

Meanwhile, Tesla unveils its long-delayed Roadster nearly a decade after first revealing a next-generation version of its original electric sports ​car, at a launch event in Waco, Texas, US, on October 15. During a demonstration event at SpaceX’s rocket development and testing facility in Texas, the electric supercar drove upside-down on a huge curved ramp, flipped, remained airborne for a few seconds, and then landed safely on the ground. "Well, it worked," Tesla CEO Elon Musk shared after it successfully landed. The supercar will not be available for purchase immediately. Elon Musk shared that the car will enter production in 2028.
Notably, Meanwhile, Yash shared that it is beautiful to see this interpretation of Ramayana and how relatable this story is even today.

As per the latest buzz, The Pushpaka Vimana is a mythical, self-moving aerial chariot or flying palace described in the Hindu epic the Ramayana. It was one of the visual elements featured in the trailer which stood out as a gigantic flying structure.

In further updates, As per Hindu mythology, the Vimana (airborne palace) was created by Vishwakarma, the celestial architect, for Lord Brahma. He then gave the Vimana as a gift to Kubera, the God of wealth and half-brother of Ravana. However, Ravana stole the Pushpaka Vimana from Kubera after defeating him. In the epic, Pushpaka Vimana is described as a flying palace which can fly at the speed of thought and expand to accommodate any number of people.

On top of that, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is a two-part cinematic adaptation of the ancient Indian epic. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi portrays Sita, and Yash plays Ravana. The cast also includes Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman and Ravi Dubey as Lakshman. The movie is produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, with music by AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer. The first part releases in theatres on November 5, on the occasion of Diwali.

title: 'Your turn to become PM won't come': Amit Shah takes potshots at Rahul Gandhi amid INDIA bloc protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:
Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday targeted Congress leader Rahul Gandhi amid the INDIA bloc's protest in Delhi, saying his turn to become the prime minister would never come.

Adding to this, Amit Shah also criticised Rahul Gandhi for holding a rally in the capital on November 1, saying it would “rub salt in the wounds” of victims of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. “If you want to become PM, stay in mock parliament your entire life; your turn won't come,” Shah shared in Chandigarh, addressing Gandhi, news agency PTI reported. The remarks came a day after the INDIA bloc held a mock Parliament session to ‘publicly impeach’ chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, who faces allegations of irregularities in the electoral processes.

Meanwhile, Speaking in Chandigarh, Shah criticised Gandhi for holding a rally in the capital on November 1, the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. “The day the Sikh genocide happened, on that very day, they had to hold a rally,” he shared, adding that it would “rub salt on the wounds” of the victims.

Notably, The home minister targeted the INDIA bloc's protest being held in Delhi on Sunday. Opposition leaders and supporters in large numbers gathered at Ramlila Maidan for the ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ rally against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, over alleged discrepancies in electoral rolls and concerns surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.

As per the latest buzz, INDIA bloc's ‘Chalo Dilli’ march began at the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction on Sunday, with leaders including Rahul Gandhi, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee proceeding towards Ramlila Maidan.

In further updates, The rally was attended by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee, Telangana chief minister Revanth Reddy, RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav, Jammu and Kashmir National Conference president Farooq Abdullah, CPI leader D Raja, PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti and other INDIA bloc leaders, news agency ANI reported.

On top of that, Meanwhile, the BJP organised a march in Delhi's Hari Nagar area on Sunday to protest against the 1984 anti-Sikh riots . The march was led by Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri and joined by various Sikh organisations, PTI reported.
In Chandigarh, Shah also attacked the Congress over the 1984 riots, saying thousands of people had been killed.

title: Himesh Reshammiya confirms plans to turn director: “It would collect Rs. 100 cr on day of release!”; wishes to become a superstar actor: “Amitabh Bachchan’s 13th film was a hit; I have done 12 films until now...”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Himesh Reshammiya was asked, “Can we see a movie that mentions ‘Directed by Himesh Reshammiya’ in the future?” Himesh replied, “100% you’ll see that. When I used to produce serials, I used to be asked, ‘Will you ever turn music director?’ Today, when I have achieved so much in the field of music and films, I do want to try my hand at direction. However, my vision is very definite for my directorial venture in terms of scale, emotional connect and beautiful songs. I am very clear about these aspects.”

Adding to this, When asked if his directorial debut would be a musical romance, Himesh Reshammiya answered, “I have 2-3 ideas. The scripts are ready and they are blockbusters. The music in my directorial venture would be such that it would fetch Rs. 100 crore rupees on the day of rollout! I am very sure of that.”

Meanwhile, It has come to light that the movie Himesh Reshammiya which plans to direct will not feature him as an star. It will feature another star. Meanwhile, the films in which Himesh will be acting will be helmed by other directors.

Notably, He was also asked if he had any unfulfilled wishes. Himesh Reshammiya confessed, “I want to become a superstar star. Mujhe banna hi hai aur banoonga bhi. Yeh toh hona hi hai, aaj nahin toh kal . Amitabh Bachchan’s 13th movie was a hit. I have done 12 films until now. So, my thirteenth movie would be a smash hit!”

title: Nikkhil Advani has a fanboy moment with Richard Gere as he shows Pretty Woman star Shah Rukh Khan's iconic Kal Ho Naa Ho song
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Nikkhil Advani got a rather special opportunity to revisit one of the most memorable moments from his first movie, and this time, he had a very special audience. The filmmaker met Hollywood star Richard Gere at the 15th edition of Dharamshala International Movie Festival 2026 and showed him the popular Pretty Woman sequence from his 2003 movie Kal Ho Naa Ho, starring Shah Rukh Khan and Preity Zinta. For someone who grew up admiring the Hollywood star, it was clearly a moment to cherish.

Adding to this, Nikkhil Advani's fanboy moment with Richard Gere: Filmmaker shows Pretty Woman star Shah Rukh Khan's iconic Kal Ho Naa Ho song. Nikkhil Advani shares a video featuring Richard Gere Sharing the experience on Instagram, Nikkhil couldn't hide his excitement. He wrote, "Huge huge fan boy moment. Showed @richardgere #PrettyWoman from #KalHoNaaHo 🙌🙌🙌🙌" He further teased his followers with "(wait for his reaction)" and added "Icing on the cake 🎂".

Meanwhile, The filmmaker also tagged Shah Rukh Khan, Preity Zinta, Karan Johar, Shankar-Ehsaan-Loy, lyricist Javed Akhtar and choreographer Farah Khan. He also tagged the official account of the late Roy Orbison in his post.

Notably, View this post on Instagram How Richard Gere's Pretty Woman became a part of Kal Ho Naa Ho Richard Gere's 1990 romantic comedy Pretty Woman remains one of Hollywood's best-known love stories. The star played Edward Lewis, a wealthy businessman who meets Vivian Ward (Julia Roberts), a Hollywood sex worker. What begins as an arrangement for business events soon develops into an unexpected romance. The movie became a worldwide hit and helped establish Julia Roberts as a leading Hollywood star. Roy Orbison's ‘Oh, Pretty Woman’, which featured in the movie, also became a timeless favourite.

As per the latest buzz, The song eventually found its way into Hindi cinema through Kal Ho Naa Ho. In the movie, Shah Rukh's character Aman breaks into a Hindi version of Pretty Woman, dancing on top of a taxi and trying to win over his neighbour Naina (Preity Zinta). The sequence is among the movie's most recognisable moments and remains a fan favourite.

In further updates, Karan Johar, who wrote the movie, had acquired the rights to recreate Roy Orbison's original track. Shankar-Ehsaan-Loy worked on the music, with singer Ravi "Rags" Khote lending his voice to the Hindi version. The team gave the familiar song a Bollywood makeover without losing the charm of the original. Shah Rukh's playful performance made it even more memorable.

On top of that, Rolled out in 2003, Kal Ho Naa Ho followed Naina (Preity Zinta), a young woman in New York who is dealing with family problems and the pressures of everyday life. Things begin to change when Aman (Shah Rukh Khan) moves into her neighbourhood. His cheerful nature brings a fresh perspective to Naina's life, even as she struggles to understand his constant optimism.

Aman also tries to bring Naina closer to her best friend Rohit (Saif Ali Khan), hoping the two will find happiness together. But there is a reason behind his efforts to make everyone around him smile. Aman is terminally ill and knows he does not have much time left. Rather than let his illness define his final days, he chooses to make the most of the time he has and ensure that Naina has a happy future.

title: Himesh Reshammiya makes a BIG revelation: “I have written, sung and composed 15 songs in English; they don’t sound WANNABE at all”; adds, “There’s one song which is ABSOLUTELY right for Rihanna”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Himesh Reshammiya was asked if there was any international singer with whom he would like to collaborate. Before answering the question, the singer-composer made an interesting revelation. He shared, “Nobody knows that I have composed 15 songs in the international language, which absolutely do not sound wannabe in any manner whatsoever. I have written, sung and composed those 15 songs in English. They are going to be launched on a very, very big scale. I am waiting to plan for it because I have been tied up with so many things and films.”

Adding to this, Himesh Reshammiya continued, “I’ll launch the album internationally the way I was launched as a singer here. Now that I have entered Bloomberg’s list of top pop stars of the world, this is the right time to present my album. Its first single will be unveiled in a grand fashion globally. So, it’s not like I sang a small part in a global song. It purely targets the universal audience who listens to English music.”

Meanwhile, Himesh added, “It’ll be very different. At one point, no one was able to imagine how I would sound when I sang Aashiq Banaya Aapne (2005). The same will happen here. It’s so good and yet again, it has a romantic connection. I am very excited about it.”

Notably, Finally, answering the original question about his dream international collaboration, Himesh Reshammiya revealed, “If I get a chance to collaborate, then there’s one song which is absolutely right for Rihanna.”

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

A source from Shah Rukh Khan’s team told Bollywood Hungama, “Shah Rukh Khan shares a very close relationship with Aditya Chopra. He starred in Adi’s directorial debut, Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge (1995), which, as we all know, was a historic smash hit and continues to run at Mumbai’s Maratha Mandir. He also worked in several other memorable YRF films and shared a wonderful bond with Aditya Chopra’s late father, the legendary filmmaker Yash Chopra. Hence, SRK decided to personally call Aditya Chopra and explain the situation.”

Adding to this, The source continued, “Both had a lovely conversation. Aditya Chopra completely understood Shah Rukh Khan’s point of view and readily agreed to part with King ’s overseas distribution rights. He wished SRK all the best for King and told him that he was eagerly looking forward to watching the movie this Christmas.”

Meanwhile, This development comes amid several interesting changes surrounding King . A few days ago, Bollywood Hungama reported that Anirudh Ravichander, who has collected a massive following for his electrifying background scores, had amicably parted ways with the movie owing to his packed schedule. Before his exit, however, he handed over the theme track of King to Shah Rukh Khan as a mark of respect for the superstar. Meanwhile, composer duo Sachin-Jigar will reimagine the track and use it as the foundation for the movie’s background score.

Notably, Bollywood Hungama had also informed readers that T-Series has secured the exclusive global commercial music rights to King for a period of 50 years. The agreement, as revealed through details shared by the music company, was facilitated by Red Chillies Entertainment through Zee Music Company.

As per the latest buzz, Besides Shah Rukh Khan, King also stars Deepika Padukone, Rani Mukerji, Abhishek Bachchan, Jaideep Ahlawat, Anil Kapoor and several others. Meanwhile, an exciting promotional asset from the movie is expected to be unveiled tomorrow, November 2, coinciding with Shah Rukh Khan’s 61st birthday.

title: Hrithik Roshan pens sweet birthday message for girlfriend Saba Azad about choosing love over convenience, shares rare picture of her with his sons
body: Here's the latest relationship update doing the rounds:

Hrithik Roshan made girlfriend Saba Azad 's birthday a little more special with a heartfelt note that was as personal as it was romantic. The star shared a series of pictures with Saba on Instagram, along with a message about why he would happily choose the longer, more complicated route in life if it meant having her by his side.

Adding to this, Hrithik Roshan says Saba Azad is 'too precious' to talk about, shares intimate birthday post and family pictures. Hrithik Roshan's sweet birthday message for Saba Azad In his Instagram post, Hrithik recalled being asked about Saba and how he initially hesitated to speak about her because she was too precious to him. He then shared an analogy about choosing between a direct flight from Mumbai to a faraway destination and another with several stopovers.

Meanwhile, The star wrote, “Someone asked me about you. I shared I don't wanna talk about you cause it's too precious. She insisted and I shared this .. ‘Well, how about this? Say if there were 2 options for flights from mumbai to a far off destination, one was a direct flight. Efficient and easy!’”

Notably, View this post on Instagram Explaining why he would prefer the longer journey, Hrithik added, "And another one that went via 8 random cities with hours of transit time each stop with possibilities of missing connecting flights. If it was with her..." I shared, “I'd pick the 2nd option... deliberately... every single time. Cause with you Sa, every mundane, every wait, every deviation from the normal inevitability turns into a dance of adventures. Let's adventure on my birthday girl. Here's to a lifetime of long layovers together. I love you Happy Birthday.”

As per the latest buzz, The photographs accompanying the note gave followers a peek into the couple's time together. Among the pictures was a candid moment of the two enjoying ice creams, while the final photograph featured Saba smiling alongside Hrithik's sons, Hrehaan and Hridhaan .

In further updates, Hrithik and Saba as per reports connected on social media in late 2021 or early 2022. It began after the star appreciated one of Saba's videos on X (formerly Twitter). Their online interaction soon moved to direct messages, and a mutual friend eventually helped arrange their first meeting. The two made their relationship public when they arrived together at filmmaker Karan Johar's 50th birthday party in May 2022. Since then, they have been spotted together at family gatherings, movie events and holidays, while occasionally sharing glimpses of their relationship on social media.

On top of that, Hrithik Roshan's last major theatrical rollout as an star was War 2, directed by Ayan Mukerji and co-starring Jr NTR and Kiara Advani. It rolled out on August 14, 2025. The star was most of late seen in a special appearance in Rajinikanth's smash hit Jailer 2 , which rolled out in October 2026.

Meanwhile,Saba Azad most of late appeared in Who's Your Gynac? Season 2, reprising her role as Dr Vidushi Kothari. The season began streaming on Amazon MX Player in 2026. She was also seen in Songs of Paradise (2025), the musical drama inspired by Kashmiri singer Raj Begum. She has also wrapped filming for Storm , a thriller series backed by Hrithik's production banner HRX Films.

title: R Madhavan reunites with horror genre after 13B and Shaitaan; joins hands with Vishal Furia
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The untitled movie will be produced by Rohit Ranjan under Frostlit Production Limited, with the filmmaker describing Madhavan as his first choice for the project.

Adding to this, Madhavan’s association with horror dates back to 13B , which developed a cult following for its unsettling premise. He later appeared in Shaitaan , further adding to his filmography in the genre. Over the years, the star has also worked across a range of roles and languages, with credits including Rehnaa Hai Terre Dil Mein , Tanu Weds Manu , 3 Idiots , Vikram Vedha and Rocketry: The Nambi Effect . He was also of late seen in Dhurandhar .

Meanwhile, Furia, meanwhile, has established a presence in the horror space, beginning with the Marathi movie Lapachhapi and subsequently developing the Chhorii franchise. His recent directorial work includes Maa , in which Madhavan made a surprise cameo. The soon-to-release project marks their first collaboration as star and director on a feature movie.

Notably, Speaking about casting Madhavan, Furia shared, “Madhavan sir was always my first and only choice. I’m stoked that he has come on board and has already started getting into the world of the movie. He is the true OG horror star of the cult classic Indian horror '13B' - one of my favourite films of all times. title: Rana Daggubati announces new horror film titled Scary Picture with Kangana Ranaut, offbeat Telugu director Ravi Babu to helm
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

At the HorrorCon India 2026 held in New Delhi on Halloween, Rana Daggubati made a surprise announcement. He opened up that he would be producing a horror movie titled Scary Picture, directed by Telugu filmmaker-star Ravi Babu, who is known for his offbeat films. It will star Kangana Ranaut , who made the news official on her Instagram on Sunday.

Adding to this, Kangana Ranaut's last horror movie was Chandramukhi 2 in 2023. Kangana Ranaut’s next movie titled Scary Picture Videos taken at HorrorCon show Rana announcing his next project on stage. A glimpse of it on screen shows that it is titled Scary Picture. The movie’s title suggests it will be made in Hindi. While Rana’s production house has yet to make an official announcement, Kangana reposted a video from an Instagram page in which the star-filmmaker reveals the movie.

Meanwhile, Rana spoke about the movie at HorrorCon and shared, “So, it’s a horror movie. It’s by a director called Ravi Babu, who is a friend of mine. He’s made multiple horror films in Telugu. And this is his first Hindi feature. The title is revealed here first. It went to no Hindi press; this is the first time we’re putting the intimation up.”

Notably, Ravi is late veteran Telugu star Chalapathi Rao’s son and has been an star since 1998 and a director since 2002. He is known for his unconventional, genre-bending, and experimental filmmaking style, which doesn’t always deliver box-office results but stands out for its offbeat quality. In 2023, he even attempted a Babe-style movie titled Adhugo, with a piglet as the central protagonist.

As per the latest buzz, Throughout his career, Ravi has helmed everything from coming-of-age stories to thrillers, with most films featuring a touch of slapstick comedy. He last starred in Coffee with a Killer last year and directed Razor this year. Given that it’s rare for the filmmaker-star to team up with known faces, it remains to be seen what he has in store with Scary Picture.

In further updates, Kangana, who is currently also busy as the MP of Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, has been juggling both politics and films. She contested elections as a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and won them. She last starred in Bharat Bhhagya Viddhaata this year, which she also produced. The movie received mixed reviews and collected ₹ 8 crore rupees worldwide in its lifetime. It is currently streaming on Zee5.

On top of that, Kangana's last Hindi-language horror movie was Raaz: The Mystery Continues in 2009. In 2023, she starred in the Tamil horror comedy Chandramukhi 2. title: Ram Gopal Varma gets ₹29 crore legal notice from Eclatant Films over 2010 agreement, production house warns OTT platforms
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Ram Gopal Varma is facing a legal notice from production house Eclatant Films Private Limited, which is seeking ₹ 29.67 crore rupees over an agreement dating back to 2010. The dispute could extend beyond the filmmaker, with the banner as per reports warning producers, distributors and OTT platforms against doing business with him or acquiring rights to projects associated with him.

Adding to this, Ram Gopal Varma faces ₹29.67 crore rupees legal notice from Eclatant Films over 2010 agreement; OTT platforms, producers put on alert. What is the row? As per a report by The Indian Express, Eclatant Films issued the notice on October 15, giving him until October 30 to settle the dues. The amount includes the pending principal and ₹ 11.38 crore rupees in interest. RGV has not commented on the matter publicly.

Meanwhile, The dispute dates back to an agreement signed by the two parties on April 10, 2010, which was as per reports upheld by the Bombay High Court on April 17, 2013. Eclatant Films claims that the agreement required Ram to obtain its written No Objection Certificate (NOC) before undertaking certain movie projects. This included work as a producer, director, writer or co-producer on films covered by the contract.
Notably, The production house alleges that these terms were not followed and is now seeking ₹ 29.67 crore rupees from the filmmaker.

As per the latest buzz, The notice is not limited to RGV. Eclatant Films has also reached out to the wider movie industry, warning producers, distributors, broadcasters and OTT platforms against entering into business deals with the filmmaker. As reported by trade publications, including Complete Cinema, the production house has cautioned industry players against buying, streaming or exploiting films linked to the filmmaker.

In further updates, The production house has also warned that it may invoke a contractual lien if he fails to pay the dues. This could mean seeking a claim to the rights, shares, financial interests, and earnings from films covered by the 2010 agreement.

On top of that, Ram Gopal Varma is busy with his next directorial, Police Company . The crime drama, led by Harshvardhan Rane , is slated to arrive in theatres on June 4, 2027. Based on true events and real-life characters, the movie looks at the circumstances behind the killing of around 300 gangsters.

The movie has an ensemble cast featuring Fardeen Khan, Fatima Sana Shaikh, Paresh Rawal, Saurabh Shukla, Makarand Deshpande and Ashwini Kalsekar. Bhushan Kumar, Krishan Kumar and RGV have produced the project, which is presented by Gulshan Kumar and T-Series.

title: Indian forces tighten security in Delhi ahead of big opposition protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Prefer the Guardian on Google Indian security personnel carrying batons and shields and accompanied by riot control vehicles surrounded the site of a planned opposition ⁠protest in Delhi on Sunday that is set to demand the resignation of the country’s election chief over a controversial revision of voter lists.

Adding to this, Authorities warned of traffic diversions ⁠ahead of the protest march ⁠and rally ​that will be led by Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi. The opposition says it expects hundreds of thousands of people to participate in what it says ⁠will be a major challenge to the prime minister, Narendra Modi, and his Bharatiya Janata party (BJP).

Meanwhile, Read more Opposition parties, student organisations and the youth-led Cockroach Janta party have held near-daily demonstrations since last month ⁠demanding that the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, step down over the voter list revision that critics say favours the ​BJP.

Notably, The Election Commission has denied favouring any ‌party and shared wrongly deleted voters ‌can re-enrol, while the BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.

As per the latest buzz, Analysts ‌say the youth protests, and growing support for the opposition, form the worst crisis for Modi since he came to power in 2014. But his government remains stable and the next general election is not due until 2029.

In further updates, The opposition parties have revealed they will hold a nearly 1.5km march on Sunday from central Delhi to the Ramlila Maidan, a ground that is the designated site for their protest ‌rally.

On top of that, Visuals from news agency ANI showed riot control vehicles and dozens of security personnel armed with batons and shields outside the rally venue, where announcements were being made urging people ​to ensure smooth traffic movement and cooperate with police officials.

title: Actor Saurabh Sachdeva unfazed by criticism surrounding ‘Ramayana’, says film made in the right way
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Mumbai, Star Saurabh Sachdeva says he is not bothered by the online chatter and public scrutiny surrounding the much-anticipated movie, "Ramayana", as the makers made it with a lot of care and authenticity.

Adding to this, Star Saurabh Sachdeva unfazed by criticism surrounding ‘Ramayana’, says movie made in the right way The movie, billed as an ambitious global-scale adaptation of the Indian epic, features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Goddess Sita and Yash as Ravana. It is directed by Nitesh Tiwari of "Dangal" fame.
Meanwhile, After the rollout of the trailer, the movie has received criticism over the visual effects and casting choices, including Kapoor's portrayal of Lord Ram.
Notably, Sachdeva, known for featuring in films such as "Animal", "Eko" and "Pushpa 2: The Rule", among others, shared the team knew religious subjects could evoke stronger reactions from people.

As per the latest buzz, "It doesn't affect me. Now, people have a forum or place to talk about, they can say anything. If you are not getting the story and emotion right, then you can talk about not liking the movie.

In further updates, "Here definitely our belief is also connected, religious belief, religious sentiment is there, that is what is a little fragile. Hence, many times people will get up strongly and talk," Sachdeva told PTI in an interview.

On top of that, The star shared he "isn't scared". "I think the movie is well-made, nothing has been added just to add, or we've not done anything just for the sake of it. Whatever I've seen, while dubbing for the movie, I feel it is done in a beautiful and right way," he shared.
Sachdeva essays the role of the complex character Maricha in the mythological epic.

title: Siang project stir: SAAYA calls for shutdown in 3 districts to protest arrests of agitators
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Itanagar, The SUMP Affected Area Youth Association has called for a shutdown in Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang districts of Arunachal Pradesh on November 2 to protest the arrests of those agitating against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project .

Adding to this, Siang project stir: SAAYA calls for shutdown in 3 districts to protest arrests of agitators SAAYA wrote a letter to Bogum Bokang Welfare Society , which represents the Bogum Bokang-Tuting area, urging it to extend its support to the shutdown.

Meanwhile, In a letter addressed to the BBWS president, SAAYA shared its emergency executive meeting, attended by representatives of the affected villages on October 29, unanimously resolved to launch the shutdown in coordination with the Siang Indigenous Farmer Forum , other community-based organisations, youth groups and affected residents.

Notably, The association shared the proposed shutdown was intended to protest the arrests of people participating in the movement against the alleged forced survey and deployment of central armed police forces in the project-affected areas.
As per the latest buzz, SAAYA shared the arrests amounted to an attempt to suppress the legitimate voices of indigenous communities opposing the project.
In further updates, The association urged BBWS to extend its cooperation and guide the movement along peaceful and democratic lines.

On top of that, Describing the agitation as a struggle to protect ancestral land, the Siang River and the future of coming generations, SAAYA shared the issue was also closely linked to the preservation of the identity of the Adi community.
The association called for unity among organisations and residents of the Siang region, reiterating its commitment to a peaceful and democratic movement.

title: TN orders withdrawal of cases against 1,800 anti-NEET protesters
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Tamil Nadu government has ordered the withdrawal of 65 cases registered against around 1,800 people who participated in protests against the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET), an official order shared.

Adding to this, The Vijay government has also proposed that admissions to medical courses in the state be based on Class 12 examination marks. Several demonstrations were held across Tamil Nadu between May 10 and July 31, demanding the scrapping of NEET, the nationwide entrance examination conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) for admission to medical courses.

Meanwhile, “The details regarding the cases that were registered against those who participated in the protests in Tamil Nadu, and their current status, were brought to the attention of Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay,” an official statement shared late on Saturday.

Notably, It added: “The government, as per the instructions of the chief minister, has issued an order immediately to take appropriate legal steps to withdraw the 65 criminal cases registered against approximately 1,800 people who took part in anti-NEET protests.”

As per the latest buzz, The ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), which came to power in the state in May, has backed the demand to scrap NEET and called for education to be moved from the Concurrent List to the State List of the Constitution.

In further updates, The Vijay government has also proposed that admissions to medical courses in the state be based on Class 12 examination marks, a position taken by the previous DMK government as well.

title: Nitesh Tiwari reveals 6.5 years went into Ravana-Jatayu fight, 50 designs created for Pushpak Viman for Ramayana
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bringing Ramayana: Rise of a Legend to the big screen has taken years of planning and work, and director Nitesh Tiwari has now shared a glimpse of what went into creating some of its key sequences. In a conversation with Shreyas Media, he opened up that the Ravana-Jatayu fight alone took six and a half years to complete. The team also spent nearly two years working on the Pushpak Viman, exploring dozens of designs before settling on the final look. He spoke about the thousands of people involved in the process and the amount of work required to get even one action sequence right.

Adding to this, Ramayana: Six and a half years to create one action sequence between Yash's Ravana and Jatayu. Ramayana: Rise of a Legend fight took six and a half years to complete The Ravana and Jatayu fight took years of planning and work to bring to life. The filmmaker opened up that the team spent six and a half years bringing this one sequence together, from the first discussion with the artist to its final completion. “You know how much time it has taken for us to finish the Ravana and Jatayu fight? From the time I briefed the previous artist to the time we finished the whole thing, six and a half years. One action sequence. I can go on and on about it for an hour just to tell you how much effort went into making everything from scratch. And thousands of people have worked on it,” he shared.

Meanwhile, The team also spent close to two years working on the Pushpak Viman, Ravana's mythical flying vehicle. Nitesh opened up that the final design went through several changes and looked very different from what they had initially planned. Since the Ravana-Jatayu fight had originally been developed around the earlier design, the team had to revisit parts of the sequence and make multiple changes.

Notably, “We took close to two years to arrive at that. And then a lot of things changed, which is why it took us so long to shape the Ravana and Jatayu fight. Because previously, we assumed the design of Pushpak Viman would be something like that, and we shaped the sequence around it. And when we loved the final design, which was completely different from what we had first thought, we had to do a lot of iterations. We created some 40-50 designs for Pushpak Viman before finalising the one you see in the movie. We didn't want something that did look like it could fly; we wanted some kind of science to go into it. Because I believe, we all believe there was science behind everything that happened that time,” he explained.

As per the latest buzz, Defending the massive visual effects work going into Ramayana, Ranbir Kapoor of late called out the audience's habit of dismissing elaborate CGI as AI-generated. He admitted that it feels terrible to see the crew's efforts reduced to an AI tag, explaining that there are actually thousands of artists working around the clock. Ranbir emphasised that it takes days of gruelling manual effort just to perfect a single frame and bring that level of finesse to the screen.

In further updates, Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi stars as Sita, while Yash takes on the role of Ravana. Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The first instalment is set to arrive in theatres on Diwali 2026, with the second part scheduled for 2027. However, the media in the West is claiming that the sequel will arrive in Diwali 2028.

title: HT Morning Brief November 1: Oppn's ‘Chalo Dilli’ march today; protests sweep France, Germany and more
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:
Good morning. Here's your quick, 5-minute brief on things you need to know from across the country, the globe, as well as, from the world of sports and entertainment.

Adding to this, E-rickshaws pass by cutouts of Indian National Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi and K C Venugopal put up outside Ramlila Maidan ahead of the "Save Democracy" march. (REUTERS) Opposition's ‘Chalo Dilli’ march today The Opposition's ‘Chalo Dilli’ march will begin at noon from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction. The march will culminate at Ramlila Maidan, where a mega rally is scheduled from 10am to 5pm. The march has been called against alleged electoral irregularities and to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
Meanwhile, The protest comes a day after the Opposition's mock impeachment of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, held at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence.

Notably, The Israeli elections ended in a stalemate on Thursday, with neither of the two main rival camps securing a clear majority. Amid suspense over what happens next, reports indicate that Ra'am and Joint List, the two main Arab parties that together secured 19 seats, may back the Opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot in a bid to oust PM Benjamin Netanyahu from power.

As per the latest buzz, According to a Times of Israel report, the Joint List is willing to back anti-Netanyahu parties from outside, even though it is doesn't want to actually be part of the government. “We want to help anyone who wants to bring down this awful government… and switch it for a different government. We want to be part of the correction, part of the hope," veteran Arab MK Ahmad Tibi was quoted as saying.

In further updates, Scores of people took to the streets in France and Germany as Europe witnessed yet another week of protests. France saw its third consecutive weekend of demonstrations, while those in Germany turned violent, with protesters looting stores and hurling petrol bombs at authorities.

title: You only live once: Why Ajay Bijli returned to his first love, music!
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

For decades, Ajay Bijli has made movie-going a very successful business. But the cinema czar has embarked on an unlikely second act, one that involves early-morning riyaaz, vocal coaches, recording studios, and the pursuit of a chartbuster.

Adding to this, a busy schedule notwithstanding, Ajay Bijli is finding time to carve a career in music even if that means riyaaz across time zones “I have always wanted to be a singer. Back in school, I sang in inter-school competitions. Then in Hindu College, I had my band,” he says. And I ask if he was the cool kid on the campus. He confirms, “Yes, I had long hair, I had a band, and we were doing gigs and festivals. But then life happened; I passed out of college and started working for PVR.”

Meanwhile, It was the pandemic and an uncomfortable realisation about life’s brevity that brought him back to his first love. “During COVID, I really panicked. I had an epiphany. "I shared life is fickle, and you only live once… I must do something about my music now!” says Bijli, managing director of PVR INOX.
Notably, “My kids also encouraged me. So I decided to train professionally,” says Bijli, a man always with a solid plan and the iron will to see it through.

As per the latest buzz, “I contacted a teacher from Berklee College of Music. I was also fortunate to have an equally fantastic Hindi teacher, Santa Singh. I practise every day at five in the morning because if I take up something, I make sure I am sincere about it,” says Bijli, who approached recording with the same rigour.

In further updates, When he was to record a song in musician Amit Trivedi’s studio, he practiced the song so relentlessly that, as he recalls, “my face turned blue. But I was sure I wanted to show up prepared."

On top of that, The recording went so well that Trivedi asked if he could include the song in his album, Azad Collab . Later, Trivedi composed music for his first EP, On Another Note . It had three songs, including a wedding number, Dil Kare Haaye Haaye , directed by filmmaker Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra.

The experience gave him the confidence to pursue his own originals in a big way. In fact, Warner Music India offered to back him! And he has been performing live at ticketed events, too, successfully.

title: INDIA bloc rally LIVE: Protesters begin arriving at Ramlila Maidan; Opposition march to begin at 12pm
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

INDIA bloc rally LIVE: Early arrivals began from 5.30 am at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi, DCP Central Rohit Rajbir shared. INDIA bloc rally LIVE: A huge crowd was seen at the Ramlila Maidan in Delhi ahead of the INDIA bloc's ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ rally. Early arrivals began from 5.30 am at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi, with cops and volunteers facilitating crowd management in and around the area, DCP Central Rohit Rajbir shared. The Opposition will first hold a march from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction, which will culminate at Ramlila Maidan, where a mega rally is scheduled. ...Read More

Adding to this, “We also have a plan in place for the route of the march, which is scheduled to take place in a few hours,” the DCP told news agency ANI, adding that proper arrangements had been made at venue. The protest comes a day after the Opposition's mock impeachment of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, held at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence. Meanwhile, to target the Opposition over the date of their stir, the BJP will take out a protest march on Sunday in Hari Nagar area over the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. The march will be led by Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri, and will also be joined by various Sikh organisations news agency PTI reported. 10,000 security personnel deployed Nearly 10,000 police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed in central Delhi on Sunday. DCP Central Rohit Rajbir shared over 200 CCTV cameras were installed in the area, adding that police personnel have been deployed across the venue, and stationed in enclosures. The police earlier shared they will facilitate the march, which Gandhi revealed on his Instagram. However, while INDIA bloc is expecting “nearly one million people” to attend their rally from across the country, the police have planned for about 50,000, the capacity of the Ramlila Maidan. Police have shared any overflow would be held back on the surrounding streets. Traffic diversions across Delhi The Delhi Traffic Police has issued an advisory on route diversions and restrictions in parts of Central Delhi. The restrictions will remain in place from 10 am to 5pm. The diversion points include: Netaji Subhash Marg T-Point Rajghat Delhi Gate ITO A-Point Ajmeri Gate Red Light Ranjeet Singh Flyover at Barakhamba Road Bhavbhuti Marg–DDU Marg Red Light Jhandewalan Roundabout Turkman Gate Mirdard Chowk Rahul Gandhi urges protesters to ‘march and shop’; support traders Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has urged those participating in the INDIA bloc rally to support Delhi traders and make purchases for the festive season while attending the protest. “I want those lakhs of people coming to Delhi from outside to support the traders here. Protest, march, hold rallies, and along with that, do a little shopping too - it will benefit the traders,” Rahul shared in a post on X Why the protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar? While the Opposition has levelled allegations of “vote chori” and objected to the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in states several times in the past, a fresh row erupted against CEC Gyanesh Kumar after an Indian Express report last month. The report shared Election Commissioners had objected to decisions made by the CEC 14 times over a 10-month period. While the poll body maintained that all its decisions were unanimous, the report gave fresh momentum to the Opposition's allegations of “vote chori”, following which protests were called by student organisations, INDIA bloc parties and the Cockroach Janta Party.

Meanwhile, INDIA bloc rally LIVE: Congress leader Pawan Khera, speaking about the Opposition rally, shared, “This is the calm before the storm. The coming storm will sweep Gyanesh away, and Amit Shah and Narendra Modi will also not remain in their positions.”

Notably, He told news agency PTI, “Will traders not suffer losses because of the BJP's rally? Will they suffer losses only because of the Opposition's rally? Ask them, please. Under what pressure do they make traders write letters and then organise rallies themselves? Nitin Nabin held a rally on Wednesday when the markets were open. Did traders suffer losses or benefit from it?”
As per the latest buzz, Delhi protest LIVE: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Sunday claimed “limits of injustice” had been “crossed”, while slamming the BJP for alleged voter deletions.

In further updates, “Now, even the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh has himself admitted that 1.27 crore rupees votes have been reduced. And when did he remember this? Only after he lost the MLC election. Those who used to talk about a “double-engine government” have now become “double zero,”” Yadav told PTI news agency.

On top of that, Delhi protest LIVE: BJP is holding a counter protest in west Delhi ahead of Ramlila rally by INDIA bloc. Party leaders and workers have gathered for the march, which will begin from Hari Nagar bus depot to Tilak Nagar and will be led by Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri. Various Sikh organisations will also join.

INDIA bloc rally LIVE: Groups from West Bengal Pradesh Youth Congress and Madhya Pradesh Adiwasi Congress marched towards Ramlila Maidan from the inner circle in Connaught Place on Sunday, ahead of the INDIA bloc rally.

title: Divya Dutta lauds Gajab Raat co-star Manoj Bajpayee for treating newcomers as equals, says working with him leaves one spoiled | HT Exclusive
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Divya Dutta and Manoj Bajpayee worked together in four films — LOC: Kargil (2003), Veer-Zaara (2004), Special 26 (2013) and Traffic (2016) — but they never shared screen space in any of these projects. The duo finally got a chance to star together in not one, but two projects this year — The Last Man and Netflix's recent crime drama Gajab Raat .

Adding to this, Divya Dutta and Manoj Bajpayee are seen at loggerheads in Gajab Raat. In Neeraj Pandey's directorial, Divya plays a shrewd politician. In an exclusive interaction with Hindustan Times, the star spoke about how sharing screen space with Manoj was on her bucket list. She also talked about why Manoj and writer/co-producer Neeraj Pandey were the reasons she shared yes to the project.

Meanwhile, He was on my bucket list because he is one of the most amazing actors we have. It was really surprising that we did four films together and in none of them did we share screen space — except, I think, Special 26, where he just ran past me for a split second. So, we had been promising each other that we must work together, and finally it happened twice this year.

Notably, Gajab Raat has been really amazing because our roles were completely different. Manoj is effortless and very simple; his brilliance comes from his simplicity and how effortlessly he does everything. I've also been observing how he approaches everyone on set — he makes it so easy for people around him. Even with newcomers, he treats them as equals, which is so lovely. Plus, he has an amazing knack for cooking food for his colleagues, and he does it with so much love. It is such an amazing combination that one gets spoiled and wants to work with Manoj again.

As per the latest buzz, In Gajab Raat, I was barely on set with any of them for long, but he sweetly compensated for it. He took all of us out for dinner one day, and we had a blast. But nothing was cooked by him on set.

In further updates, What made me say yes was Neeraj Pandey, Manoj Bajpayee, Netflix. When I work with Neeraj Pandey, I know he will use me beautifully in the movie. He is the only person in the entire industry with whom I do this: when he calls me for a movie or a show, I just hand over my dates and go into his project like an audience member. I love the twists, turns, excitement, and thrill that come with being on his set. I just let it unfold. Even to me, some scenes come as a surprise — like, "Oh, this happened like that!" I love that little thrill. It's just great to work with people who know what they want out of you and how they are going to present you. When you are working with the best in the business — be it the director, the co-star, or the platform — it just feels great.

On top of that, The thing is, this movie was actually called something else even before the title you are talking about. Everyone thought people wouldn't understand the original title. Production teams always have a list of shortlisted titles — if not this, then that. No one really thought so much about it, but okay, if someone felt offended, that's fine. They didn't change anything in the movie, just the title. I think Gajab Raat suits the movie beautifully and has been loved by people so much. Anyone who raised an issue with the previous title has made up for it by loving this one.

Yes, we are a male-dominated industry — there is no two ways about it. However, efforts are underway to produce story-driven films. When you see a movie like Laapataa Ladies, there is a good marriage between strong storytelling, a talented filmmaker, a solid production house, and proper distribution.

title: Netflix's Ruchikaa Kapoor Sheikh says film reviews matter but are no longer a measure of a film's success | Interview
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:

Streaming in India has grown exponentially since its humble beginnings some 10 years ago, when ‘web series’ meant independently produced shows on YouTube. Today, the series are produced by the biggest studios in India, star A-listers, and stream on international platforms like Netflix . This proliferation of ‘content’, for lack of a better word, has also meant a dilution in quality. Yet, none of that has stopped people from watching it.

Adding to this, Netflix India's movie head Ruchikaa Kapoor Sheikh talks to HT about how streaming has changed cinema landscape. Even insiders agree that streaming has made the process of experiencing films and making them more democratic. In a chat with Hindustan Times, Ruchikaa Kapoor Sheikh , Director, Original Films, Netflix India, opens up about how streaming has changed not just viewers’ consumption patterns but also makers’ approach to films.

Meanwhile, Not long ago, reviews were seen as a make-or-break for films. Bad reviews had the power to sink films on the first weekend, while good reviews could often elevate even struggling films. Reviews, coupled with audience interest, translated into word of mouth, the critical engine for any movie’s ticket-window prospects. But streaming films do not rely on ticket-window. But now they no longer have to rely on reviews, either. Ruchikaa cautions against dismissing reviews completely, but agrees that audience perception now builds on more than just critics’ opinion. “I'll be honest. I wouldn’t say reviews don't matter. I think reviews are an important part of the conversation around and about a movie, but at no point are they a measure of its potential success,” she says.

Notably, “There was a time that critics were your only way in being able to decipher, understand, or get access to a movie. That was the only way. Today, it's such a democratic entertainment landscape that every movie arrives on its own terms, and every audience member individually arrives to that movie on their own terms,” adds Ruchikaa.

As per the latest buzz, The head of Netflix films says today that the films that get recommended are the ones that generate chatter, not necessarily the best-reviewed. “What we see very often is that films that get recommended are films that are spoken of. Like everyone will recommend Amar Singh Chamkila. Many people don’t recommend Haseen Dilruba or Sikandar Ka Muqaddar, but they are being watched. So we are acutely aware that there will be films that may not be spoken of as widely, but they do something for an individual,” she explains.

In further updates, Streaming has also changed how filmmakers approach titles and ‘projects’ today. In the past, many filmmakers like Karan Johar and actors like Naseeruddin Shah have admitted to doing big-budget masala stuff only so that they can make niche films that appeal to them creatively. Ruchikaa says streaming doesn’t have that compulsion. “Those are not the times anymore,” she says. “At this point, I don't have to choose between making an entertaining movie and making a thought-provoking one. On streaming, we definitely right-size that because we're aware that a certain movie has a certain audience, and therefore we need to make sure that it optimises for that audience, which is when it becomes super successful for us.”

On top of that, Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well. A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism. Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Movie Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day. Even as his role has evolved from reporter to supervisor over the years, his first love remains writing (and of late, talking on camera). With a good understanding of cinema and its trends, and a keen eye for detail, he continues to spark conversations around showbiz for readers around the world. Read More

title: Manushi Chhillar: Not every project has to be the dream job, sometimes it just has to get you closer to it
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Winning Miss World at 20 is quite the career head start. For Manushi Chhillar , it was also a passport to a world far bigger than pageantry. Almost a decade later, she is navigating acting, fashion and entrepreneurship, learning that life after a crown comes with its own plot twists, and not all of them are scripted.

Adding to this, Outfit: Priyanka Verma Jewellery: Soni Sapphire If there is one thing she has learnt along the way, it is to trust her gut. When she first entered the movie industry, the excitement of being new came with an eagerness to listen to those who knew the ropes. But experience, she says, has taught her that too many opinions can sometimes drown out the one that matters most: her own.

Meanwhile, “When you are younger and you come into an industry which is so new for you, you are excited,” she says. “You start listening to a lot of people around you who come with a lot of experience, but you eventually develop a sense of your own. Whatever I have done, whatever has come from my heart and whatever I have chosen for myself, has always given me more joy.”

Notably, It is a philosophy that has proved useful in an industry where even the most well thought-out plans can come with a question mark. “It's such an unpredictable profession,” Chhillar says. Without the backing of a movie industry family, she points out, there is no guarantee of what comes next. “You don't know when you're going to be starting your next movie. It's not like someone's sitting and creating a project for you.”

As per the latest buzz, For a newcomer, waiting for the perfect role can be a luxury few can afford. “I might have felt then, ‘I don't have the luxury to sit at home and wait for a big filmmaker to write this role specifically for me’,” she says. Sometimes, the sensible move is to take a project that gets you through the door rather than wait outside for the role of a lifetime. “So, not every project has to be the dream job. Sometimes, it just has to get you closer to it".

In further updates, Her Miss World win also gave her something more tangible than a global platform: financial independence. Brand endorsements helped support her during the early years of acting, giving her the freedom to build a career without putting all her eggs in one cinematic basket. Entrepreneurship is now another way to create a safety net of her own—one that allows her to keep pursuing acting without asking every role to pay both the bills and the emotional dividends.

On top of that, “I feel that it also gives me the opportunity to create something for myself, which in a way takes the pressure off acting,” she says. That does not mean she is any less invested in her craft. If anything, it gives her the breathing room to enjoy it. “You need to enjoy it if you're in an artistic profession.”

Her soon-to-release movie with Vikrant Massey is one project that has her particularly excited. She describes it as one of the most interesting scripts she has read in Mumbai, and the experience has offered a behind-the-scenes education of its own. The production involved sophisticated technology she had not encountered on previous projects, prompting her to pay closer attention to the mechanics of filmmaking.

title: Mark Bennington turns writer-director with Dear Tillo, says the seed of the short film was born in Lucknow
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

American star Mark Bennington says he has visited Lucknow only twice, but his connection with the city has shaped new avenues. The Heeramandi star says that his visit inspired him to make the short movie Dear Tillo , with which he turned writer, director, and producer.

Adding to this, Star-director Mark Bennington on his visit to Lucknow and in a still from his debut short movie Dear Tillo On his recent visit, to participate in Lucknow Movie Festival Season 4, he says, “It’s a movie that actually happened because of my previous visit to Lucknow as a jury member. I saw so many short films and it kind of gave me an idea of what I would do if I were to ever make a short movie? It inspired me to make a universally themed movie that is easy to watch, with which the audience could relate to, and has a little twist at the end. So, the seed of this short movie was born in Lucknow.”
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dear Tillo (@deartillo)

Notably, Of late seen in Vibes and Operation Safed Sagar , Bennington says he shot for the movie last year. “Last winter I did the whole edit and sound design, everything. And then this year, started submitting it to the movie festivals. We had our world premiere in Chicago South Asian Movie Festival, at International Movie Festival South Asia Toronto, then Mumbai and in Pune where we got the best star award. After Lucknow, we are going to Jaipur, the Indian festival in Florence. It is slowly making its way around the globe.”
As per the latest buzz, Working on his own project gave him the opportunity to explore something different from what he is offered.

In further updates, “Nobody has ever seen me in a role like this because I play a regular guy, a professor from the United States who’s come to India for the first time searching for his former student."

On top of that, He adds, “They meet again, and he realises that the life he had imagined for her is very different from the one she is actually leading. That’s where the story unfolds. He arrives with a certain expectation, only to discover that reality is quite different from what he had envisioned. That’s what makes it interesting!”

On his experience in Lucknow he says, “This time I noticed a change. Two years back, during the screening, it was a pretty respectable audience that was quietly watching and intent and listening. But, this time, people were having full conversations while someone was even doing a video call which was quite distracting. Even during the question and answer session it continued. There's only so many times you can tell somebody to be quiet. But, anyways, I watched some nice films, so it was a mixed experience.” He movie was showcased in the Beyond Borders in the international movie section.
