title: Heartbroken Hrithik Roshan remembers director Sanjay Gupta in moving tribute, thanks him for the best experience during the making of Kaabil
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The Hindi movie industry is mourning with the sudden demise of director Sanjay Gupta on Saturday. The filmmaker died at his residence after he slipped and hit his head. He was 59. Star Hrithik Roshan has now penned a moving tribute to the director, with whom he worked in the 2017 movie Kaabil.

Adding to this, Sanjay Gupta with Hrithik Roshan during a pre-rollout event for Kaabil. Hrithik remembers Sanjay Gupta Hrithik shared a picture with Sanjay in his X account and wrote in the caption, “Sanjay , I'm gonna miss you man. One movie with you wasn't enough ... I will always remember our time together with so much love for you .. your laughter, your passion , that child in you that lit up with every good idea , there was so much more we needed to do together man , this is way too soon.”

Meanwhile, He added, "I am gonna remember you with so much gratitude my friend , I wish I had hugged you harder and thanked you for giving me the best experience of my life with kaabil. Nobody will fully know how much you gave that movie. I'm heartbroken , this was too soon.

Notably, The Versova police have registered an accidental death report (ADR) in connection with the incident and are probing to ascertain the exact sequence of events. The police were informed in the morning about the death of Sanjay Gupta.

As per the latest buzz, The police shared the CCTV footage of the house shows that around 2.00 am. Gupta, who was sitting in the drawing room, went to the kitchen and later lost his balance and fell against the wall.

In further updates, Born in 1967 in Mumbai, Sanjay Gupta began his career at age 26 with the 1994 rollout, Aatish: Feel the Fire, starring Sanjay Dutt, Aditya Pancholi, Raveena Tandon, Karisma Kapoor and Atul Agnihotri.

On top of that, Over the next few years, he developed expertise in making gangster films, culminating in the 2002 movie Kaante, starring Amitabh Bachchan, Sanjay Dutt,. Suniel Shetty, Kumar Gaurav, Lucky Ali, and Mahesh Manjrekar. Widely regarded as his best work and one of the best gangster films to come out of Bollywood, it was inspired by Quentin Tarantino's Reservoir Dogs. He followed this up with critically acclaimed and successful films such as Zinda, starring Sanjay Dutt and John Abraham. One of his most high-profile films was the Hrithik Roshan-starrer Kaabil, which collected ₹ 208 crore rupees worldwide, emerging as his highest-grosser.

Santanu Das is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times with over 5 years of experience, writing on films, pop culture and movie festivals. He has a keen interest in writing about South Asian independent films and has covered several movie festivals, including Sundance and CPH: Docx. He also brings a sharp perspective to the monthly column called The Fault in Our Stars, where he writes about a recent movie/series and what stops the ‘good’ from becoming ‘great’. A gold medalist from Banaras Hindu University, Santanu completed his postgraduate studies in English from Jadavpur University. He is also a Rotten Tomatoes-certified movie critic. When not watching films or in conversation with celebrities, Santanu can be found reading a book. Some of his favourite films are Aparajito, Ponyo and The Double Life of Veronique. His favourite books include The Corrections, The God of Small Things and A Room of One's Own. Santanu continues to write passionately about films and star culture. He brings a relatable, as well as critically informed, lens to entertainment and culture for a wide audience. Find him on LinkedIn: santanudasfilm Instagram: @santupecha Read More

title: T-Series acquires 50-Year exclusive global music rights for Shah Rukh Khan starrer King through Zee Music
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The long-term agreement gives the music label control over the movie’s audio and music video rights, amid reports of a shorter licensing arrangement.

Adding to this, According to the announcement, the deal gives T-Series exclusive commercial exploitation rights over the movie’s musical assets worldwide for the next five decades. This includes its songs, music videos and associated publishing interests. The arrangement is positioned as a long-term acquisition rather than a temporary or short-duration licensing agreement.

Meanwhile, A T-Series spokesperson clarified the nature of the deal, stating, "There is no transient licensing structure or short-term handover at play. T-Series has locked in an absolute 50-year commercial monopoly over the audio and music video rights for King. Every song, video, and publishing interest rests squarely under the T-Series banner for the long haul."

Notably, The soundtrack is expected to be among the key attractions of King , with compositions by Sachin-Jigar and background music by Anirudh Ravichander. The movie is also expected to feature a musical collaboration between Ed Sheeran and Arijit Singh, which has already generated curiosity around its soundtrack.

As per the latest buzz, Directed by Siddharth Anand, King stars Shah Rukh Khan alongside Deepika Padukone, Suhana Khan and Abhishek Bachchan. The project marks the first time Shah Rukh and Suhana will share screen space as a father-daughter duo, adding to the anticipation surrounding the movie.

In further updates, The action spectacle is scheduled for a Christmas theatrical rollout. With T-Series acquiring the music rights for an extended period, the agreement places the label in charge of the movie’s global music exploitation well beyond its theatrical run. The arrangement also sets the stage for the soundtrack to be monetised across platforms and formats over the coming decades.

title: Prakash Raj’s wife Pony Varma says actor lost films and ad deals over his political views
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Prakash Raj is among the few actors who openly express their political views. The star was an active supporter and participant in the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) protest in Delhi following the NEET paper leak. In a recent interaction, his wife, Pony Verma, spoke about how Prakash has lost work because of his outspoken political views.

Adding to this, Prakash Raj has been vocal in his support of the Cockroach Janata Party movements against NEET paper leak and SIR. (PTI) 'Films were taken away from him' In conversation with Prema The Journalist, Pony recalled how Prakash was "devastated completely and broken" after his close friend and journalist Gauri Lankesh was shot dead in 2017. She shared that Gauri's death shook him and that he refused to remain silent, deciding instead to raise pertinent questions. However, she also admitted that Prakash's outspoken nature has often cost him work.

Meanwhile, She shared the star lost several movie opportunities and advertising assignments because of his political positions. "We all know Prakash is a fearless man. He was banned in Telugu multiple times. He stands his ground. He will believe in certain things and do it with 100% conviction. Several films, people have simply backed off after paying advance."

Notably, She added, "I know how much his work got affected in the industry. The way the ads went off, films were taken away from him. He has suffered immensely in his profession. But he says, my conscience says what is happening is wrong, so I should not accept this.”

As per the latest buzz, Pony also recalled the time Prakash participated in the CJP protest in Delhi and how ‘shaken and scared’ she was during the Chalo Sansad march after witnessing lathi charges and pellets guns used against protestors. However, she shared Prakash remained unfazed. He told her that at least the mothers of the protesting students would know that he was standing alongside their children.

In further updates, After the NEET protest, Prakash joined the CJP movement, which demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and opposed the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. He also spoke out against the detention of CJP leaders.

On top of that, On Saturday, Prakash shared a video urging people to join a protest in Delhi, calling for collective action to protect democracy. “Please join us in Delhi tomorrow for protest to save our democracy,” he shared. The appeal comes amid concerns over electoral transparency and democratic rights, with protesters questioning the electoral process.

title: Halloween 2026 | From Tumbbad to Bhoot, Bramayugam to The Conjuring, here are 10 films to binge watch
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Halloween, being celebrated on October 31, is a great time to revisit some horror classics. We shortlist 10 films which are all about guaranteed scares:

Adding to this, Stills from Bhoot, Bhool Bhulaiyaa Tumbbad (2018) This Anil Barve directorial has had an interesting journey. Declared a flop upon its original rollout, it went on to acquire cult status. Upon its theatrical re-rollout in 2024, it finally received its commercial due. The story revolves around a man, Vinayak Rao (played by Sohum Shah), whose greed for gold lures him into a monster's cave. Widely regarded as one of the finest horror films produced in India, its eerie period setting makes for a deeply disturbing watch.

Meanwhile, Ram Gopal Varma's Bhoot, starring Ajay Devgn and Urmila Matondkar in the lead roles, has acquired a cult following over the years. This 2003 movie revolves around a couple, Vishal and Swati Bhatia, who move into a new house in Mumbai. Soon after, they begin experiencing paranormal activity, with Swati eventually getting possessed. Such was the fear induced by Bhoot that a man in Delhi as per reports passed away while watching the movie.

Notably, This 2007 movie, directed by Priyadarshan, revolves around an Indian palace believed to be haunted by the spirit of a woman. Mysterious events begin unfolding, leading the villagers to believe that the spirit has returned for revenge. A psychological horror comedy, Bhool Bhulaiyaa's emotionally overwhelming climax has since become iconic. Akshay Kumar and Vidya Balan played key roles in the hit movie.

As per the latest buzz, The debut movie of actors Bipasha Basu and Dino Morea, Raaz was a rare hit, widely credited with establishing the popularity of horror in Bollywood. The story revolves around a married couple, Sanjana and Aditya Dhanraj, who decide to vacation in Ooty in an attempt to revitalise their failing marriage. However, they soon begin experiencing supernatural occurrences. Bipasha and Dino turned into overnight stars, with the movie's music further fueling its popularity.

In further updates, Not as widely known as some of the other films on this recommendation list, 13B: Fear Has A New Address had a rather unique premise. Manu's (R Madhavan) family moves into a new house, where strange events begin to unfold. Every day at 1 pm, the television switches on automatically and tunes into channel 13, which airs a serial about a family. Manu soon notices striking similarities between the events in each episode and what is happening inside his own house. Is it all in Manu's head, or is something sinister at play? Not a big hit upon its rollout, 13B has cultivated a dedicated fan following over the years.

On top of that, This horror drama spawned an entire successful movie franchise. Widely considered one of the scariest films ever made, it was based on the real-life demonologists Ed and Lorraine Warren. One of their cases involved the Perron family, who move into a new farmhouse in the early 1970s. Paranormal incidents begin occurring and soon escalate, prompting the Warrens to investigate. A massive hit upon its rollout, rewatching it on Halloween should already be a ritual.

Described as a deeply disturbing watch, Hereditary (2018) is consistently ranked among the scariest films ever made. The story follows a family grappling with the death of its secretive matriarch. Soon, they find themselves being hunted by a demon-worshipping cult intent on transferring a dark force into their bloodline.

title: Sanjay Gupta death: Ronit Roy breaks down; Rakesh Roshan, Fardeen Khan and Ashoke Pandit visit filmmaker's home
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood filmmaker Sanjay Gupta has died at the age of 59. His sudden death on Saturday morning has sent a shock waves through the movie industry. Following his death, several actors and friends visited his home in Mumbai to pay their last respects.

Adding to this, Sanjay Gupta's sudden death has shocked many in the movie industry. Ronit Roy in tears Ronit Roy was among the first ones to arrive at his residence, as he struggled to hold back tears. He was seen with several other close friends on Saturday afternoon. The star was closely acquainted with the filmmaker, having worked with him twice in Shootout At Wadala and Kaabil.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by SnehZala (@sneyhzala)

Notably, Filmmaker Milap Zaveri was also seen in tears, as he was consoled by other friends and relatives of Sanjay Gupta. Veteran filmmaker Rakesh Roshan , star Sudhanshu Pandey and Ashoke Pandit also arrived to pay their tributes.

As per the latest buzz, In a post on Instagram, Ashoke Pandit wrote, “It’s really shocking and sad. Just got the news that our dear friend an ace director Sanjay Gupta is no more. He passed due to a head injury at home. Another talent gone too soon. He was a wonderful narrator, full of life persona & a passionate filmmaker. A great loss to our industry. Will miss you my friend. Condolences to his family & dear ones. Om Shaanti. Details of his last rites will be shared soon.”

In further updates, The Versova police have registered an accidental death report (ADR) in connection with the incident and are probing to ascertain the exact sequence of events. The police were informed in the morning about the death of Sanjay Gupta.

On top of that, The police shared the CCTV footage of the house shows that around 2.00 am. Gupta, who was sitting in the drawing room, went to the kitchen and later lost his balance and fell against the wall.
Born in 1967 in Mumbai, Sanjay Gupta began his career at age 26 with the 1994 rollout, Aatish: Feel the Fire, starring Sanjay Dutt, Aditya Pancholi, Raveena Tandon, Karisma Kapoor and Atul Agnihotri.

title: Diljit Dosanjh addresses Satluj controversy at Delhi concert; says “Don't teach Punjabis how to fight”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The singer-star defended the movie based on human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra, recalling the long struggle to bring the project to the screen.

Adding to this, Addressing the audience, Diljit shared, “I love all of you because I am an artist, bro. I am being quiet, so let me stay quiet. I support all of you. But don't teach Punjabis how to fight.” He then spoke about the movie and the effort that went into making it, adding, “The movie you are making fun of on stage, Jaswant Singh Khalra's movie we fought for that movie for a long time. I love all of you. If someone hates us, it's okay. But I love all of you.”

Meanwhile, Directed by Honey Trehan, Satluj is a biographical drama based on the life of human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra, with Diljit playing the central role. The movie was initially titled Ghallughara and later renamed Punjab '95 before arriving under the title Satluj . Its narrative examines Khalra’s investigation into the alleged secret cremation of thousands of unidentified bodies in Punjab during the early 1990s. Khalra was abducted in September 1995 and killed, with his body disposed of in the Sutlej River.

Notably, The project faced prolonged certification hurdles with the Central Board of Movie Certification (CBFC). The board initially sought 21 cuts and a title change. After the makers challenged the demands and the movie went through further review, the proposed edits as per reports increased to 127. The filmmakers maintained their position against releasing a heavily edited version, with planned theatrical rollout dates being pushed back.

As per the latest buzz, In July 2026, the movie was unexpectedly made available on ZEE5 under the title Satluj . However, it was removed from the platform in India within 48 hours following directions from the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, according to the details surrounding its rollout.
In further updates, Diljit’s latest comments bring renewed attention to the movie’s journey and the debate surrounding its portrayal of a sensitive chapter in Punjab’s history.

title: Shriyam Bhagnani recalls intense 9-month training to transform into sumo wrestler for Sumo Didi, says people treated her differently after weight gain
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Shriyam Bhagnani took on one of the biggest challenges of her career with Sumo Didi , which marks her first movie in a leading role. Having previously appeared in films such as Baaghi 2 and Aap Jaisa Koi , as well as the series City of Dreams 2, Shriyam now finds herself at the centre of a women-led sports biopic. The movie follows the story of Hetal Dave, India's first female sumo wrestler, and required Shriyam to undergo an intense physical transformation to portray her on screen.

Adding to this, Shriyam Bhagnani's stills from Sumo Didi. In an exclusive interview with Hindustan Times, Shriyam spoke about the nine months of training that went into preparing for the role, the challenges of playing a real-life person and the responsibility of carrying a women-led movie. She also opened up about the movie's long journey to its rollout and how her experiences in the industry have shaped her career choices.

Meanwhile, For Shriyam, getting her first leading role in a women-led movie was a big opportunity. However, the fact that it was a biopic about a real person brought with it a different kind of responsibility. She explained, "Getting a lead movie is one thing, and getting a biopic, to play a real-life person, is another thing. And that too, someone who is alive and very similar to your age, so the comparison can happen very easily. So the pressure wasn't that I was leading a movie; it was that her story is so powerful and unique that it needed to be done justice. There are so many sports films that have been made, but this sport is so different, and the story is so different that it needed to be told in a certain way."

Notably, Taking on the role also meant making significant changes to her physical appearance. However, Shriyam shared she was not worried about being stereotyped for taking up such a role early in her career. She recalled having undergone physical transformations for other projects and how her perspective changed after seeing people's reactions to her new appearance.
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Shriyam Bhagnani (@shriyambhagnani)

In further updates, Shriyam siad, "I had also gained and lost weight for other projects. Growing up, I watched actors like Aamir Khan and Johnny Depp, and I felt it was a normal process for an star to go through this physical transformation. But once you mature, you realise that there are people who would probably not perceive you well when you are a different body type or weight. That comes in much later, and it happened after I gained the weight and the shoot had begun. When we were travelling to different places, I could see people behaving very differently with me because of that."

On top of that, "I was under contract for 9-10 months and couldn't sign anything else. So if any audition was coming, I had to tell them that I couldn't take up that part and that we would take something else up. They would try to warn me, to a certain extent scare me also, saying, 'Don't give something so much time, bharosa nahi hai iss industry ka, kuch bhi ho sakta hai (You can't trust this industry; anything can happen).' And I had already changed my body type for a couple of projects that got shelved a week before filming. They were all coming from their own good places, but these things happened," she added.

Shriyam's preparation for Sumo Didi went beyond gaining weight. She underwent several hours of training every day, including weight training, yoga, physiotherapy, sumo and judo. She also stressed that the physical training seen in the movie was performed by her without the use of AI or editing.

title: In final interview weeks before death, Sanjay Gupta revealed he proposed to wife after 7 years apart, shared their pets, families kept them connected
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta passed away on Saturday at the age of 59. While he was known for directing acclaimed gangster dramas such as Kaante, Shootout at Lokhandwala and others, not many knew about the romantic side of his personal life. In his last interview, rolled out a month before his death, the filmmaker opened up about separating from his first wife, Anuradha Gupta, and eventually marrying her again after seven years apart.

Adding to this, Sanjay Gupta died on Saturday at the age of 59. Sanjay Gupta proposed to first wife again after seven years of separation In a podcast on Hussain Zaidi Files, Sanjay spoke about how he and Anuradha separated after seven years of marriage due to issues in their relationship. The two filed for divorce and spent the next seven years apart. However, they never completely lost touch, as their families and pets continued to bring them together.

Meanwhile, Recalling how they remained connected during their separation, Sanjay shared, "I had other relationships during the time we were separated, but during this time there was this common factor between us, which was our two pets who used to live with me. So, she would come almost once a week, twice a week to meet them. During that time we would also meet. There was also this strong connect - she was really attached to my mother, who used to live separately, and I was very attached to her family. So, every birthday, wedding, Diwali - everything was celebrated together. So we never really went out of touch completely."

Notably, He eventually decided to propose to Anuradha again, realising that neither of them had been able to move on. Recalling the moment, he shared, "I separated from her, but I never fell out of love with her. Then one fine day, I just went up to her and proposed to her and shared what is the point of living like this. You have not been able to move on and same with me, so let’s give ourselves another shot. I was lucky that she shared yes. "

title: Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta passes away; director leaves behind a distinctive crime cinema legacy
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The filmmaker, who shaped the Hindi crime thriller genre with his stylised storytelling and neo-noir aesthetic, made his directorial debut with Aatish: Feel the Fire in 1994.

Adding to this, Gupta made his directorial debut with Aatish: Feel the Fire in 1994. Starring Sanjay Dutt and Aditya Pancholi, the action drama introduced audiences to his approach to high-impact action, sharp dialogues and stylised storytelling. Over the years, he became associated with a distinctive visual language, particularly in films exploring crime and the Mumbai underworld.

Meanwhile, One of his most recognised films remains Kaante (2002), which he directed and produced. The heist thriller featured an ensemble cast comprising Amitabh Bachchan, Sanjay Dutt, Suniel Shetty, Mahesh Manjrekar, Lucky Ali and Kumar Gaurav. Shot extensively in the United States, the movie developed a cult following for its gritty treatment, ensemble storytelling and technical presentation.

Notably, Gupta continued to explore the crime genre with projects such as Musafir (2004), while he was also associated with Shootout at Lokhandwala (2007) as a producer. He later directed Shootout at Wadala (2013), another movie centred on the Mumbai underworld. These projects further established his association with stories inspired by crime and gangland conflicts.

As per the latest buzz, His filmography also included projects beyond the gangster genre. Gupta directed the action revenge thriller Kaabil (2017), starring Hrithik Roshan, followed by the ensemble action drama Mumbai Saga (2021). Across these films, his work was marked by high-contrast visuals, stylised lighting and an emphasis on sound and action design.

In further updates, Through his production banner, White Feather Films, Gupta was involved in several projects that contributed to the evolution of the mainstream Hindi crime thriller. His approach to filmmaking and his focus on technical presentation made him a recognisable voice in the industry.

On top of that, Following reports of his passing, tributes and condolences have as per reports begun pouring in from members of the movie fraternity, collaborators and followers. Further details regarding the circumstances of his demise are awaited.
We at Bollywood Hungama express our heartfelt condolences to the filmmaker’s family and loved ones.

title: Sanjay Dutt pays tribute to late friend Sanjay Gupta, vows to fulfil his dream of making Kaante 2
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Sanjay Dutt has paid tribute to his late friend and filmmaker Sanjay Gupta , who died on Friday at the age of 59 after an accidental fall at his home. Sanjay posted on Instagram to share old photographs with the filmmaker and remember their years of friendship.

Adding to this, Sanjay Dutt paid tribute to his friend and filmmaker Sanjay Gupta. 'Will make Kaante 2 your dream, in memory of you my brother' In his Instagram post, Sanjay wrote about the bond he shared with Sanjay Gupta . He shared, "Gupts, my brother. I still cannot believe that you are gone. We have shared so much together, so many memories and so many years of friendship. You have always been family to me, and that will never change."

Meanwhile, The star also opened up that he had of late been discussing a sequel to their iconic movie Kaante with Gupta. The star shared he would fulfil the filmmaker's dream of making the sequel in his memory. He wrote, "I will miss you, our conversations and all the times we spent together. We were just discussing Kante 2 of late, I will make Kaante 2 your dream, in memory of you my brother, I will do everything for this dream of yours to come true, love you forever and always. Life will not be the same without you, brother. May God bless your soul 🙏🏼."
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sanjay Dutt (@duttsanjay)

As per the latest buzz, Sanjay Gupta shared a close friendship with Sanjay Dutt. The two first bonded on the sets of Raj Sippy's Thanedaar (1990), where the filmmaker worked as an assistant director and the star played the lead role. Sanjay Dutt later starred in Sanjay Gupta's directorial debut, Aatish: Feel the Fire (1994).

In further updates, However, their friendship as per reports hit a rough patch in 2007 during the making of Shootout at Lokhandwala, following disagreements. In an old interaction with The Times of India in 2013, Sanjay Gupta admitted that the two had not spoken for three years. They eventually ended their dispute at Amitabh Bachchan's 70th birthday party in 2012.

On top of that, Suniel, who worked with Sanjay in projects like Kaante and Mumbai Saga, remembered the filmmakers and wrote, "Still trying to come to terms with this news. We've spent so many days together, made films, shared laughs, arguments, ideas and memories that will stay with me forever. Never imagined I'd be writing something like this for you. Rest easy Sanj. You'll be missed more than words can say.

Sanjay Gupta was found dead at his home in Versova on Saturday morning. He was 59. According to the police, he appears to have fallen inside his house late on Friday night, suffering a severe head injury. His wife and two children found him lying in a pool of blood when they woke up in the morning. They rushed him to a hospital, where he was declared dead.

title: Ramayana advance booking crosses ₹40 crore five days before release; deadlock with Indian exhibitors ends for Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

The floodgates have opened for Ramayana advance booking with less than a week to go for its big rollout. The Nitesh Tiwari movie had its world premiere in Los Angeles earlier this week, which led to a huge jump in pre-sales in the US. But back home, the movie had been crippled by a deadlock between the distributors and exhibitors, due to which many shows hadn’t opened up. On Saturday, the deadlock was finally broken, raising hopes for an increased pace of advance bookings in its final week.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor stars as Lord Rama in Ramayana. How Ramayana pre-sales are faring Advance bookings for Ramayana opened on Dussehra, 15 full days before its global rollout. But for the next 10 days, only the Hindi version had extensive shows. And there, too, most of the single-screen and smaller centres had yet to open. The reason was a stalemate between the distributors and exhibitors. Dharma Productions, the movie’s distributor in India, had asked for a higher share of theatrical revenue, citing the movie's higher production costs. The distributors had shared two options: a 55% share over the first 11 days, or a three-week slab structure, with 60% going to the distributor in week 1, 50% in week 2, and 40% in week 3. The exhibitors were unwilling to give up higher revenue as they shared they were responsible for their costs. Additionally, they were wary of setting a precedent, as a settlement could prompt other big films to seek higher revenue.

Meanwhile, This led to a stalemate, with negotiations continuing for over a week. Sacnilk reported that on Friday, the deadlock was resolved, even though neither party shared the exact terms agreed upon. By Saturday, the number of screens for the movie had increased to almost 2500. By October 31 afternoon, five days before its rollout, the movie had grossed ₹ 16.5 crore rupees in advance bookings in India, selling over 3 lakh tickets. The Kannada version, which had been limited to a handful of shows, now accounted for 13% of the total gross across 150 screens. The Telugu and Tamil shows are also opening up steadily now and should be fully open by Monday.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ramayana: Rise of a Legend (@ramayanamovie)

As per the latest buzz, What has helped Ramayana’s case is the pre-sales buzz overseas. In North America, the movie will have paid previews on November 4, the eve of its rollout. The 24 hours after its world premiere saw the movie register a 27% jump in collections. By Friday, the movie had collected $2.5 million in overseas advance bookings, including over $1 million for the US paid previews alone. This takes the movie’s worldwide advance-booking gross to ₹ 40 crore rupees five days before its rollout.

In further updates, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The first part is scheduled for worldwide rollout on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2027. The films will rollout in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam across India.

On top of that, Sony Pictures will handle global distribution, excluding India, while Dharma Productions will distribute the movie in the Hindi-speaking market. The movie is also planned for a worldwide IMAX rollout.

title: ‘A blanket order would go too far’: Madras high court refuses to restrict protests against court rulings
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Madras high court has refused to restrict public protests against court rulings and emphasised that citizens have an undeniable right to disagree with a judgment, underscoring citizens' right to “question and peacefully protest” against judicial decisions.

Adding to this, However, the court directed the state and police authorities in Tamil Nadu to “deny” permission to any gathering aimed at “personally targeting a sitting judge.” (HT File) However, the court directed the state and police authorities in Tamil Nadu to “deny” permission to any gathering aimed at “personally targeting a sitting judge.”

Meanwhile, In an order passed on Friday, October 30, a bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan shared authorities must assess applications seeking permission for meetings, marches or protests relating to judicial matters on a “case-by-case basis,” using their powers under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and local police laws.

Notably, “However, the state remains under a strict obligation to ensure that its public spaces and digital networks are not used to threaten the safety and integrity of our judicial institutions,” it added.

As per the latest buzz, The court also directed the Cyber Crime Division of the Tamil Nadu police to actively monitor digital platforms to ensure that online content does not cross the line into criminal intimidation directed at sitting judges.

In further updates, It directed the police to complete their investigations into two criminal cases registered in connection with protests against a Madurai Bench judgment in a fair, thorough and expeditious manner.

On top of that, The court was hearing a public interest litigation filed by one R Karthikeyan, who sought action against organised campaigns, public meetings, processions, demonstrations and social media publications allegedly targeting judges and undermining the authority of the judiciary.

The petitioner told the court that, in a judgment passed in June last year, another bench of the Madurai bench of the Madras high court had struck down a government order concerning the grant of backwards-class benefits. At the time, the court had held that a person could not claim such benefits purely on the basis of religious conversion. The judgment had also noted that such a practice was “inconsistent with constitutional principles and Islamic theology.”

title: Sanjay Gupta remade Reservoir Dogs as Kaante; Quentin Tarantino said he loved the ‘rip-off’, called it fabulous
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Right from the start of his career, filmmaker Sanjay Gupta made a name for himself by remaking, or sometimes blatantly ripping off, Hollywood films. But his remakes often captured a new aesthetic, untapped in Indian cinema, helping them stand on their own. His most famous work is undoubtedly Kaante , the 2002 rollout that ushered in an era of stylised gangster flicks set in the US. Kaante was a remake of Quentin Tarantino’s seminal hit Reservoir Dogs, and the director went on record to say he ‘loved the rip-off’.

Adding to this, Amitabh Bachchan and Sanjay Dutt in a still from Kaante. Tarantino on Kaante Both Kaante and Reservoir Dogs were stories of six criminals coming together for a bank heist, only to be betrayed by one of their own. Reservoir Dogs, rolled out in 1992, put Tarantino on the map as a director to watch out for. Kaante, rolled out 10 years later, did the same for Sanjay Gupta. In 2007, Tarantino spoke at the Indian Movie Festival of Los Angeles, where Indian filmmaker Srinivas asked him about his opinion of Kaante. Tarantino responded, “I think it was fabulous. Of the many rip-offs, I loved Hong Kong's Too Many Ways to Be No 1 and this one, Kaante. The best part is, you have Indian guys coming to the US and looting a US bank. How cool is that! I was truly honoured. And these guys are played by legends of Bollywood.”

Meanwhile, Kaante starred Amitabh Bachchan, Sanjay Dutt, Suniel Shetty, Lucky Ali, Mahesh Manjrekar, and Kumar Gaurav in the lead roles. The movie was a moderate box-office success, earning ₹ 43 crore rupees worldwide. It was also noted for its differences with Reservoir Dogs, as it dealt with the characters’ backstories, something the Hollywood original did not. Tarantino himself noted, “Here I am, watching a movie that I've directed, and then it goes into each character's background. And I'm like, 'Whoa! For I always write backgrounds and stuff, and it always gets chopped off during the edit. And so I was amazed seeing this. I felt this isn't Reservoir Dogs, and then it goes into the warehouse scene, and I am like, 'Wow, it's back to Reservoir Dogs'. Isn't it amazing!” The filmmaker reserved some special praise for Big B, saying he particularly liked the “big beard guy, the famous guy in Bollywood’.

Notably, Sanjay Gupta died at the age of 59 on Friday. The news of his death was verified by filmmaker and FWICE chief advisor Ashoke Pandit on social media. The filmmaker died sometime between Friday night and Saturday morning at his home in Mumbai. In his social media post, Ashoke Pandit shared the cause of death was a head injury. However, there is no official confirmation yet.

title: Ramayana international reviews hail dazzling visuals, but say exhausting narrative makes Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film an 'overproduced B movie'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Days after its grand world premiere in Los Angeles, the first international reviews for Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana are out. The review embargo for the epic lifted on Friday night, and a handful of international publications shared their assessment of the Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer. So far, the select reviews have been critical of the movie’s length and stuffed narrative, but lauded the visual effects and scale.

Adding to this, Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama. Ramayana international reviews praise visuals and scale As of Saturday morning (October 31), five major international reviews of Ramayana have been published, with two of them praising the movie wholeheartedly. However, overall, there has been praise for the movie’s visuals. Avi Offer of NYC Movie Guru called the movie ‘a visually dazzling action adventure with great set and costume design’. Similarly, Screen Rant’s Brandon Zachary rated the movie 7/10 and wrote: “On a purely visual and technical level, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is an impressive cinematic achievement.” IndieWire gave the movie a ‘B’ and called it an ‘epic’. Reviewer Christian Zilko wrote, “( Nitesh) Tiwari appears primarily focused on dramatising the classic epic with the highest level of production value that’s currently available. He undeniably achieves that goal, even if it means that the final product lacks some voice that would have made it more memorable on its own terms.”
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ramayana: Rise of a Legend (@ramayanamovie)

Notably, The English version of the Ramayana is almost half an hour shorter than the Indian version. Yet the 2-and-a-half-hour runtime has not pleased early reviewers. NYC Movie Guru called the movie “bloated, clunky, exhausting, emotionally hollow and poorly acted.” Avi Offer added, “In a double feature with Sita Sings the Blues, it would be the inferior, overproduced B-movie.” Next Best Picture’s Giovanni Lago gave the movie a middling 5/10, saying the movie may have been better as a TV adaptation in the mould of Game of Thrones. “Overall, audiences can still be swept up by Ramayana, even if it feels so stuffed at times that it might’ve needed a "Game of Thrones"-level television adaptation to flesh out its narrative fully,” he wrote.

As per the latest buzz, Perhaps the harshest review of the lot was by Siddharth Adlakha of IGN, who rated the movie just 4 out of 10, writing, “A majestic epic falls victim to clunky action, eye-sore CGI, and awkward AI lip-syncing in what is, unfortunately, just a Part 1.”

title: Sacred Games, Farzi motion designers call out criticism of Ramayana’s VFX, say Indians should support it ‘regardless of its flaws’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Writer-director and VFX supervisors Yashoda Parthasarthy and Vijesh Rajan, who have worked on projects such as Sacred Games , Farzi and Gangs of Wasseypur , of late opened up about the criticism surrounding the VFX of Ranbir Kapoor -starrer Ramayana.

Adding to this, Ramayana will rollout worldwide on November 5. In an exclusive conversation with Hindustan Times, the VFX supervisors called out the online criticism. They pointed out the effort that goes into making visual effects look photorealistic and echoed the movie's star and co-producer Yash's words, emphasising that films like Ramayana must be supported as they could open doors for other Indian filmmakers to reach a global audience.

Meanwhile, Speaking about supporting Ramayana, Vijesh Rajan shared, "When I was doing my MA in Movie in Australia, my thesis idea was whether an epic like Ramayana or Mahabharata could be made on the scale of The Lord of the Rings or Chronicles of Narnia. I've always dreamt of a movie like this being made. As an Indian audience, we should support such endeavors. Other than Toxic, I don't think a movie has gotten this wide rollout. It's mounted on a massive budget and is being rolled out globally on an unprecedented scale with collaborations from Hans Zimmer, AR Rahman, and top technicians. "

Notably, Vijesh emphasised that while criticism is necessary, trolling and nasty comments can leave a bad taste for filmmakers. He shared, "It is a project we should back regardless of flaws; we should discuss the flaws, but there is a way in which people speak, and that can be off-putting to a lot of filmmakers. There is a lot of trolling, and there is some sort of campaign against the movie, and I feel like, why? We should support any endeavour that is mounted on this scale. It will only open doors for other Indian filmmakers to reach the international audience, and that is a huge step."

As per the latest buzz, Yashoda, who has worked on projects such as Raman Raghav 2.0 and Ghoul, also spoke about the effort involved in creating visual effects that look realistic. She shared, "Having worked in visual effects and motion design, I remember when I was studying and 3D animation was such a difficult process in itself, and in the past decade, it has evolved a lot. But having shared that, there is a lot of work that goes into making anything photoreal and people compare our films to Marvel or Avengers movies, which have 10x the budget that we have."

In further updates, She added, “There's a lack of research, empathy, and understanding of how visual effects work. We don't support art and design, and when statements are thrown, it is a little heartbreaking because those 10,000 people have worked on it. So, definitely need to support films like Ramayana. Also, not everybody can animate, if they did, then everybody would be an expert. Let's be a little more empathetic.”

On top of that, Yashoda and Vijesh's latest short movie Aakhri Ride stars Chandan Roy and Aamir Dalvi, and features Faisal Malik in an interesting role. It is presented by Anurag Kashyap and Vasan Bala. It is produced by Ranjan Singh, Vishesh Agrawal, Rajan EPK and Anurag. It will rollout on the YouTube channel Oh Short Flips, which is curated by Anurag, on Halloween, October 31,

title: Shah Rukh Khan's King sells overseas rights for ₹175 crore, highest in Indian cinema history; film needs to out-earn Pathaan, Jawan to break even
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Even as South behemoths have conquered the Indian market with their pan-India offerings, Shah Rukh Khan remains the ‘king’ overseas. That much is evident from reports on his new movie, King , and its overseas rights deal. A new report claims that the movie’s overseas theatrical rights have been acquired for ₹ 175 crore rupees, setting a new record for Indian cinema.

Adding to this, Shah Rukh Khan's King will rollout on Christmas this year. King’s reported record overseas rights deal Pinkvilla reported that Phars Films has acquired the rights to sell the movie overseas for ₹ 175 crore rupees (over $18 million). Till now, the overseas rights of Shah Rukh’s films have been with Yash Raj Films. The company famously distributed both Pathaan (made under its own banner) and Jawan starring Shah Rukh in 2023, to great success. However, Phars also has experience in overseas distribution. It partnered with YRF on many of its films and handled Prabhas’ Saaho on its own. The Pinkvilla report states that Phars has paid a minimum guarantee (MG) amount of ₹ 175 crore rupees for King’s distribution rights. No Indian movie has reached the ₹ 100 crore rupees mark so far, which makes this achievement staggering.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Shah Rukh Khan (@iamsrk)

Notably, The MG amount paid for a movie reflects the distributor’s faith in its theatrical performance. Overseas, distributors usually receive only 50% of the ticket-window gross, which means that King would have to earn $37-40 million just to break even. That corresponds to around ₹ 350-375 crore rupees gross internationally. Incidentally, Shah Rukh’s two most successful films - Pathaan and Jawan - both collected around ₹ 400 crore rupees overseas. King would have to earn at least as much, if not more, to be profitable. Given this high MG, King’s overseas collections would have to be at least as high as those of Dhurandhar 2 ( ₹ 460 crore rupees) or RRR ( ₹ 430 crore rupees) to be a success there. And these are some of the biggest overseas successes in Indian cinema history.
As per the latest buzz, King stars Shah Rukh Khan in the lead role and is directed by Siddharth Anand. The movie marks Shah Rukh's second collaboration with Siddharth after the 2023 rollout, Pathaan.

In further updates, The movie also features Suhana Khan, Deepika Padukone, Abhishek Bachchan, Rani Mukerji, Jaideep Ahalawat, Raghav Juyal, Saurabh Shukla, among others. The project marks Shah Rukh's first movie with his daughter Suhana, who made her acting debut with The Archies in 2023. The movie is scheduled to arrive in theatres on December 24.

title: Udta Teer box office collection day 8: Ayushmann Khurrana and Sara Ali Khan film refuses to slow down, crosses ₹33 crore so far
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Ayushmann Khurrana and Sara Ali Khan ’s Udta Teer has had a surprising ticket-window haul in the first few days of rollout. It opened to positive reviews and stood its ground despite the mammoth ticket-window pull of Rajinikanth's Jailer 2. But, that momentum has slowed down considerably as the movie entered its second week.

Adding to this, Ayushmann Khurrana plays a Pakistani spy in Udta Teer. Udta Teer ticket-window report Udta Teer surpassed expectations and collected ₹ 4.10 crore rupees on its opening day in theatres. It opened to decent reviews, which helped its cause and the movie gradually showed growth on Saturday to collect ₹ 7.25 crore rupees. Sunday showed more growth, at ₹ 8.20 crore rupees. It is the highest single-day haul of the movie so far. The dip started on Monday, as expected, but the movie stayed steady.

Meanwhile, As per the latest update on Sacnilk, Udta Teer has managed to collect ₹ 2.36 crore rupees on Wednesday. It is slightly above last day's haul which was at ₹ 2.25 crore rupees. This brings the total India collection to ₹ 33.26 crore rupees . The movie has to remain steady in the soon-to-release days, before the big rollout this Diwali in the form of Ranbir Kapoor's Ramayana.

Notably, Taran Adarsh also pointed at the ticket-window performance of Udta Teer and wrote on X, “Udta Teer remains on par with Monday on Tuesday, with the discounted ticket offer boosting footfalls... The #BOGO ticket offer today [Wednesday] should help the numbers remain stable. The *Week 1* total is expected to be around ₹ 31 cr [+/-] – a fair result... The movie has one more week to make the most of its theatrical run, starting this Friday, before #Ramayana arrives next Thursday [5 Nov].”

As per the latest buzz, The movie follows a Pakistani spy, played by Ayushmann Khurrana, who loses his memory after a blast and begins to believe that he is an Indian Counter-Terrorism Squad officer. title: Exclusive| I will soon initiate the necessary criminal proceedings: Vidnyan Mane on Palash Mucchal case
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star-producer Vidnyan Mane , a childhood friend of India women’s cricket team captain Smriti Mandhana, says the Bombay High Court has dismissed a defamation case filed against him by music composer Palash Muchhal, Mandhana’s former fiancé. “This verdict conveys an important message: people should not file baseless and false cases in court merely to generate publicity,” Mane tells us, adding that he “now plans to initiate criminal proceedings against Muchhal”.

Adding to this, Palash Mucchal and Vidnyan Mane The legal dispute surfaced in January this year, weeks after Muchhal and Mandhana called off their wedding in December 2025. Mane had accused the composer of cheating him out of ₹ 40 lakh invested in his movie Nazaria. As per his complaint, the two met in Sangli in December 2023, and Mane transferred the money by March 2025. He alleged that the movie was never completed and his money was not returned. Mane also made personal allegations against Muchhal, who denied them and sent him a ₹ 10 crore rupees defamation notice.

Meanwhile, Claiming that the case was dismissed over procedural deficiencies, Mane says, “No one is above the law, and compliance with judicial procedures is mandatory for everyone.” Muchhal’s legal team did not respond for comments.

Notably, Mane adds, "I intend to bring before the public the various fabricated and imaginary stories that he has narrated so far, and expose how people are being misled. I also want the truth to become known to his family members, so that they too can understand the reality of his conduct and the alleged falsehoods, and see the truth behind his actions. Very soon, I will initiate the necessary and appropriate judicial as well as criminal proceedings in this matter, strictly through lawful channels."

title: Shraddha Kapoor proud to be part of Eetha, says what matters is a good film and she does not look at how many box office records are broken
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

As per the latest update on news agency PTI, the star shared on the trailer launch event that she is always in search of good stories and that's why she sometimes does one movie in two years.

Adding to this, Shraddha Kapoor at the trailer launch of her movie Eetha in Mumbai on October 30, 2026. (Photo by Sujit JAISWAL / AFP) (AFP) What Shraddha shared With the movie, Shraddha Kapoor reunites with producer Dinesh Vijan after the mega success of horror-comedy films Stree and Stree 2. Meanwhile, "I don't think (in terms of) women or men-oriented films. Our industry needs good stories and such stories should be made. I think it is a narrow thought (to divide films on the basis of gender). .. The success of a movie is incidental and not in anyone's hand. I'm just happy and proud to be part of Eetha," she added.

Notably, Eetha is a biographical drama directed by Laxman Utekar. The musical drama is rooted in Maharashtra's traditional tamasha and lavani dance forms and inspired by the life of Vithabai Narayangaonkar. People from several parts of the state flocked to watch her performances, which were a colourful amalgamation of music, dance and storytelling. For her artistry, she was bestowed with the prestigious President's award in the Tamasha genre. She also began to be known as "Tamasha Samradini" (Tamasha Empress) by her followers, and the government later instituted the annual Vithabai Narayangavkar Lifetime Achievement Award in her memory in 2006. Her figure became a symbol of dedication and bravery in Maharashtra. She died on January 15, 2002, at the age of 66 in Narayangaon, Maharashtra, following a paralytic attack.

Meanwhile, "I'm not shocked, nor I'm surprised with Naseeruddin Shah's abusive language because, since last few months, in a year in fact, he's been constantly misbehaving, has become a compulsive abuser. The kind of language which he uses, the way he distorts his face, he exposes his frustration. There are reasons behind it, I can understand, and I pity him," shared Ashoke Pandit.
Notably, He further alleged that Shah's public appearances showed signs of frustration and claimed that the star's comments were affecting his public image.

As per the latest buzz, Pandit also attributed what he described as Shah's frustration to ideological differences over films that have performed well commercially. He specifically mentioned The Kashmir Files , The Kerala Story and Dhurandhar while making the claim.

In further updates, "Probably one of the reasons why he's feeling insecure is that the films which are doing well in the in the in the country is not suiting him. Films like Kashmir Files, Kerala Story, Dhurandhar. These narratives are not suiting them. They're suffering from an inferiority complex. Hence, this is kind of behaviour with which he's trying to come out. So I think, in the end, I would like to tell him that he should consult a psychiatrist because it's affecting his mental health. A normal person will not behave like this," shared Ashoke Pandit.

On top of that, Pandit's comments were made as reactions continued to emerge around Shah's video supporting the Jamia students. Shah has also of late spoken in support of students protesting at the Satyajit Ray Movie and Television Institute, making his latest statement part of a series of comments on student-related issues.

title: Shraddha Kapoor unveils EETHA trailer as she steps into the role of Lavani legend Eetha Bai; film to release on December 4
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Directed by Laxman Utekar, the musical drama explores the journey of an artist who overcame social conventions and personal challenges to leave behind a lasting legacy.

Adding to this, The trailer offers a glimpse into the world of Lavani, placing its music, performances and cultural traditions at the centre of the narrative. Through its visuals and musical sequences, the movie appears to explore not just the art form but also the experiences of the women who helped shape it. EETHA aims to bring the story of an artist and her journey to a wider audience through a big-screen musical drama.

Meanwhile, Speaking about the project, producer Dinesh Vijan shared, “One of the most exciting things about cinema is that every once in a while, you come across a story so extraordinary that you wonder why the world doesn’t already know about it. For me, EETHA was one of those stories.

Notably, When I first heard it, I was fascinated not just by the incredible world of Lavani — its music, its rhythm, its energy and its larger-than-life characters — but by the extraordinary women who brought this art form to life. We have celebrated their performances for generations, but how often have we stopped to understand their journeys? The courage, the sacrifices, the struggles and the sheer strength of these women are as extraordinary as the art itself. What amazed me was that a world so rich in culture, emotion and powerful human stories had remained largely unexplored in Hindi cinema. It felt like an incredible opportunity to bring this world and the people who shaped it to the big screen.

As per the latest buzz, We’ve given so much love to their art. Perhaps it’s time we gave just as much love to their stories. That’s what EETHA means to me. It’s more than a movie inspired by true events; it’s a celebration of an extraordinary art form and the remarkable women whose lives deserve to be seen, heard and remembered.”

In further updates, Shraddha Kapoor, who essays Eetha Bai, spoke about her experience of playing the central character and shared, “It’s a story about a woman whose art, courage and individuality make her unforgettable. The more Laxman sir told me about the character, the more I felt connected to her world. Playing this role has been an incredibly exciting experience, and I am thrilled for audiences to discover her journey on the big screen. This is also my grand reunion with Maddock Films after we made magic with Stree and Stree 2, which is thrilling to say the least. The entire team has put in so much hard work, and I cannot wait for audiences to experience the world of Eetha.”

On top of that, For director Laxman Utekar, the movie marks a departure in setting and subject from his previous rollout Chhaava . He shared, “After the smash hit success of Chhaava , which became a mega cinematic spectacle, I wanted to take audiences into a completely different world with EETHA . While the two films are vastly different in their settings, both are rooted in the extraordinary strength of their central characters. EETHA is the story of an artist who became a legacy. We have brought together authenticity, emotion and scale to create a cinematic experience that audiences can truly immerse themselves in.”

Producer Karishma Sharma of Kathputli Creations added, “India is home to extraordinary stories, rich cultural traditions and fascinating characters that deserve to be celebrated on the big screen. For us, the most exciting stories are those that are deeply rooted in our soil yet have the power to entertain and connect with audiences everywhere. EETHA brings together this very spirit. It is a remarkable story from our cultural heritage, told through music, drama, emotion and spectacle. We hope audiences discover a world that feels uniquely Indian, yet resonates universally.”

title: Sharvari wears mother’s heirloom pink Patola saree for Yeh Prem Mol Liya promotions; says it feels like being ‘wrapped in her love and blessings’
body: Here's the latest fashion moment turning heads:
The star revisits a treasured family heirloom gifted by her mother after watching ‘Jhumka Patola’, giving the traditional saree a fresh interpretation.

Adding to this, The saree holds a special place in Sharvari’s family, having been worn by her mother over the years and associated with several cherished memories. According to the star, her mother gifted it to her after watching her song ‘Jhumka Patola’ for the first time. The gesture made the outfit particularly meaningful, turning it into more than just another look for a promotional appearance.

Meanwhile, Sharvari chose to give the traditional garment a fresh interpretation while retaining its sentimental value. The process also involved looking through old photographs of her mother wearing the saree, allowing the star to revisit the memories attached to it before presenting the reimagined look.

Notably, Sharing the story behind the outfit on Instagram, Sharvari wrote, “When my Aai watched #JhumkaPatola for the first time, I will never forget the love and pride in her eyes. She gave me her beautiful pink Patola saree as a blessing! An heirloom she has adorned over the years and made so many beautiful memories in. Reinventing something so precious to her and wearing it for promotions has been such a special feeling. Going through old pictures of her wearing it and then seeing her reaction to what we created was just priceless. Wearing her saree feels like being wrapped in her love and blessings!”

As per the latest buzz, The look reflects a personal approach to fashion, with Sharvari choosing to incorporate a family heirloom into her public appearances rather than opting for an entirely new ensemble. By reworking a garment connected to her mother’s memories, the star has also highlighted how traditional clothing can carry emotional significance across generations.

Adding to this, AISA National President Neha Bora address the media during a press conference on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) issue at the Press Club of India, in New Delhi, India, on Thursday, October 29, 2026. title: Mohit Malik on playing Birju Lohar in Mirzapur The Movie: “We cannot approach a character by simply deciding whether he is good or bad”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
As the crime drama arrives on Prime Video, the star discusses the challenge of portraying a flawed character whose choices do not always fit into clear moral categories.

Adding to this, The franchise has built its narrative around characters who frequently blur the lines between right and wrong. Birju Lohar fits into this morally complex world, with his flaws, questionable decisions and unpredictable nature shaping his character. For Mohit, the challenge was to understand Birju’s motivations without judging him through the lens of his own personal beliefs.

Meanwhile, Rather than categorising Birju as either good or bad, the star approached the role by examining the circumstances and emotions that influence his decisions. According to Mohit, portraying such characters requires an star to understand the reasoning behind their actions, even when those choices may be difficult to justify.

Notably, Speaking about playing Birju Lohar, Mohit Malik shared, “Birju is a flawed character who makes choices that may not always be right, and that is what makes him interesting to play. As actors, we cannot approach a character by simply deciding whether he is good or bad. We have to understand his mindset, his circumstances and what drives him to make certain decisions. Even when you don't agree with a character's actions, you have to find the reasoning behind them and make them believable. The challenge is to portray the character honestly without judging him. I believe audiences connect with characters who feel human, with their flaws, contradictions and complexities. With Birju, I wanted to understand the person behind his actions and bring that truth to the screen.”

As per the latest buzz, Mohit’s comments highlight an important aspect of his approach to the role: understanding a character beyond the choices he makes. By exploring Birju’s mindset and the circumstances surrounding his decisions, the star sought to present a layered portrayal while leaving audiences to form their own opinions.

In further updates, The digital rollout of Mirzapur: The Movie gives viewers another opportunity to explore the franchise’s familiar world of power struggles, rivalries and morally ambiguous characters. Mohit’s portrayal of Birju Lohar adds to that landscape, reflecting the complexity that has remained central to the crime drama’s storytelling.
On top of that, Mirzapur: The Movie is now streaming exclusively on Prime Video India.

title: Sara Ali Khan faces fatwa over Kedarnath Temple visit: Reports
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Reacting to the visit, the cleric shared that Islamic Sharia does not permit Muslims to participate in religious practices associated with another faith. “I want to make it clear that Islamic Sharia does not permit its followers to engage in shirk,” the cleric shared, as reported by Bhaskar English. He further added, “This means that no Muslim, whether a man or a woman, is allowed to adopt the religious practices of another faith or worship at a temple.”

Adding to this, The cleric as per reports described such acts as “impermissible and haram” under Sharia and shared Sara should repent before Allah. He also reiterated his position on the star's temple visit, saying, “I want to make it clear that such acts are not permissible.”

Meanwhile, As per the latest buzz, Sara travelled to Kedarnath by helicopter before joining devotees waiting for darshan. Pictures and videos from the visit showed her standing in the queue and later offering prayers at the temple.

Notably, Reports also shared that the star participated in the temple's puja and aarti and visited the Bhukunt Bhairav Temple. Her visit as per reports took place amid cold weather, with some reports stating that women devotees offered her a shawl to help her keep warm.

As per the latest buzz, Sara has maintained a connection with Kedarnath for several years. The shrine also has a link to her movie career, as she made her Bollywood debut with the 2018 movie Kedarnath , which starred the late Sushant Singh Rajput. She has returned to the temple on multiple occasions since then.

In further updates, The row has also brought attention to the Badrinath-Kedarnath Temple Committee's rules for non-Hindu visitors. As per the latest buzz, the committee requires non-Hindu devotees who wish to offer prayers at the shrine to submit an affidavit.
On top of that, BKTC CEO Sohan Singh Rangar as per reports verified to News18 that Sara's team had submitted the required affidavit before her visit.

A fatwa is generally understood as a religious opinion or ruling issued by an Islamic scholar on a question concerning Islamic law. In this case, the reported ruling reflects the position expressed by the cleric and should not be presented as a universal view shared by all Muslims or Islamic scholars.

title: SCOOP: Anirudh exits Shah Rukh Khan’s King due to packed schedule; gifts SRK the theme track as Sachin-Jigar take over
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

And now, Bollywood Hungama has exclusively learnt of a major development that could leave Shah Rukh Khan and Anirudh followers with mixed emotions. Anirudh, who has collected a massive following for his electrifying background scores, has amicably parted ways with King owing to his packed schedule. A source informed Bollywood Hungama, “Siddharth Anand and Shah Rukh Khan are determined to bring King to cinemas this Christmas without any delays. However, Anirudh has been juggling multiple commitments down South, making it difficult for him to devote the time and attention that a movie of this scale demands. After a cordial discussion, both parties mutually decided to part ways.” The source further opened up that the makers have now entrusted Sachin-Jigar with the responsibility of composing the movie’s music and background score.

Adding to this, "However, Anirudh has given the Theme Track of King to Shah Rukh Khan as a mark of his respect for the megastar, and Sachin-Jigar too will be reimagining the track for the entire background score of the movie. So King will still have the Anirudh touch with the theme track, but the entire score also the album, otherwise will be done by Sachin-Jigar," the source tells us.

Meanwhile, King is touted to be the most ambitious action movie of Hindi cinema, mounted on a mammoth budget as the makers are up to deliver a never-before spectacle. The estimated costs excluding SRK's fees and PnA is touted to be in the zone of Rs. 450 crore rupees, and every penny will be visible on the screen as per insiders.
Notably, "This is Siddharth Anand's biggest movie till date and a love letter to the legend of SRK. He has designed the full movie keeping his aura in mind."

title: Exclusive|Zoya Akhtar on Mumbai's floating advertising barges: We need respite not sponsored sunsets
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Zoya Akhtar, born and brought up in Mumbai, has always been vocal about developments in the city and concerns citizens face. Of late, the Maharashtra Maritime Board (MMB) invited tenders to introduce floating advertising barges and illuminated hoardings along Mumbai’s coastline, and Zoya opens up on her thoughts on it.

Adding to this, Zoya Akhtar “This city is bursting at the seams, with its population, construction, traffic, pollution, noise, garbage, lack of open spaces, felling of trees etc. It’s already an assault on the senses. We are in desperate need to connect with nature, and not disconnect further. And we need respite, not sponsored sunsets! Why would people want to look at ugly hoardings when sitting by the water,” she shares.

Meanwhile, Zoya adds that citizens should have a say before such installations are approved. “People pay through their noses for homes with a view and even if they don’t live by the sea, they spend a considerable amount to live in Mumbai. Their opinion has to matter.”

Notably, Concerns have also been raised about the impact of such advertising on Mumbai’s coastal environment and marine life. Separately, the growing presence of commercial signage raises another question: where should one draw the line between creative advertising and visual pollution? “Please mark certain areas for commercial advertising and limit it to that. A city must not have signage everywhere. It’s mentally taxing, we don’t realise but to be bombarded with constant messaging is very stressful for the mind,” Zoya ends.

title: Nakhrewaalii review: Aanand L Rai's rom-com is a familiar yet fun ride with enough laughs
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Are Aanand L Rai 's production Nakhrewaalii and Ayushmann Khurrana's Dream Girl 2 long-lost cousins? Well, both revolve around gender swapping, cross dressing, mistaken identities and romantic confusion. Are there then enough differences that allow Nakhrewaalii to carve out an identity of its own? Read on to find out.

Adding to this, Nakrewaalii stars Ansh Duggal and Pragati Srivastava. The premise The story revolves around Sumit Mishra (Ansh Duggal), a typical good for nothing guy who believes women have it easy, whether it is reservations or getting their way in almost every sphere of life. After his girlfriend back home gets married to someone else, he moves to Delhi to pursue higher studies. Here, he meets Paridhi (Pragati Srivastava), the daughter of his landlord. Sparks fly, there's intimacy, but his mindset immediately classifies Paridhi as a girl only good for 'fun' in his own words, while another girl who likes him at his college, and is a 'virgin', is fit for marriage. His life turns upside down as he realises his feelings for Paridhi, and has to bag a government job for her parents to agree to the union. How Sumit manages that forms the rest of the plot.

Meanwhile, The story is as old as time. But director Rahul Shanklya, along with writers Divy Nidhi Sharma, manage to keep things entertaining by peppering the first half with plenty of funny one-liners and amusing sequences.
Notably, The second half too manages to keep the laughter quotient intact, and that works in the movie's favour.

As per the latest buzz, However there are certain inconsistencies that are hard to overlook. For instance, our male protagonist transforms into a woman for a major part of the runtime, but the continuity in his appearance is messed up. One morning, he is seen sporting a clean shaven face, only for a rather noticeable two to three day old stubble to appear by the same evening. Heck, even in a wedding sequence where the scenes unfold back to back, the inconsistency is glaring. These may seem like minor details in the larger scheme of things, but they can be distracting, especially when the premise itself relies so heavily on it. One wonders why the makers didn't pay closer attention to something so basic.

In further updates, In the performance department, Ansh and Pragati both have a confident screen presence. Kumud Mishra plays a key role as a government official, and he's reliable, as usual. Gopal Datt as Paridhi's father is very funny with his one liners. Akash Makhija as Jhaadi's, Sumit's best friend makes you chuckle.
On top of that, The music by Vayu, Vaibhav Pani, Sharan Rawat, Gaurav Chatterji, Tanishk Bagchi is soothing and goes with the story.

Overall, Nakhrewaalii may share some DNA with Dream Girl 2, but it has enough of its own quirks and comic moments to stand independently. It isn't ambitious in its storytelling, and even tries to include a moral lesson. But with a likeable lead pair and funny moments, it largely serves its purpose.

title: Eetha trailer out: Shraddha Kapoor celebrates Maharashtra's Lavani legacy as she transforms into Vithabai Narayangaonkar in Laxman Utekar's musical
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Shraddha Kapoor is stepping into the world of Lavani with her next movie, Eetha , in which she takes on the role of a celebrated performer who made her mark against all odds. Maddock Films and Kathputli Creations have unveiled the trailer, offering a first glimpse of Shraddha in the role of Eetha Bai. Directed by Laxman Utekar, the musical drama draws inspiration from the life of Vithabai Bhau Mang Narayangaonkar, the renowned Maharashtrian Lavani and Tamasha artist. Interestingly, this movie will mark one of the late Nana Patekar's last performances.

Adding to this, Eetha trailer out: Shraddha Kapoor's journey as a Lavani performer promises drama, dance and an inspiring story of survival. Trailer of Eetha The trailer offers a glimpse into the colourful world of dance forms such as Lavani and Tamasha, but there is more to Eetha Bai's story than music, dance and applause. It follows a woman navigating betrayal, heartbreak and the many obstacles that come her way as she tries to make a name for herself. A line from the trailer sums up her determination: “If I die without trying, I'll be remembered as helpless. But if I die dancing, I'll be remembered as a legend.”

Meanwhile, The movie also shines a light on the cultural roots of Lavani and Tamasha, as well as the women who have kept these traditions alive. Through Eetha Bai's journey, it celebrates an art form that has been an important part of Maharashtra's cultural identity. The trailer also features a lively exchange about the nauvari saree, with one character explaining why it is far more than just an outfit. It stands for the pride, identity and traditions of Marathi women.

Notably, On playing the titular role, Shraddha spoke about the opportunity to explore a character whose individuality and relationship with her art make her story worth telling. She shared, “It’s a story about a woman whose art, courage and individuality make her unforgettable. The more Laxman sir told me about the character, the more I felt connected to her world. Playing this role has been an incredibly exciting experience, and I am thrilled for audiences to discover her journey on the big screen. This is also my grand reunion with Maddock Films after we made magic with Stree and Stree 2, which is thrilling to say the least. The entire team has put in so much hard work, and I cannot wait for audiences to experience the world of Eetha.”

As per the latest buzz, Producer Dinesh Vijan shared the story stood out to him because it highlighted women whose contributions to an important cultural art form have not received enough recognition in mainstream Hindi cinema. He shared, “One of the most exciting things about cinema is that every once in a while, you come across a story so extraordinary that you wonder why the world doesn’t already know about it. For me, Eetha was one of those stories. When I first heard it, I was fascinated not just by the incredible world of Lavani — its music, its rhythm, its energy and its larger-than-life characters — but by the extraordinary women who brought this art form to life. We have celebrated their performances for generations, but how often have we stopped to understand their journeys?"

In further updates, He added, “The courage, the sacrifices, the struggles and the sheer strength of these women are as extraordinary as the art itself. What amazed me was that a world so rich in culture, emotion and powerful human stories had remained largely unexplored in Hindi cinema. It felt like an incredible opportunity to bring this world and the people who shaped it to the big screen. We’ve given so much love to their art. Perhaps it’s time we gave just as much love to their stories. That’s what Eetha means to me. It’s more than a movie inspired by true events; it’s a celebration of an extraordinary art form and the remarkable women whose lives deserve to be seen, heard and remembered.”

On top of that, Following the smash hit success of Chhaava, Laxman Utekar now returns with Eetha. Speaking about directing this musical story, he shared, “After the smash hit success of Chhaava, which became a mega cinematic spectacle, I wanted to take audiences into a completely different world with EETHA. While the two films are vastly different in their settings, both are rooted in the extraordinary strength of their central characters. EETHA is the story of an artist who became a legacy. We have brought together authenticity, emotion and scale to create a cinematic experience that audiences can truly immerse themselves in.”

Karishma Sharma, producer at Kathputli Creations, also spoke about the importance of taking stories rooted in India's cultural heritage to the big screen. She shared, “India is home to extraordinary stories, rich cultural traditions and fascinating characters that deserve to be celebrated on the big screen. For us, the most exciting stories are those that are deeply rooted in our soil yet have the power to entertain and connect with audiences everywhere. EETHA brings together this very spirit. It is a remarkable story from our cultural heritage, told through music, drama, emotion and spectacle. We hope audiences discover a world that feels uniquely Indian, yet resonates universally.”
